title: Chemically defined ribosome biogenesis
open: Can a functional ribosome be built from a fully enumerated set of purified components, with every assembly, processing, and modification factor required identified and supplied? In other words, can ribosome biogenesis be reconstituted in a chemically defined system that supports a claim of molecular sufficiency?
status: Kosaka et al. (2025), [Autonomous ribosome biogenesis in vitro](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-55853-7), achieved coordinated ribosomal RNA and protein expression with functional assembly in cell extract, but undefined extract activities prevent a molecular sufficiency claim.
solved_when: Functional ribosomes are produced in vitro from a defined, enumerated purified-component system, with all necessary assembly, processing, and modification factors identified and no reliance on undefined extract activities.
why: It identifies the complete machinery needed for translation to reproduce itself, a core step toward self-sustaining synthetic cells.
key_works: Kosaka et al. (2025), [Autonomous ribosome biogenesis in vitro](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-55853-7).

title: Regeneration of an energy-producing artificial organelle
open: Can an artificial organelle keep producing ATP while it replaces, from within, every protein and membrane component of its energy-transducing module? Formally, the goal is a self-regenerating energy-producing compartment whose output is sustained through complete, repeated internal renewal of its parts.
status: In 2019, Berhanu, Ueda, and Kuruma demonstrated light-powered ATP production supporting protein synthesis and partial component production ([Artificial photosynthetic cell producing energy for protein synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-09147-4)); complete repeated renewal remains open.
solved_when: ATP production is maintained continuously while all protein and membrane components of the energy-transducing module are internally synthesized and replaced, and this complete renewal can be achieved repeatedly.
why: Without regeneration, the machinery powering cellular maintenance exhausts itself; solving it would give synthetic cells a persistent, self-sustaining energy supply.
key_works: Berhanu, Ueda, and Kuruma (2019), [Artificial photosynthetic cell producing energy for protein synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-09147-4).

title: Mechanisms of the minimal-cell division genes
open: How do the poorly characterized division genes of the genomically minimal cell JCVI-syn3A work together with known division proteins to drive cell division? In particular, what are their substrates and mechanical effects in the division machinery?
status: Seven genes that jointly restore regular division were identified in 2021 (Pelletier et al. 2021, [Genetic requirements for cell division in a genomically minimal cell](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2021.03.008)); several of them lacked established molecular functions.
solved_when: The molecular roles of these minimal-cell division genes are established — their substrates, interaction partners among known division proteins, and mechanical contributions — such that the cooperative mechanism restoring regular division is explained.
why: It explains how a genetically minimal cell divides reliably, and connects gene function to the biophysics of cellular force generation and membrane mechanics.
key_works: Pelletier et al. (2021), [Genetic requirements for cell division in a genomically minimal cell](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2021.03.008).

title: Higher-order synthetic lethality in reduced genomes
open: Which combinations of gene deletions, each individually dispensable, become lethal or severely damaging when introduced together — and can we predict these interactions, including those among three or more loci, in reduced genomes?
status: The 2021 MiniBacillus compendium provides 105 progressively reduced genomes, but this samples deletion trajectories rather than exhaustively mapping interactions. Key work: Michalik et al. (2021), [The Bacillus subtilis Minimal Genome Compendium](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.1c00339).
solved_when: A predictive map of lethal or severely damaging higher-order (three-or-more-locus) deletion combinations is available for progressively reduced genomes, going beyond sampled deletion trajectories to an interaction-level account.
why: Without such a map, genome simplification risks unexpected failure when individually safe deletions are combined; with it, streamlining can proceed predictably.
key_works: Michalik et al. (2021), [The Bacillus subtilis Minimal Genome Compendium](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.1c00339).

title: Complete Sc2.0 chromosome consolidation
open: Can all designed Sc2.0 chromosomes, together with the required tRNA complement, be combined into a single stable yeast strain that retains the intended designed sequences and maintains acceptable performance?
status: All 16 individual synthetic chromosomes have been built; a 6.5-chromosome consolidated strain was reported in Zhao et al. (2023), [Debugging and consolidating multiple synthetic chromosomes reveals combinatorial genetic interactions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2023.09.025), and consortium work in 2026 still identifies full consolidation as unfinished.
solved_when: A single strain carrying every designed Sc2.0 chromosome plus the required tRNA complement is stable, retains the intended sequences, and shows acceptable performance — superseding the existing 6.5-chromosome consolidated strain.
why: It would complete an integrated synthetic eukaryotic genome, delivering the Sc2.0 project's end goal.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2023), [Debugging and consolidating multiple synthetic chromosomes reveals combinatorial genetic interactions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2023.09.025).

title: Stable dosage of a relocated tRNA genome
open: Can a cell maintain balanced tRNA gene expression when its entire tRNA complement is relocated onto a single designed chromosome? Formally, this asks for relocation of the complete tRNA set onto a neochromosome such that dosage balance is preserved without selection for deletions or ploidy changes.
status: A roughly 190-kb neochromosome containing 275 tRNA genes was built in 2023, but substantial dosage-related selection was observed (Schindler et al. (2023), [Design, construction, and functional characterization of a tRNA neochromosome in yeast](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2023.10.015)).
solved_when: The complete tRNA complement is carried on a designed chromosome and balanced tRNA expression is preserved, with no selection for deletions or ploidy changes.
why: It would make large-scale genome reorganization compatible with balanced translation, so designed chromosomes do not destabilize the cell's protein synthesis machinery.
key_works: Schindler et al. (2023), [Design, construction, and functional characterization of a tRNA neochromosome in yeast](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2023.10.015).

title: Full orthogonality of a parallel translation channel
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: How completely can an engineered translation system be isolated from the cell's native translation machinery? Formally, quantify and minimize the exchange of ribosomal subunits, RNAs, and translation factors between the orthogonal and native channels while retaining useful throughput.
status: Stapled orthogonal ribosomes (Schmied et al., 2018, [Controlling orthogonal ribosome subunit interactions enables evolution of new function](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0773-z)) constrained subunit interactions in 2018, but this does not establish complete biochemical or resource isolation.
solved_when: An engineered translation channel is described in which exchange of subunits, RNAs, and factors with native translation is quantitatively measured and minimized, while the channel sustains throughput sufficient for independent operation and evolution.
why: Full orthogonality allows an engineered translation system to evolve and operate independently of native translation, rather than being coupled to — and constrained by — the host machinery.
key_works: Schmied et al. (2018), [Controlling orthogonal ribosome subunit interactions enables evolution of new function](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0773-z).

title: Predictable relocation of genomic circuits
open: Can a synthetic gene circuit be relocated to a different genomic locus and function as designed without retuning — or better, can we predict in advance what compensation a new locus requires before building it?
status: Highly insulated E. coli landing pads were demonstrated in 2020 in Park et al. (2020), [Precision design of stable genetic circuits carried in highly-insulated E. coli genomic landing pads](https://doi.org/10.15252/msb.20209584); arbitrary locus-to-locus portability remains unresolved.
solved_when: A designed circuit can be moved between arbitrary genomic loci while preserving its behavior, or a predictive method identifies the necessary compensatory changes for a target locus prior to construction.
why: It would enable stable genomic integration of circuits without repeated retuning, making designed biology portable rather than locus-specific.
key_works: Park et al. (2020), [Precision design of stable genetic circuits carried in highly-insulated E. coli genomic landing pads](https://doi.org/10.15252/msb.20209584).

title: Wall-clock-stable biological oscillators
open: Can a synthetic biological oscillator keep a prescribed elapsed-time period — true wall-clock stability — despite changes in growth rate, temperature, and cellular load, with phase diffusion quantified and controlled? Formally, the goal is an engineered gene circuit whose period, measured in absolute time, stays within specified tolerance under these perturbations while accumulating only bounded, quantified phase noise.
status: Highly regular, long-lived repressilator oscillations were demonstrated in 2016 by Potvin-Trottier et al. (2016), [Synchronous long-term oscillations in a synthetic gene circuit](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature19841); however, broad environmental compensation — stability of the period across growth, temperature, and load — remains open. Related work in physics addresses precision limits of autonomous clocks.
solved_when: A constructed oscillator maintains its prescribed elapsed-time period across growth, temperature, and load changes, with a quantified measurement of its phase diffusion reported against a stated tolerance.
why: It would enable dependable timing and scheduled cellular actions in engineered organisms — circuits that execute delayed or periodic behaviors on real-world clocks rather than on the cell's variable physiological tempo.
key_works: Potvin-Trottier et al. (2016), [Synchronous long-term oscillations in a synthetic gene circuit](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature19841).

title: Scalable rewritable memory in living cells
open: Can we build rewritable memory inside living cells that scales — many independently addressable bits that can be written, erased, and rewritten reliably over many cycles?
status: Rewritable memory was demonstrated in 2012 (Bonnet, Subsoontorn, and Endy, [Rewritable digital data storage in live cells via engineered control of recombination directionality](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1202344109)); larger permanent memories followed, but capacity, reversibility, and reliability remain difficult to combine.
solved_when: A cellular memory system exists with measured capacity (number of independently addressable elements), write error rates, retention times, and rewrite endurance, all quantified.
why: It enables persistent, updateable cellular state, letting engineered cells record and revise histories of their environment and internal events.
key_works: Bonnet, Subsoontorn, and Endy (2012), [Rewritable digital data storage in live cells via engineered control of recombination directionality](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1202344109).

title: Independently programmable RNA lifetime
open: Can an RNA transcript's lifetime be programmed as an independent design parameter, set without disturbing its translation, localization, or regulatory function across host states? Formally, achieve orthogonal, transcript-by-transcript control over decay rate that is portable across transcripts and hosts.
status: Degradation-tuning RNAs provided a 40-fold stability range in E. coli in 2021, per Zhang et al. (2021), [Predictable control of RNA lifetime using engineered degradation-tuning RNAs](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-021-00816-4); broad transcript and host portability remains open.
solved_when: A designer can specify a target lifetime for a transcript and achieve it without altering translation, localization, or regulatory function, across diverse transcripts and hosts — going beyond the demonstrated 40-fold stability range in E. coli.
why: It makes circuit timing an independently adjustable knob, so kinetic behavior of synthetic RNA circuits can be tuned without redesigning their functional parts.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2021), [Predictable control of RNA lifetime using engineered degradation-tuning RNAs](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-021-00816-4).

title: Portable RNA logic between translation systems
open: Can RNA-based computational circuits be transferred between prokaryotic and eukaryotic translation systems so that they still compute — with predictable shifts in thresholds, leakage, and timing?
status: Eukaryotic toeholds were demonstrated in 2021/2022, and successful distinct architectures exist, but a general portability framework remains open; key work includes Zhao et al. (2022), [RNA-responsive elements for eukaryotic translational control](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-021-01068-2).
solved_when: A demonstrated transfer of an RNA computation between a prokaryotic and a eukaryotic system in which thresholds, leakage, and timing change predictably, ideally within a general portability framework.
why: It makes RNA design libraries reusable across organisms rather than requiring full redesign for each host.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2022), [RNA-responsive elements for eukaryotic translational control](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-021-01068-2).

title: Large protein-logic libraries with collective orthogonality
open: Can we design large libraries of protein logic components that stay mutually orthogonal when all expressed together in the same cell? Formally, the goal is a set of coexpressed protein components whose intended pairwise specificities are preserved even in the presence of unintended assemblies and sequestration among library members.
status: Orthogonal protein heterodimers were achieved in 2019 (Chen et al., 2019, [Programmable design of orthogonal protein heterodimers](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0802-y)) and protein Boolean gates in 2020; collective scaling of many coexpressed components remains open.
solved_when: A collectively orthogonal library of protein logic components is designed and demonstrated to retain mutual specificity under coexpression, including against unintended assemblies and sequestration.
why: It unlocks larger and faster post-translational protein programs, moving protein computation beyond small demonstration circuits.
key_works: Chen et al. (2019), [Programmable design of orthogonal protein heterodimers](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0802-y).

title: Low-cost insulation from downstream molecular load
open: Can an upstream molecular signaling module keep its dynamics essentially unchanged when arbitrary downstream loads are attached, without paying a large price in energy consumption, signaling bandwidth, or component count? More precisely, is there a general design principle for low-cost insulation of biomolecular circuits under variable downstream load?
status: A yeast phosphotransfer load driver was demonstrated in Mishanaboina et al. (2014), "A load driver device for engineering modularity in biological networks" (https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3044); general low-cost insulation across variable loads remains open. Related ideas come from electrical impedance matching and the thermodynamics of feedback.
solved_when: A construction or theorem is given that insulates upstream dynamics from variable downstream molecular load while keeping energy dissipation, bandwidth, and component costs within stated low bounds.
why: Without insulation, connecting a downstream module distorts the upstream behavior it was designed for, breaking compositional modularity in engineered biological systems.
key_works: Mishra et al. (2014), [A load driver device for engineering modularity in biological networks](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3044).

title: Learning within protein neural circuits
open: Can a protein-level neural circuit inside a living cell adapt its classification behavior from feedback, rather than relying on externally retuned parameters? Formally, this asks for an intracellular learning rule that updates a protein classifier while preserving its earlier useful classifications.
status: Perceptein circuits demonstrated tunable winner-take-all classification in 2024; onboard learning remains a separate target. Key work: Chen et al. (2024), [A synthetic protein-level neural network in mammalian cells](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.add8468).
solved_when: An intracellular protein classifier is experimentally shown to learn from feedback and adapt its behavior, while retaining previously learned useful classifications.
why: It would enable adaptive cellular decision-making, letting engineered cells correct their own protein-level classification instead of requiring external retuning.
key_works: Chen et al. (2024), [A synthetic protein-level neural network in mammalian cells](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.add8468).

title: Composable multivariable intracellular control
open: Can a cell be engineered so that several outputs and their ratios are regulated independently even when they draw on shared intracellular resources? A formal version asks for a control architecture with explicit stability guarantees and quantitative cross-coupling bounds between the regulated variables.
status: Resource-aware multilayer autocatalytic models solved selected concentration and ratio-control tasks in 2025 (Zand et al. (2025), [Multi-Layer Autocatalytic Feedback Enables Integral Control Amidst Resource Competition and Across Scales](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.4c00575)); general experimental designs remain open. Related work exists in decentralized control of coupled positive systems.
solved_when: A resource-aware control design is provided that independently regulates multiple outputs and ratios in the presence of shared resources, with explicit stability and cross-coupling bounds, and demonstrated beyond selected concentration and ratio-control tasks on general experimental designs.
why: Solving it enables coordinated control of complex cellular programs, where many modules must function simultaneously without resource competition degrading their performance.
key_works: Zand et al. (2025), [Multi-Layer Autocatalytic Feedback Enables Integral Control Amidst Resource Competition and Across Scales](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.4c00575).

title: Experimental inverse design of arbitrary spatial expression patterns
subfield: Spatial computation and programmed multicellular organization
open: Given a desired two- or three-dimensional spatial expression pattern, can we automatically design a gene regulatory circuit that, when implemented in cells, realizes the pattern within a specified spatial error tolerance?
status: Automated design produced diverse patterns in simulations in 2024 (Mousavi and Lobo (2024), [Automatic design of gene regulatory mechanisms for spatial pattern formation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41540-024-00361-5)); prospective physical realization remains open.
solved_when: A desired 2D or 3D expression pattern is converted into a realizable circuit that is physically implemented and reproduces the target pattern within the specified spatial error.
why: It would make programmed multicellular organization practical, turning arbitrary spatial patterns into buildable biology rather than simulation-only designs.
key_works: Mousavi and Lobo (2024), [Automatic design of gene regulatory mechanisms for spatial pattern formation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41540-024-00361-5).

title: Comparable active-learning efficiency across real DBTL tasks
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Do experiment-selection (active-learning) methods genuinely differ in how many experiments they save when deployed on real design–build–test–learn tasks, rather than on retrospective benchmarks? The question is whether a controlled prospective comparison — equal budgets, identical starting information, matching delays, assay noise levels, and stopping criteria — reveals meaningful efficiency gaps between methods on real biofoundry workflows.
status: ART demonstrated probabilistic engineering recommendations in 2020 (Radivojević et al. (2020), [A machine learning Automated Recommendation Tool for synthetic biology](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-18008-4)); broad comparisons on unfamiliar tasks remain open.
solved_when: A prospective comparison of active-learning/experiment-selection methods is completed on real DBTL tasks in which all methods are run under equal budgets, identical starting information, matched delays and assay noise, and common stopping criteria, with reported experiment-savings outcomes across tasks unfamiliar to the method developers.
why: It identifies which algorithms actually save experiments, replacing benchmark-driven assumptions with evidence about real-world performance in biofoundry settings.
key_works: Radivojević et al. (2020), [A machine learning Automated Recommendation Tool for synthetic biology](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-18008-4).

title: Reproducible workflows across independent biofoundries
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Can a complete design–build–test–learn workflow be transferred between independently equipped biofoundries and still perform within predefined tolerances?
status: An interoperable workflow hierarchy was proposed in 2025 (Kim et al. (2025), [Abstraction hierarchy to define biofoundry workflows and operations for interoperable synthetic biology research and applications](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61263-6)); prospective round-robin equivalence remains a further requirement.
solved_when: A workflow moved between differently equipped facilities is shown, prospectively and in a round-robin manner across facilities, to preserve performance within the predefined tolerances.
why: It enables distributed, reproducible biological manufacturing, so results and production do not depend on a single facility's equipment.
key_works: Kim et al. (2025), [Abstraction hierarchy to define biofoundry workflows and operations for interoperable synthetic biology research and applications](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61263-6).

title: Full catalytic-cycle conformational design
open: Can we design an enzyme whose conformational ensemble supports every stage of a full catalytic cycle — substrate entry, all chemical steps, product release, and reset — so that turnover is predicted correctly, not just the stabilization of a single transition-state geometry?
status: Ensemble-based serine-hydrolase design advanced multistep treatment in 2025; complete-cycle prediction remains unresolved. Key work: Lauko et al. (2025), [Computational design of serine hydrolases](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adu2454).
solved_when: A design method produces enzymes whose conformational populations across the entire cycle yield correct turnover predictions, covering substrate entry, all chemical steps, product release, and reset.
why: It would move computational enzyme design beyond optimizing one transition-state geometry to engineering the complete dynamics of a working catalyst.
key_works: Lauko et al. (2025), [Computational design of serine hydrolases](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adu2454).

title: Autonomous orthogonal redox homeostasis
open: Can an engineered cell autonomously hold the pool size and reduction potential of a noncanonical redox cofactor at set levels while demand on it fluctuates? Formally, this asks for an internal synthesis, regeneration, and replacement system that keeps an orthogonal cofactor economy homeostatic under perturbation.
status: Intracellular synthesis of nicotinamide cytosine dinucleotide was established in Wang et al. (2021), [Creating enzymes and self-sufficient cells for biosynthesis of the non-natural cofactor nicotinamide cytosine dinucleotide](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-22357-z); a robust additional redox economy remains open.
solved_when: A cell is demonstrated whose noncanonical-cofactor abundance and reduction potential are maintained by its own synthesis, regeneration, and replacement machinery despite changing metabolic demand, without external cofactor supply.
why: A stable, independent redox economy lets redox-intensive production pathways run in parallel with native metabolism without draining or being drained by the cell's natural cofactors.
key_works: Wang et al. (2021), [Creating enzymes and self-sufficient cells for biosynthesis of the non-natural cofactor nicotinamide cytosine dinucleotide](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-22357-z).

title: Complete THETA-cycle autotrophy
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can a living cell run the complete THETA cycle as its sole route of carbon assimilation? In other words, can the full cycle operate in vivo with sustained net carbon fixation into biomass and products, with no hidden supplementation from organic carbon sources?
status: The 17-enzyme cycle was constructed in vitro in 2023, with three separate modules validated in cells; integrated autotrophy remains open. Key work: Luo et al. (2023), [Construction and modular implementation of the THETA cycle for synthetic CO₂ fixation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-023-01079-z).
solved_when: An engineered organism harboring all 17 THETA-cycle enzymes demonstrates sustained net inorganic-carbon assimilation into biomass and products in vivo, with no organic-carbon supplementation contributing to growth.
why: Success would establish a new whole-cell carbon-fixation architecture, expanding the set of synthetic autotrophy platforms available for one-carbon biomanufacturing.
key_works: Luo et al. (2023), [Construction and modular implementation of the THETA cycle for synthetic CO₂ fixation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-023-01079-z).

title: Practical biological methane-to-methanol conversion
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can methane be converted biologically to methanol at titers, rates, and selectivities that make the process economically practical, under realistic constraints on reductant supply, gas transfer, and dilute methane feeds?
status: An engineered miniature soluble methane monooxygenase system reported about 3 g/L methanol and 0.11 g/L/h in 2024 (Yu et al. (2024), [A rationally designed miniature of soluble methane monooxygenase enables rapid and high-yield methanol production in Escherichia coli](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-48671-w)); integrated competitiveness remains open.
solved_when: An engineered biological system sustains selective methane-to-methanol conversion while meeting or exceeding the benchmark of about 3 g/L methanol at about 0.11 g/L/h under realistic operating conditions, with integrated process competitiveness demonstrated.
why: It would turn dilute or stranded methane resources into a liquid, transportable fuel and chemical feedstock, converting a potent greenhouse gas into useful product.
key_works: Yu et al. (2024), [A rationally designed miniature of soluble methane monooxygenase enables rapid and high-yield methanol production in Escherichia coli](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-48671-w).

title: Cost-competitive artificial starch
open: Can starch be produced from CO₂ by an artificial route at a measured cost and energy demand competitive with agricultural production? A full solution must account for every input — enzymes, hydrogen, cofactor recycling, and downstream purification and recovery.
status: An eleven-reaction chemoenzymatic pathway synthesizing starch from CO₂ was demonstrated in 2021; the full-process economics and any environmental advantage over agriculture remain open.
solved_when: Purified starch is produced from CO₂ with a measured cost and energy demand competitive with conventional production, with the accounting including enzymes, hydrogen, recycling, and recovery.
why: Success would decouple carbohydrate supply from farmland, sharply reducing the land requirements for starch production.
key_works: Cai et al. (2021), [Cell-free chemoenzymatic starch synthesis from carbon dioxide](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abh4049).

title: Efficient depolymerization of bulk nylon
open: Can crystalline, high-molecular-weight nylon be converted back into recoverable monomers at practically useful rates, without resorting to severe pretreatment?
status: Diverse nylon-6 enzymes were characterized in 2024, but demonstrated oligomer hydrolysis does not establish efficient recycling of the bulk polymer. Bell et al. (2024), [Natural diversity screening, assay development, and characterization of nylon-6 enzymatic depolymerization](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-45523-5).
solved_when: A process achieves depolymerization of bulk crystalline high-molecular-weight nylon into recoverable monomers at practical rates, with no severe pretreatment step.
why: It would open biological recycling of a major class of polyamides, diverting bulk nylon waste from landfill or energy recovery.
key_works: Bell et al. (2024), [Natural diversity screening, assay development, and characterization of nylon-6 enzymatic depolymerization](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-45523-5).

title: Repeated mechanical repair over realistic service lifetimes
open: Can an engineered living material recover its specified strength and toughness again and again across a realistic service lifetime? Formally, this means repeated mechanical repair while the material endures realistic wet–dry, temperature, and nutrient cycling.
status: Healable and tunable living materials were demonstrated in 2024, per Manjula-Basavanna, Duraj-Thatte, and Joshi (2024), [Mechanically Tunable, Compostable, Healable and Scalable Engineered Living Materials](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-53052-4); extended service-life mechanical reliability remains open.
solved_when: The material restores its specified strength and toughness repeatedly under realistic wet–dry, temperature, and nutrient cycles, with demonstrated extended service-life mechanical reliability.
why: It would turn self-repair from a laboratory demonstration into a dependable engineering property that can be specified and trusted in design.
key_works: Manjula-Basavanna, Duraj-Thatte, and Joshi (2024), [Mechanically Tunable, Compostable, Healable and Scalable Engineered Living Materials](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-53052-4).

title: Predictable synthetic lineage transitions
open: Can synthetic gene circuits drive a predetermined sequence of cell-fate decisions reproducibly across different donor cell lines? In formal terms, can a synthetic lineage-control network execute a specified differentiation program in any donor line with only low off-target lineage formation and full maturation of the intended cell type?
status: A synthetic network generated glucose-sensitive beta-like cells in 2016; broad transfer across donors and lineages remains open. Key work: Saxena et al. (2016), [A programmable synthetic lineage-control network that differentiates human IPSCs into glucose-sensitive insulin-secreting beta-like cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms11247).
solved_when: A specified cell-fate sequence is reproduced across multiple donor lines, with low off-target lineage formation and mature function of the desired differentiated cell type.
why: It would make production of differentiated cells reproducible rather than donor-dependent, turning cell therapies and tissue engineering from bespoke efforts into a predictable manufacturing process.
key_works: Saxena et al. (2016), [A programmable synthetic lineage-control network that differentiates human IPSCs into glucose-sensitive insulin-secreting beta-like cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms11247).

title: Tissue repair to a programmed stopping condition
open: Can an engineered tissue reliably regenerate to a pre-programmed size and cell-type composition after repeated rounds of injury, and then stop? Formally, this asks for a synthetic circuit or design principle that restores specified tissue dimensions and proportions while returning proliferation and cell loss to a homeostatic balance.
status: Simple structures were self-repaired by Toda et al. (2018), [Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0271); quantitative size restoration with reliable growth arrest remains open.
solved_when: A specified tissue recovers its target size and cell proportions after repeated injury and proliferation/loss reliably returns to homeostatic balance without further intervention.
why: It enables regeneration without progressive overgrowth or lineage depletion.
key_works: Toda et al. (2018), [Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0271).

title: Plant-autonomous nitrogen fixation with net agronomic benefit
open: Can a plant supply a meaningful fraction of its own nitrogen demand through nitrogen fixation engineered into its cells, without paying a larger penalty in energy or growth? In other words, can cereal crops be made autonomously nitrogen-fixing to an agronomically useful degree?
status: In 2022, plant-produced NifB supported cofactor synthesis in vitro after cluster reconstitution, but this did not demonstrate nitrogen fixation inside plants. Key work: Jiang et al. (2022), [Functional Nitrogenase Cofactor Maturase NifB in Mitochondria and Chloroplasts of Nicotiana benthamiana](https://doi.org/10.1128/mbio.00268-22).
solved_when: A plant demonstrates internal nitrogen fixation that supplies a meaningful fraction of cereal nitrogen demand while showing no larger energy or growth penalty than the fixation benefit it delivers.
why: Success could substantially reduce dependence on synthetic nitrogen fertilizer, cutting a major cost and environmental burden of cereal agriculture.
key_works: Jiang et al. (2022), [Functional Nitrogenase Cofactor Maturase NifB in Mitochondria and Chloroplasts of Nicotiana benthamiana](https://doi.org/10.1128/mbio.00268-22).

title: A complete chloroplast carbon-concentrating mechanism
open: Can a crop chloroplast be engineered with a fully functional carbon-concentrating mechanism — carboxysomes, inorganic-carbon transporters, and control of CO₂ leakage — that raises net carbon assimilation under ambient air?
status: Carboxysome-containing tobacco supported autotrophic photosynthesis at elevated CO₂ in 2023; complete ambient-air concentration remains open. Key work: Chen et al. (2023), [Engineering α-carboxysomes into plant chloroplasts to support autotrophic photosynthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-37490-0).
solved_when: A engineered chloroplast combining carboxysomes, inorganic-carbon transport, and leakage control demonstrates improved net assimilation under ambient (not elevated) CO₂.
why: It would raise photosynthetic carbon efficiency in crops, converting a cyanobacterial-style concentration mechanism into a working agricultural trait rather than a greenhouse-only curiosity.
key_works: Chen et al. (2023), [Engineering α-carboxysomes into plant chloroplasts to support autotrophic photosynthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-37490-0).

title: Reliable synthetic apomixis across crops
open: Can we engineer synthetic apomixis — clonal seed formation — that reliably preserves hybrid genotypes across diverse crops, while maintaining fertility, germination, and multigeneration agronomic performance? In formal terms, the goal is a portable engineering strategy for apomictic seed production whose performance holds beyond the current rice demonstrations.
status: High-frequency synthetic apomixis was achieved in rice in 2022 (Vernet et al. (2022), [High-frequency synthetic apomixis in hybrid rice](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-35679-3)), followed by fertility advances; broad crop portability remains open.
solved_when: Synthetic apomixis is demonstrated at high frequency in crops beyond rice, with preserved hybrid genotypes through clonal seed, and with maintained fertility, germination, and multigeneration agronomic performance.
why: It would let farmers preserve hybrid vigor through saved seed, eliminating the need to re-purchase hybrid seed each generation.
key_works: Vernet et al. (2022), [High-frequency synthetic apomixis in hybrid rice](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-35679-3).

title: Predictable therapeutic-strain abundance in diverse human guts
open: Can we predict and control the abundance of a therapeutically introduced microbial strain in the human gut, across different diets and resident communities, without broadly disrupting the ecosystem? More formally, the goal is cohort-general quantitative control of engrafted-strain abundance.
status: Dietary-niche control was demonstrated in mice in 2018 (Shepherd et al. (2018), [An exclusive metabolic niche enables strain engraftment in the gut microbiota](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0092-4)), and reversible engraftment in humans was shown in 2025 (Whitaker et al. (2025), [Controlled colonization of the human gut with a genetically engineered microbial therapeutic](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adu8000)); cohort-general quantitative control remains open.
solved_when: Introduced-strain abundance can be predicted and controlled quantitatively across diets and resident communities, in a cohort-general manner, without broad ecosystem disruption.
why: It would make the exposure delivered by living medicines predictable, turning engineered microbes into dosable therapeutics rather than uncertain colonizers.
key_works: Shepherd et al. (2018), [An exclusive metabolic niche enables strain engraftment in the gut microbiota](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-018-0092-4); Whitaker et al. (2025), [Controlled colonization of the human gut with a genetically engineered microbial therapeutic](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adu8000).

title: Knowing when pairwise community models fail
open: When can a microbiome community's dynamics be reliably predicted from pairwise interaction measurements alone? Establish testable conditions under which pairwise models are guaranteed to work, and bound the number of experiments needed to detect when higher-order interactions are required.
status: Pairwise modeling successfully described a defined gut community in 2018; general approximation limits remain unresolved. Key works: Venturelli et al. (2018), [Deciphering microbial interactions in synthetic human gut microbiome communities](https://doi.org/10.15252/msb.20178157).
solved_when: There exist checkable conditions for deciding whether a pairwise model reliably describes a given community, together with an explicit bound on the number of experiments needed to detect necessary higher-order interactions.
why: It determines how much community complexity must be measured, telling experimenters when pairwise assays suffice and when they must be supplemented with higher-order measurements.
key_works: Venturelli et al. (2018), [Deciphering microbial interactions in synthetic human gut microbiome communities](https://doi.org/10.15252/msb.20178157).

title: Selective recall of deployed living medicines
open: Can a deployed therapeutic microbial population be recalled from a host on demand — cleared from every spatial refuge it may occupy — without harming the resident microbiome and without later rebound from surviving remnants? Formally, this asks for a removal strategy achieving complete, durable recall of the engineered strain while preserving resident community composition.
status: Controllable microbial removal was demonstrated in 2022, but complete durable recall in humans remains a stronger, unmet criterion. Key work: Rottinghaus et al. (2022), [Genetically stable CRISPR-based kill switches for engineered microbes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-28163-5).
solved_when: A demonstrated removal method recalls the therapeutic population completely and durably in a human host — no delayed rebound from residual cells — while leaving resident communities intact.
why: It would make persistent living medicines reversible, so a therapy that stays in the body long after deployment can be reliably withdrawn when it is no longer wanted or is causing harm.
key_works: Rottinghaus et al. (2022), [Genetically stable CRISPR-based kill switches for engineered microbes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-28163-5).

title: Francevillian biota
open: Were the Francevillian biota organisms genuinely multicellular, making them among the earliest known multicellular life? More precisely, can their fossils be shown to represent coordinated multicellular organisms rather than aggregations of single cells or abiotic structures?
solved_when: A defensible determination, from the fossil evidence, of whether the Francevillian biota were early multicellular organisms or not.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20biology

title: Xenacoelomorpha
open: Where do the Xenacoelomorpha sit on the animal tree of life — are they deuterostomes, forming the clade Xenambulacraria together with echinoderms and hemichordates, or are they instead primitive bilaterians, sister group to the Nephrozoa?
solved_when: A well-supported resolution of xenacoelomorph phylogenetic position is established: either Xenambulacraria (Xenacoelomorpha + Ambulacraria as deuterostomes) or Xenacoelomorpha as sister to Nephrozoa is convincingly demonstrated.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20biology

title: Nervous system
open: Why do Lobatocerebridae — simple, unsegmented annelids that feed unselectively on deposits and lack sense organs — possess a relatively complex brain?
solved_when: An explanation (evolutionary, developmental, or ecological) is given for why these organ-less, unselective deposit feeders evolve and maintain a relatively complex brain, supported by detailed reconstruction of their nervous system.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20biology

title: Glycogen body
open: What is the function of the glycogen body, a structure found in the spinal cord of birds? A satisfying answer would identify its physiological role and explain why this glycogen-rich organ is maintained in the avian cord.
status: The problem is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07).
solved_when: The biological function of the glycogen body is identified and experimentally confirmed, accounting for its glycogen content and localization in the bird spinal cord.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20biology

title: Arthropod head problem
open: How are the heads of the different arthropod groups built from segments, and how are those head segments evolutionarily related across groups? More precisely, which segmental correspondences among the heads of insects, crustaceans, chelicerates, and myriapods reflect shared ancestry?
status: The problem remains listed as unsolved on Wikipedia (2026-10-07), per the list of unsolved problems in biology (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20biology).
solved_when: A consensus account of the segmental composition of arthropod heads exists that is consistent across arthropod groups and supported by comparative developmental and morphological evidence.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20biology

title: Mitochondria
open: Do loriciferans living under anoxic conditions possess mitochondria? In particular, it is unknown whether members of the phylum Loricifera adapted to life in the anoxic L'Atalante basin, such as *Spinoloricus cinziae*, have mitochondria.
status: The question is listed as unsolved on Wikipedia's list of unsolved problems in biology (as of 2026-10-07); no further state-of-the-art details appear in the record.
solved_when: Direct evidence establishes whether anoxic-adapted loriciferans such as *Spinoloricus cinziae* possess mitochondria or lack them.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20biology

title: Ten-generation macromolecular autonomy
open: Can a synthetic cell built from the bottom up sustain ten successive growth–division generations while internally renewing all of its macromolecular components — proteins, ribosomes, genome, and membrane — from only specified small-molecule nutrients and energy? Formally, this demands coupled, internally driven synthesis of every macromolecular class so that reproduction proceeds without externally supplied macromolecules.
status: The July 2026 SpudCell preprint reports five generations with feeding and mechanical division; genetically dependent division was demonstrated separately. Complete macromolecular autonomy remains open. Key work: Gaut et al. (2026), [A Chemically Defined Synthetic Cell Capable Of Growth And Replication](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.01.735724), preprint.
solved_when: A bottom-up cell lineage achieves at least ten growth–division generations with internal synthesis of proteins, ribosomes, genome, and membrane, using only the specified small-molecule nutrient and energy sources.
why: It would establish that autonomous cellular reproduction can be constructed reproducibly from defined parts, a milestone for bottom-up synthetic biology and a benchmark for origins-of-life scenarios of how autonomous reproduction first emerged.
key_works: Gaut et al. (2026), [A Chemically Defined Synthetic Cell Capable Of Growth And Replication](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.01.735724), preprint.

title: Tenfold lower full-cost cell-free protein manufacture
open: Can cell-free protein manufacturing achieve a tenfold reduction in the full cost per gram of correctly folded, recovered protein relative to a reproducible baseline? The reduction must account for the complete process — preparation, purification, quality control, and the cost of failed batches — not just reagent prices.
status: Low-cost formulations advanced in 2026, notably Olsen et al. (2026), [Design-driven optimization of low-cost reagent formulations for reproducible and high-yielding cell-free gene expression](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69605-8); however, reagent savings alone do not establish full manufacturing-cost reductions.
solved_when: A demonstrated process reaches a tenfold lower cost per gram of correctly folded, recovered protein against a reproducible baseline, with all costs included: preparation, purification, QC, and failed batches.
why: A solution makes distributed and small-batch protein production genuinely accessible, rather than confined to centralized high-volume facilities.
key_works: Olsen et al. (2026), [Design-driven optimization of low-cost reagent formulations for reproducible and high-yielding cell-free gene expression](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69605-8).

title: Complete EuMP-cycle methylotrophy
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can the erythrulose-monophosphate (EuMP) cycle be closed in a living cell, so that a microbe grows and produces target compounds using formaldehyde derived from methanol as its sole carbon source? Formally, this asks for an engineered organism in which the full cyclic pathway operates end-to-end in vivo, with each turn of the cycle regenerating its acceptor metabolite.
status: The constituent pathway modules were demonstrated in engineered sensor strains in 2023 (Wu et al. (2023), [Engineering a synthetic energy-efficient formaldehyde assimilation cycle in Escherichia coli](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-44247-2)); complete-cycle production remains open.
solved_when: An engineered organism demonstrates the complete EuMP cycle functioning in vivo, sustaining both growth and product formation from methanol-derived formaldehyde.
why: It would establish an alternative, energy-efficient architecture for one-carbon assimilation, expanding the design space for methylotrophy-based biomanufacturing beyond naturally occurring pathways.
key_works: Wu et al. (2023), [Engineering a synthetic energy-efficient formaldehyde assimilation cycle in Escherichia coli](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-44247-2).

title: Butterfly migration
open: How do the descendants of monarch butterflies spread across Canada and the US, after migrating over several generations, ultimately find their way back to a few small overwintering sites?
solved_when: A mechanism is identified that accounts for how successive generations of monarch butterflies across Canada and the US navigate to the same few relatively small overwintering spots.
key_works: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List%20of%20unsolved%20problems%20in%20biology

title: Purification-free renewal of the complete PURE proteome
open: Can a complete PURE cell-free transcription–translation system renew its own proteome in place, so that every nonribosomal protein is continuously replaced through repeated growth-and-dilution cycles without any purification step or external addition of enzymes?
status: Mottaghi and Maerkl (2026) synthesized all 36 proteins together and recovered functional PURE after purification ([PURE makes PURE: reconstitution of the PURE cell-free system from self-synthesized proteins](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73337-0)); continuous internal renewal remains unresolved.
solved_when: A reactor sustains functional PURE transcription–translation through repeated dilution rounds in which all 36 PURE proteins are internally resynthesized, with no purification or externally supplied enzymes at any point.
why: It removes the last major external maintenance dependency of PURE-based synthetic cells, moving them toward autonomous self-renewal.
key_works: Mottaghi and Maerkl (2026), [PURE makes PURE: reconstitution of the PURE cell-free system from self-synthesized proteins](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73337-0).

title: Translation-component stoichiometry under self-regeneration
open: Can a self-regenerating protocell hold its translation machinery in the right proportions indefinitely, even though its components are synthesized at unequal rates, degraded unevenly, and partitioned randomly at division? The goal is to derive feedback rules — and implement them — that stabilize functional ratios of the translation components in such a coupled autocatalytic network.
status: Localized simultaneous production of 30 translation proteins was demonstrated in 2026, but functionality remains sensitive to dilution and spatial organization; see Schwarz-Schilling et al. (2026), [Autonomous biogenesis of all thirty proteins of the Escherichia coli translation machinery](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67772-8).
solved_when: Feedback rules are derived and implemented that maintain functional translation-component ratios under unequal synthesis, degradation, and partitioning, preventing depletion of any indispensable component.
why: Without such control, a single indispensable translation component can be diluted or lost, causing the whole self-regeneration process to fail.
key_works: Schwarz-Schilling et al. (2026), [Autonomous biogenesis of all thirty proteins of the Escherichia coli translation machinery](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67772-8).

title: Demand-responsive synthetic tRNA pools
open: Can a synthetic translation system adjust the abundance of individual tRNAs in response to changing codon demand, while preserving measured translation fidelity and throughput? More formally, this asks for demand-responsive control over a synthetic tRNA pool rather than fixed, unregulated expression of its members.
status: All 21 minimal tRNAs were expressed from one template in 2025; position-dependent abundance and unregulated expression remain limitations.
solved_when: A synthetic tRNA pool is demonstrated in which individual tRNA abundances are tuned to codon demand without degrading measured translation fidelity or throughput, overcoming the position-dependent abundance and unregulated expression limitations of current single-template expression.
why: It would let researchers reprogram protein-coding sequences without exhausting particular decoding resources, making protocell translation robust to arbitrary codon usage changes.
key_works: Miyachi et al. (2025), [Simultaneous in vitro expression of minimal 21 transfer RNAs by tRNA array method](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62588-y).

title: Minimal tRNA maturation and modification requirements
open: Which tRNA processing and modification steps are actually required for accurate translation of a full proteome? More precisely, what is the minimal set of maturation and modification events sufficient to sustain faithful, proteome-wide decoding in a synthetic cell?
status: Continually transcribed minimal tRNA sets sustained reporter translation in 2025 (Li, Baranwal, and Maerkl (2025), [Continuous in situ synthesis of a complete set of tRNAs sustains steady-state translation in a recombinant cell-free system](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61671-8)), but proteome-wide accuracy and maturation sufficiency remain unestablished.
solved_when: A defined set of tRNA processing and modification steps is shown to be sufficient for accurate translation of an entire synthetic-cell proteome.
why: It tests whether simplified decoding systems can support complete cellular reproduction, a central question for bottom-up synthetic cells and protocells.
key_works: Li, Baranwal, and Maerkl (2025), [Continuous in situ synthesis of a complete set of tRNAs sustains steady-state translation in a recombinant cell-free system](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61671-8).

title: Reliable segregation of a synthetic genome
open: Can a synthetic cell be engineered so that, over many successive divisions, every essential genetic element is delivered to each daughter with a loss rate that is quantified and low — with no post-hoc selection of the viable daughters? Formally, this asks for a segregation mechanism whose inheritance error rate per division is measured and bounded, rather than merely demonstrated anecdotally.
status: A 2021 synthetic-cell-cycle roadmap (Olivi et al. (2021), [Towards a synthetic cell cycle](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-24772-8)) identified segregation as an integration bottleneck: existing replication and division modules operate separately and do not jointly establish reliable inheritance.
solved_when: A synthetic protocell lineage undergoes repeated divisions in which both daughters reliably receive the full complement of required genetic components, the per-division loss rate is quantitatively measured, and no selection step discards failed daughters to sustain the lineage.
why: Without reliable segregation, DNA replication produces copies that are not inherited, so synthetic cells cannot form stable, evolving lineages; solving it converts replication into heredity.
key_works: Olivi et al. (2021), [Towards a synthetic cell cycle](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-24772-8).

title: Complete FtsZ-driven vesicle scission
open: Can a synthetic vesicle be made to divide completely — membrane scission and all — driven by FtsZ assembled inside it, so that daughter vesicles retain their contents and can divide again?
status: Large equatorial FtsZ rings have constricted vesicles to almost complete closure (Panevska et al. (2026), [Optimizing spatial organization of FtsZ rings for large-scale constriction in synthetic cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-70091-1)); reproducible final neck scission remains a distinct, unsolved step.
solved_when: FtsZ constriction proceeds from ring formation through full neck scission, producing daughter vesicles that preserve encapsulated contents and support repeated division cycles.
why: It would supply an internally controlled mechanical division module, a core step toward self-reproducing synthetic cells.
key_works: Panevska et al. (2026), [Optimizing spatial organization of FtsZ rings for large-scale constriction in synthetic cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-70091-1).

title: Feedback between genome copying and membrane growth
open: Can DNA replication and membrane production be coupled so that each regulates the other, keeping genome dosage and cell size bounded across repeated cycles? In formal terms, a synthetic protocell in which genome copying and membrane growth form a closed mutual-feedback loop maintaining both quantities within fixed bounds over multiple generations.
status: Expression, DNA self-replication, and lipid synthesis were integrated together in vesicles in 2026 (Restrepo Sierra et al. (2026), [A synthetic cell with integrated DNA self-replication and lipid biosynthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69531-9)); however, coordinated control across multiple generations remains open.
solved_when: A protocell is demonstrated in which genome dosage and cell size remain bounded through repeated cycles, with DNA replication and membrane production each actively regulating the other, rather than merely co-occurring.
why: Without such feedback, integrated synthetic cells suffer overreplication of the genome, membrane starvation, and drift in cell size — failures that break multigeneration propagation.
key_works: Restrepo Sierra et al. (2026), [A synthetic cell with integrated DNA self-replication and lipid biosynthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69531-9).

title: One-chromosome replication at synthetic-cell genome scale
open: Can a bottom-up synthetic cell faithfully replicate a single chromosome that carries its entire genome — fast enough that genome copies keep pace with growth and division?
status: Self-encoded DNA replication in liposomes dates to 2018, with Van Nies et al. (2018) showing self-replication of DNA by its encoded proteins in liposome-based synthetic cells. The SpudCell program (Gaut et al., 2026) is multipartite, so integration into a single chromosome remains open.
solved_when: A synthetic cell demonstrates accurate copying of one chromosome encoding the complete chosen synthetic-cell program, at a rate sufficient to replenish genomes during growth.
why: A single-chromosome design reduces assortment failures and simplifies inheritance, removing a key obstacle to reliable reproduction of synthetic cells.
key_works: Van Nies et al. (2018), [Self-replication of DNA by its encoded proteins in liposome-based synthetic cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-03926-1); Gaut et al. (2026), [SpudCell preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.07.01.735724).

title: Homeostatic membrane composition
open: Can a synthetic or protocellular membrane hold a prescribed lipid composition while it keeps growing, even as precursor supply, enzyme abundance, and selective lipid loss shift over time? In other words, can composition homeostasis be sustained across multiple generations of membrane synthesis rather than in a single burst?
status: Genetically controlled, metabolically balanced membrane synthesis was demonstrated in Blanken et al. (2020), [Genetically controlled membrane synthesis in liposomes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-17863-5); multigeneration composition control remains a stronger, unmet requirement.
solved_when: A growing membrane maintains its target lipid ratios over multiple generations under changing precursor supply, enzyme abundance, and selective lipid loss.
why: Lipid composition controls permeability, curvature, and protein activity, so composition drift undermines any downstream function built on the membrane.
key_works: Blanken et al. (2020), [Genetically controlled membrane synthesis in liposomes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-17863-5).

title: Self-renewing membrane protein insertion
open: Can a synthetic membrane continuously regenerate its own proteins — and the machinery that inserts them — while membrane growth proceeds, without losing correct orientation, folding, activity, or density of those proteins?
status: DNA-directed membrane-enzyme synthesis is established, per Blanken et al. (2020), [Genetically controlled membrane synthesis in liposomes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-17863-5); however, a membrane proteome that renews its own assembly machinery over generations remains open.
solved_when: A synthetic cell or protocell membrane expands over generations while its membrane proteome maintains correct orientation, folding, activity, and density, renewing both the membrane proteins and the insertion machinery that assembles them.
why: It unlocks sustained transport and energy conservation in synthetic cells, which otherwise deplete as membrane components and their assembly machinery fail to be replaced.
key_works: Blanken et al. (2020), [Genetically controlled membrane synthesis in liposomes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-17863-5).

title: Coupled osmotic, ionic, and pH homeostasis
open: Can a synthetic cell simultaneously keep its volume, ionic strength, and pH within bounds while it takes up nutrients, expresses genes, and accumulates waste? Formally, this asks for an engineered, energy-coupled homeostatic layer that regulates osmotic, ionic, and acid–base state together in a genetically active, growing protocell.
status: Energy-coupled physicochemical homeostasis was reconstructed in vesicles in 2019; its integration with growing, genetically active cells remains unresolved (Pols et al. (2019), [A synthetic metabolic network for physicochemical homeostasis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-12287-2)).
solved_when: A growing, genetically active synthetic cell is demonstrated to maintain stable volume, ionic strength, and pH throughout nutrient uptake, expression, and waste accumulation.
why: Without coupled homeostasis, otherwise functional modules destabilize one another, so no integrated synthetic cell can run reliably.
key_works: Pols et al. (2019), [A synthetic metabolic network for physicochemical homeostasis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-12287-2).

title: Closed protein turnover and amino-acid recycling
open: Can a synthetic or artificial cell be built in which selectively damaged proteins are degraded and their amino acids recycled back into protein synthesis, without the degradation machinery destroying the essential translation apparatus itself? In formal terms, this asks for a coupled proteolysis–translation system whose material loop closes, so that amino-acid flux from proteolysis feeds synthesis rather than being lost as waste.
status: Simultaneous protein synthesis and ClpXP-mediated degradation were demonstrated in cell-free systems in 2018, in Shi et al. (2018), [Optimization of ClpXP activity and protein synthesis in an E. coli extract-based cell-free expression system](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-21739-6); however, closed recycling of amino acids and self-maintaining quality control remain unachieved additional requirements.
solved_when: A cell-free or protocell system demonstrates selective degradation of damaged proteins together with amino-acid reuse in protein synthesis, while maintaining translation activity — i.e., closed recycling and self-maintaining quality control operating concurrently.
why: Closing the protein-turnover loop would allow synthetic cells to run for extended periods with bounded material inputs, rather than exhausting their amino-acid supply and halting as waste accumulates.
key_works: Shi et al. (2018), [Optimization of ClpXP activity and protein synthesis in an E. coli extract-based cell-free expression system](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-21739-6).

title: Parasite-resistant protocell heredity
open: Under what experimentally validated conditions can a protocell population preserve cooperative genetic functions in the face of continuously arising faster-copying parasitic sequences? Formally, the question asks for a mechanism or regime — compartmentalization, assortment, or otherwise — demonstrated in experiment, in which heredity of useful functions persists despite parasite pressure.
status: Transient compartmentalization was shown to prevent parasite takeover in 2016, but growing, heritable compartments introduce further assortment and selection constraints that remain to be worked out. Key work: Matsumura et al. (2016), [Transient compartmentalization of RNA replicators prevents extinction due to parasites](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aag1582).
solved_when: A set of conditions is identified and experimentally validated under which cooperative genetic functions are preserved despite continuously arising faster-copying parasitic sequences.
why: It would make protocell evolution compatible with the persistence of useful functions, rather than collapsing under parasitic exploitation.
key_works: Matsumura et al. (2016), [Transient compartmentalization of RNA replicators prevents extinction due to parasites](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aag1582).

title: Cell-level selection of multistep metabolic functions
open: Can a synthetic cell be engineered so that selection at the whole-cell level — reproduction — acts on a complete multistep metabolic pathway rather than a single gene? Formally, can cell-level fitness be coupled to multienzyme function tightly enough that evolution improves the integrated pathway, while design features block mutants that merely exploit the selection readout without genuinely improving the pathway?
status: A first step was achieved in 2026, when Sierra Heras and Danelon (2026), [Autocatalytic selection of gene functions in synthetic cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-026-10372-z), linked individual gene functions to DNA replication and enriched them; selection of complete pathway performance remains broader than what has been shown.
solved_when: A synthetic-cell system is demonstrated in which a complete multienzyme function is selected through its contribution to cell reproduction, with enrichment of the pathway as a whole, and with readout-exploiting improvements shown to be prevented.
why: It would turn synthetic cells into evolvable systems whose integrated functions — not just isolated genes — can be improved by directed evolution.
key_works: Sierra Heras and Danelon (2026), [Autocatalytic selection of gene functions in synthetic cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-026-10372-z).

title: Quantitative synthetic-cell module interfaces
open: Can we characterize synthetic-cell modules quantitatively so that their compatibility can be predicted before they are combined? The goal is a module description capturing resource demand, kinetics, inhibition, membrane coupling, and environmental tolerances that yields a general, experimentally validated compatibility calculus.
status: The 2025 international synthetic-cell summit called for coordinated integration, but no general experimentally validated compatibility calculus currently exists. See Giaveri et al. (2025), [Building a Synthetic Cell Together](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62778-8).
solved_when: A general compatibility calculus, grounded in quantitative module descriptions of resource demand, kinetics, inhibition, membrane coupling, and environmental tolerances, is experimentally validated across independently developed synthetic-cell modules.
why: Such descriptions would make independently developed modules composable, allowing modules built in different labs to be combined without ad hoc re-engineering.
key_works: Giaveri et al. (2025), [Building a Synthetic Cell Together](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62778-8).

title: Single-vesicle multigeneration accounting
open: Can we build a public benchmark that jointly tracks inheritance, molecular replacement, membrane growth, division, and supplied resources across the lineages of individual synthetic vesicles? Such a benchmark would let each of these coupled processes be measured together, in a single tracked lineage, rather than in separate experiments.
status: The 2026 Asian synthetic-cell roadmap proposes single-cell multi-omics and digital twins, but cross-module measurements remain fragmented. Reference: Chinese Academy of Sciences (2026), [Asian Scientists Unveil 10-year Roadmap for Building Synthetic Cells](https://english.cas.cn/newsroom/research-news/202605/t20260528_1159994.shtml).
solved_when: A public benchmark exists that jointly measures inheritance, molecular replacement, membrane growth, division, and supplied resources in tracked single-vesicle lineages.
why: It makes autonomy claims about synthetic cells quantitatively comparable, replacing fragmented cross-module measurements with a shared standard.
key_works: Chinese Academy of Sciences (2026), [Asian Scientists Unveil 10-year Roadmap for Building Synthetic Cells](https://english.cas.cn/newsroom/research-news/202605/t20260528_1159994.shtml).

title: Complete functional annotation of essential minimal-cell proteins
open: Can we determine, experimentally and with causal validation, the molecular function and physiological role of every protein in a minimal cell that remains uncharacterized? In other words, for each of the unannotated essential genes in JCVI-syn3.0, can we establish what the protein does and why the cell cannot live without it?
status: Annotation has advanced since JCVI-syn3.0's 2016 construction. A 2026 analysis, Mushegian et al. (2026), "Minimal organism JCVI-syn3.0… encodes an assortment of unrecognized membrane transporters and immunity factors" (https://doi.org/10.1128/msphere.00077-26), reports 50–60 previously unassigned proteins and proposes computational assignments that still require validation.
solved_when: Every remaining uncharacterized minimal-cell protein — including the 50–60 previously unassigned proteins reported in the 2026 analysis — has an experimentally assigned molecular function and physiological role with causal validation.
why: It converts a viable minimal genome into an understood one, replacing a list of essential genes with a mechanistic account of why each is essential.
key_works: Mushegian et al. (2026), [Minimal organism JCVI-syn3.0… encodes an assortment of unrecognized membrane transporters and immunity factors](https://doi.org/10.1128/msphere.00077-26).

title: Environment-indexed minimal genomes
open: For a precisely specified chemical environment, what is the smallest set of genes sufficient to sustain a living cell, and how does that set change when the environment's composition shifts? Formally, this asks for a mapping from environment descriptions to minimal viable gene sets, together with a predictive rule for which additional genes become required as conditions change.
status: A viable 473-gene genome was established in 2016 by Hutchison et al. (2016), [Design and synthesis of a minimal bacterial genome](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aad6253); this is a demonstrated genome size, not a proven minimum.
solved_when: For an explicitly specified environment, a minimal viable gene set is determined with a proof (or compelling demonstration) of minimality — not merely a working genome — and the additions required under a stated change in conditions are correctly predicted.
why: A solution would give conditional, environment-dependent definitions of the gene requirements for life and enable robust chassis design, where the organism's essential gene set is known for each intended operating environment.
key_works: Hutchison et al. (2016), [Design and synthesis of a minimal bacterial genome](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aad6253).

title: Predicting adaptation of minimized chassis
open: Can we predict which compensatory mutations arise after genome reduction in a minimized chassis, and whether adaptation will preserve engineered production traits across environments? More formally, is there a predictive framework linking genome minimization to the fitness-recovering mutational trajectories and their trade-offs with production?
status: Minimal cells recovered substantial fitness during 2,000 generations of evolution reported in 2023, but the trajectories and trade-offs remain difficult to predict; see Moger-Reischer et al. (2023), [Evolution of a minimal cell](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06288-x).
solved_when: A framework correctly predicts compensatory mutations (and their trajectories/trade-offs) following genome reduction and forecasts whether engineered production is preserved across environments, including the 2,000-generation evolutionary regime.
why: It would make simplified production organisms evolutionarily predictable, so engineered yields can be trusted to survive adaptation rather than being eroded by fitness recovery.
key_works: Moger-Reischer et al. (2023), [Evolution of a minimal cell](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06288-x).

title: Prospective whole-cell prediction under genome redesign
open: Can a computational model of a whole cell predict how an organism will grow, look, and respond molecularly after genome edits it has never seen, without any edit-specific parameter fitting? Formally, the target is calibrated prospective prediction of growth, morphology, and molecular phenotypes across substantial genome redesigns, with uncertainty quantification that holds out of distribution.
status: A complete spatial JCVI-syn3A cell cycle was modeled in 2026 (Thornburg et al. (2026), [Bringing the genetically minimal cell to life on a computer in 4D](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.02.009)); broad prospective prediction under substantial redesign remains a stronger test beyond that achievement.
solved_when: A model predicts growth, morphology, and molecular responses to previously unseen genome edits prospectively — before experiments are run — with calibrated uncertainty and no edit-specific fitting, across substantial genome redesign rather than single known perturbations.
why: It would make genome redesign reliable at the design stage, avoiding expensive construction of designs that fail, and would establish whole-cell models as predictive rather than descriptive tools.
key_works: Thornburg et al. (2026), [Bringing the genetically minimal cell to life on a computer in 4D](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.02.009).

title: Identifiable whole-cell parameter uncertainty
open: Which parameters of a whole-cell model can actually be identified from available data, and how should the uncertainty in the remaining, unidentifiable parameters be carried through into predictions of engineered phenotypes? Formally, this asks for a structural and practical identifiability analysis of whole-cell parameter sets together with a propagated uncertainty quantification on predicted phenotype outcomes.
status: Whole-cell genotype-to-phenotype modeling dates to 2012, with Karr et al. (2012), [A Whole-Cell Computational Model Predicts Phenotype from Genotype](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2012.05.044); many parameters still rely on estimates or measurements borrowed from other contexts.
solved_when: A characterization exists of the identifiable versus non-identifiable parameter subsets for whole-cell models, together with a method that propagates the unresolved parameter uncertainty into engineered-phenotype predictions, yielding predictions annotated with their uncertainty.
why: It separates reliable whole-cell predictions from nonunique fitted explanations, so engineers can tell which genotype-to-phenotype forecasts to trust.
key_works: Karr et al. (2012), [A Whole-Cell Computational Model Predicts Phenotype from Genotype](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2012.05.044).

title: Experimentally validated spatial inheritance distributions
open: Can we predict, and experimentally measure, the joint distributions of molecular partitioning, chromosome configuration, and daughter-cell physiology across generations of dividing cells? A complete answer would characterize the full multigenerational joint distribution — not merely average outcomes such as mean doubling time — for a spatial whole-cell model and its living counterpart.
status: The 2026 spatial whole-cell model predicts heterogeneous daughter states, but testing its predicted joint distributions requires richer data than average doubling times can provide. Relevant measurement capability is expected from multiplexed live-cell microscopy, with conceptual links to statistical physics of fluctuation propagation. Key work: Thornburg et al. (2026), [Bringing the genetically minimal cell to life on a computer in 4D](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.02.009).
solved_when: The joint distributions predicted by the 2026 spatial whole-cell model for molecular partitioning, chromosome configuration, and daughter physiology over multiple generations are quantitatively matched by experimentally measured distributions from live-cell observation.
why: It tests whether whole-cell models can reproduce cellular variability, not just average behavior — a direct probe of whether spatial whole-cell prediction captures the mechanisms generating heterogeneity.
key_works: Thornburg et al. (2026), [Bringing the genetically minimal cell to life on a computer in 4D](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2026.02.009).

title: Predicting interactions between synthetic chromosomes
open: Can we predict which combinations of individually tolerated synthetic chromosome designs will fail together? A general model is sought that forecasts deleterious transcriptional, metabolic, and dosage interactions among chromosome-scale designs before they are built.
status: Systematic debugging during Sc2.0 consolidation in 2023 exposed combinatorial defects among synthetic chromosomes, as reported in Zhao et al. (2023), [Debugging and consolidating multiple synthetic chromosomes reveals combinatorial genetic interactions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2023.09.025); a general predictive interaction map remains absent.
solved_when: A predictive interaction map exists that identifies deleterious combinations of individually tolerated designs prospectively, replacing the current reliance on empirical debugging during consolidation.
why: It would replace repeated empirical debugging with prospective design, avoiding the combinatorial defects that currently surface only during chromosome consolidation.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2023), [Debugging and consolidating multiple synthetic chromosomes reveals combinatorial genetic interactions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2023.09.025).

title: Predictable centromere placement
open: What sequence, chromatin, and transcriptional conditions make a centromere function reliably at a location of the designer's choosing? Formally, determine the rules governing centromere establishment and maintenance so that centromere placement on a synthetic chromosome is predictable rather than context-dependent.
