status: Relocated minimal yeast centromeres showed context-dependent activity and chromosome-copy effects in 2023; see Lauer et al. (2023), [Context-dependent neocentromere activity in synthetic yeast chromosome VIII](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100437).
solved_when: A stated set of sequence, chromatin, and transcriptional conditions is shown to confer reliable, context-independent centromere function at an arbitrary chosen locus.
why: Without such rules, centromere activity varies with genomic context and perturbs chromosome copy number, undermining any redesign of chromosome architecture; with them, chromosome engineering becomes dependable.
key_works: Lauer et al. (2023), [Context-dependent neocentromere activity in synthetic yeast chromosome VIII](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xgen.2023.100437).

title: Designer rDNA copy-number stability
open: Design rewritten or relocated rDNA arrays with predictable copy number, expression, recombination, and nucleolar function over extended growth.
status: Modified rDNA was regenerated at multiple locations in 2017; placement flexibility does not establish long-term quantitative stability.
why: Stabilizes a major repetitive and physiologically important genome region.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2017), [Engineering the ribosomal DNA in a megabase synthetic chromosome](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaf3981).

title: Faithful delivery of megabase mammalian constructs
open: Can we deliver megabase-scale DNA designs into diverse mammalian cells so that the constructs arrive intact, at predictable copy number, with reliable establishment efficiency and controlled rates of unintended changes? More precisely, the goal is a transfer method whose outcomes — construct intactness, copy number, establishment efficiency, and unintended-change rate — are predictable across diverse mammalian recipients.
status: Efficient single-copy human artificial chromosome formation advanced in 2024, per Gambogi et al. (2024), [Efficient formation of single-copy human artificial chromosomes](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adj3566); delivery across primary and differentiated cell types remains a broader open challenge.
solved_when: Megabase-scale constructs can be transferred into diverse mammalian cell types with predictable intactness, copy number, establishment efficiency, and unintended-change rates; the record states no quantitative thresholds.
why: It would enable large, coordinated mammalian genetic programs to be deployed reliably, rather than being bottlenecked at the delivery step.
key_works: Gambogi et al. (2024), [Efficient formation of single-copy human artificial chromosomes](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adj3566).

title: Artificial-chromosome epigenetic portability
open: Can an engineered artificial chromosome carry its segregation machinery and specified expression program intact through cell-state transitions, rather than depending on a favorable initial epigenetic accident for its establishment?
status: Single-copy formation was improved in 2024 (Gambogi et al. (2024), [Efficient formation of single-copy human artificial chromosomes](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adj3566)), but efficient formation, establishment, and long-term epigenetic stability remain separate requirements, and portability through cell-state transitions is unaddressed.
solved_when: An artificial chromosome is demonstrated to maintain stable single-copy segregation and its specified expression profile across cell-state transitions, with establishment that does not rely on a favorable initial epigenetic state.
why: This would make chromosome-scale synthetic programs portable across differentiation, so a program written once could function in any descendant cell state.
key_works: Gambogi et al. (2024), [Efficient formation of single-copy human artificial chromosomes](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adj3566).

title: Defined biochemical bootstrapping of a synthesized genome
open: Can we write down a complete, fully specified biochemical starting state — a defined mixture of molecules rather than an inherited cytoplasm — that is sufficient to activate a synthesized cellular genome? Formally, the goal is a construction target: identify a defined molecular boot state that switches a chemically synthesized genome into a functioning cellular program.
status: Synthetic-genome control after transplantation into an existing cell was achieved in 2010; a defined minimal molecular boot state was not established. Key work: Gibson et al. (2010), [Creation of a bacterial cell controlled by a chemically synthesized genome](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1190719).
solved_when: A synthesized genome is activated from a starting state in which every molecular component is specified, with no reliance on inherited cytoplasmic organization; the boot state and activation are demonstrated experimentally.
why: It would cleanly separate genome design from inherited cytoplasmic organization, making genome function a consequence of sequence plus a defined molecular context rather than of an inherited cell.
key_works: Gibson et al. (2010), [Creation of a bacterial cell controlled by a chemically synthesized genome](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1190719).

title: Prospective viability prediction for synonymous genome rewrites
open: Can we predict, before building a recoded genome, how genome-wide synonymous replacements will affect fitness, RNA structure, expression, overlapping functions, and environmental responses?
status: Multi-omics-guided debugging in 2026 revealed extensive molecular and condition-dependent effects in heavily recoded genomes, per Nyerges et al. (2026), [Probing the limits of genetic recoding using multi-omics-guided evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74300-9).
solved_when: A predictive framework exists that forecasts genome-wide synonymous replacement effects on fitness, RNA structure, expression, overlapping functions, and environmental responses prospectively, prior to genome construction.
why: It would enable reliable large-scale sequence rewriting, so heavily recoded genomes could be designed with confidence rather than debugged after construction.
key_works: Nyerges et al. (2026), [Probing the limits of genetic recoding using multi-omics-guided evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74300-9).

title: Conditional lower bounds on genetic-code compression
open: Is there a fundamental floor on how few codons a viable genetic code can use, given fixed requirements for decoding accuracy, organism growth, and translational fidelity — or can a smaller, functional code actually be built? Formally: prove a minimum codon count under specified decoding, growth, and fidelity constraints, or construct a smaller viable code.
status: A complete four-megabase E. coli genome using 57 codons, including 55 sense codons, was reported in 2025; optimality remains unproved. Key work: Robertson et al. (2025), [Escherichia coli with a 57-codon genetic code](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.ady4368).
solved_when: Either a rigorous lower bound on the codon count is proved under stated decoding, growth, and fidelity constraints, or a viable organism with a genetic code using fewer than 57 codons (fewer than 55 sense codons) is constructed.
why: It fixes the physical and informational limits of translation architectures, telling synthetic biologists whether the current design frontier is near optimal or far from it.
key_works: Robertson et al. (2025), [Escherichia coli with a 57-codon genetic code](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.ady4368).

title: Hidden translated sequences in recoded genomes
open: Are there translated sequences — including in alternative reading frames — that still use codons a synthetic genome was designed to eliminate, and do any of them carry condition-specific functions? A satisfying answer would identify such physiologically relevant sequences and characterize when they matter.
status: Annotation-related defects and unassigned codons were detected in extensively recoded genomes in 2026, per Nyerges et al. (2026), [Probing the limits of genetic recoding using multi-omics-guided evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74300-9).
solved_when: The translated sequences retaining supposedly removed codons, including alternative-frame cases and any condition-specific functions, are identified in extensively recoded genomes.
why: Incomplete annotation leaves hidden translations that can sabotage recoding completeness; identifying them prevents incompletely recoded genomes.
key_works: Nyerges et al. (2026), [Probing the limits of genetic recoding using multi-omics-guided evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74300-9).

title: Physiological termination with a compressed stop code
open: Can a synthetic organism whose genetic code has been compressed to fewer stop codons — with the associated termination factors altered accordingly — still terminate translation accurately, recycle ribosomes properly, and mount normal stress responses across the environments it encounters? More precisely, does broad physiological equivalence hold after stop-codon reduction, and can it be ported beyond the engineered chassis?
status: An organism with one stop codon was engineered in 2025 (Grome et al. (2025), [Engineering a genomically recoded organism with one stop codon](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08501-x)); broad physiological equivalence and portability remain open.
solved_when: A compressed-stop-code organism is shown to retain accurate termination, recycling, and stress responses at levels matching its unmodified counterpart across diverse environmental conditions, with the system demonstrated to be portable.
why: It would establish that genetic code compression is compatible with robust cellular function, making stop-code compression a practical engineering tool rather than a fitness liability.
key_works: Grome et al. (2025), [Engineering a genomically recoded organism with one stop codon](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08501-x).

title: High-fidelity multiplex amino-acid incorporation
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Can we incorporate several distinct noncanonical amino acids into arbitrary proteins at the same time, with measured fidelity at each insertion site, useful yields, and minimal disruption of the host proteome? More sharply, this asks for a sequence-general platform — not a special case — where multiple distinct noncanonical residues are installed positionally faithfully and the engineered translation machinery tolerates them broadly.
status: Up to five distinct noncanonical amino acids were incorporated into a mammalian protein in 2026 (Fang et al. (2026), [Recoding multiple rare codons enables the simultaneous incorporation of up to five distinct noncanonical amino acids](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-026-02084-y)); sequence-general performance remains open.
solved_when: A method exists that incorporates several distinct noncanonical amino acids into arbitrary target proteins with experimentally measured positional fidelity at each site, useful yields, and minimal host-proteome disruption.
why: It unlocks chemically richer proteins and multifunctional biologics — molecules with multiple orthogonal chemical handles and functions that natural translation cannot produce.
key_works: Fang et al. (2026), [Recoding multiple rare codons enables the simultaneous incorporation of up to five distinct noncanonical amino acids](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-026-02084-y).

title: Predictable quadruplet decoding in long proteins
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Can we predict, from sequence context alone, how efficiently a quadruplet codon will be decoded and how likely frameshifting becomes in long proteins with many such sites? More formally, is there a model that forecasts quadruplet decoding efficiency and frameshift risk across sequence contexts and repeated sites in long proteins?
status: Work published in 2024/2025 reduced context dependence and identified 12 mutually orthogonal tRNA–synthetase pairs; general transfer to long proteins remains unresolved. Key work: Costello et al. (2024/2025), [Efficient genetic code expansion without host genome modifications](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-024-02385-y).
solved_when: A predictive account of quadruplet decoding efficiency and frameshift risk exists that holds across sequence contexts and repeated sites in long proteins, and generalizes beyond the specific contexts studied in 2024/2025 work.
why: It would expand the coding capacity of engineered organisms without unpredictable synchronization errors — the current obstacle to reliably building long noncanonical proteins.
key_works: Costello et al. (2024/2025), [Efficient genetic code expansion without host genome modifications](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-024-02385-y).

title: Cell-state-robust modified-codon decoding
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Can modified-base codons be made to act only on their intended transcripts, while keeping their decoding specificity intact across different cell types, stress conditions, and changes in endogenous RNA modifications? In formal terms, this asks for a decoding architecture in which codon meaning is conditioned on transcript identity and robust to cellular context.
status: Programmable pseudouridine-dependent decoding and mutually orthogonal pairs were demonstrated in mammalian cells in 2025; see Liu et al. (2025), [RNA codon expansion via programmable pseudouridine editing and decoding](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09165-x).
solved_when: Modified-base codons are decoded exclusively in their intended transcripts, and decoding specificity is preserved across cell types, stresses, and endogenous modification changes.
why: It would make transcript-selective code expansion reliable, so engineered genetic codes can be deployed without off-target translation or context-dependent failure.
key_works: Liu et al. (2025), [RNA codon expansion via programmable pseudouridine editing and decoding](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09165-x).

title: Predicting synthetase substrate confusion
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Can we predict which chemically similar substrates an aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase will accept when several of them coexist at physiological concentrations? More precisely, can we compute a synthetase's discrimination profile — its catalytic selectivity across competing substrates — accurately enough to anticipate cross-charging in an expanded genetic code?
status: A 2025 simulation–experiment comparison, Lee and Choi (2025), [Predicting the polyspecificity of aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase for non-canonical amino acids using molecular dynamics simulation and MM/PBSA](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0316907), covered a limited substrate panel; broadly calibrated catalytic-selectivity prediction remains open.
solved_when: A broadly calibrated predictor of catalytic selectivity is available that matches experimental discrimination measurements across a wide range of coexisting substrates, going beyond the limited substrate panel of the 2025 simulation–experiment comparison.
why: It prevents unintended monomer incorporation in expanded codes, which is what silently corrupts an orthogonal translation system once multiple non-canonical substrates are present at once.
key_works: Lee and Choi (2025), [Predicting the polyspecificity of aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase for non-canonical amino acids using molecular dynamics simulation and MM/PBSA](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0316907).

title: Long sequence-defined noncanonical backbone synthesis
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Can we manufacture long sequence-defined polymers whose backbone incorporates specified noncanonical units at consecutive positions, with verified sequence fidelity and practical isolated yield? In formal terms, this asks for a general synthesis platform — not a single demonstrated motif — placing arbitrary noncanonical backbone units at arbitrary consecutive positions along a long chain.
status: Ribosome-generated cyclic backbone motifs were demonstrated in 2025 (Lee et al. (2025), [Expanded ribosomal synthesis of non-standard cyclic backbones in vitro](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60126-4)), but arbitrary long-sequence synthesis remains beyond individual chemistry demonstrations.
solved_when: A platform produces long polymers with specified noncanonical backbone units at consecutive positions, with verified fidelity of the installed sequence and practical isolated yield of the isolated product.
why: Success extends biological manufacturing into polymer classes beyond natural biopolymers, opening new sequence-defined macromolecular materials.
key_works: Lee et al. (2025), [Expanded ribosomal synthesis of non-standard cyclic backbones in vitro](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60126-4).

title: General consecutive D-amino-acid incorporation in vitro
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Can a cell-free translation system be engineered to produce peptides containing arbitrary contiguous runs of bulky D-amino acids with predictable yield and minimal sequence bias?
status: Consecutive incorporation of nine bulky D-amino-acid types was demonstrated with an alternative ribosome in 2026 — the Alteromonas macleodii ribosome (Katoh et al. (2026), [The Alteromonas macleodii ribosome enables consecutive incorporation of bulky D-amino acids into peptides](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkag341)) — but general sequence efficiency remains open.
solved_when: Finite peptides with any desired contiguous combination of bulky D-amino acids can be synthesized in vitro at predictable yield and with low sequence bias across sequences.
why: It expands access to stable, protease-resistant peptide scaffolds for medicinal chemistry, including protease-resistant peptide design.
key_works: Katoh et al. (2026), [The Alteromonas macleodii ribosome enables consecutive incorporation of bulky D-amino acids into peptides](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkag341).

title: Affordable multiplex noncanonical amino-acid supply
subfield: Orthogonal translation and expanded polymer chemistry
open: Can a single, affordable process synthesize a diverse set of noncanonical amino acids at once and accurately incorporate each of them into proteins? Formally, this asks for simultaneous multi-monomer supply and incorporation with complete product-normalized cost accounting.
status: A 2025 platform synthesized 40 aromatic amino acids and incorporated 19 (Zhang et al. (2025), [A robust platform streamlining aromatic noncanonical amino acid biosynthesis and genetic code expansion in Escherichia coli](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63679-6)); broader chemistries and simultaneous production remain unfinished.
solved_when: Several chemically diverse noncanonical amino acids are produced economically in parallel and simultaneously incorporated with fidelity, with complete product-normalized costs reported — going beyond the current platform's 40 synthesized aromatic amino acids, of which 19 were incorporated.
why: It removes precursor cost and availability bottlenecks that currently limit expanded-polymer chemistry.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2025), [A robust platform streamlining aromatic noncanonical amino acid biosynthesis and genetic code expansion in Escherichia coli](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63679-6).

title: Long-read, quantitative XNA sequencing
open: Can we sequence long stretches of chemically diverse xeno-nucleic acids (XNAs) directly and quantitatively, with substitution, insertion, and deletion errors that are calibrated rather than merely characterized, while retaining information about chemical modifications along the strand?
status: An XNA-adapted Sanger method read strands up to 50 bases in 2026 (Wang et al. (2026), [Sanger Sequencing of Xeno-Nucleic Acid](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202516617)); long reads and broad quantitative profiling remain open.
solved_when: A sequencing method produces long reads of chemically diverse XNAs — substantially beyond the demonstrated 50 bases — with calibrated substitution, insertion, and deletion error rates and preservation of modification information across broad profiling contexts.
why: It would make it possible to measure and evolve alternative genetic polymers, turning XNA from a synthesis target into a system that can be read and iterated on quantitatively.
key_works: Wang et al. (2026), [Sanger Sequencing of Xeno-Nucleic Acid](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202516617).

title: High-fidelity long-XNA copying at physiological conditions
open: Can long XNA templates be copied faithfully under physiologically compatible conditions, with sequence-dependent error rates low enough that information survives repeated rounds of copying?
status: Modified-nucleotide copying at 37°C advanced in 2026 via Zhang et al. (2026), [Single-residue engineering of Klenow fragment enables broad acceptance of chemically modified nucleotides](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkag697), but short-template performance does not establish uniform accuracy across long sequences.
solved_when: Long XNA templates are copied at physiological conditions (e.g., 37°C) with sequence-dependent error rates sufficiently low for repeated information retention, demonstrated uniformly across long sequences rather than only short templates.
why: It would establish sustained heredity for alternative genetic polymers, a prerequisite for any stable XNA-based genetic system.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2026), [Single-residue engineering of Klenow fragment enables broad acceptance of chemically modified nucleotides](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkag697).

title: DNA-independent cell-free XNA heredity
open: Can a cell-free system sustain heredity and selection in an XNA genetic polymer without passing through a DNA intermediate at any stage? A successful demonstration would show XNA-templated XNA copying driving repeated cycles of replication and selection, with the information capacity of the system actually measured.
status: DNA-mediated XNA evolution was established in 2012 by Pinheiro et al. (2012), [Synthetic genetic polymers capable of heredity and evolution](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1217622), and XNA-templated copying advanced in 2026 with Zhang et al. (2026), [Klenow-fragment engineering](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkag697); sustained DNA-independent evolution remains open.
solved_when: XNA information transfer and selection are sustained entirely DNA-independently in a cell-free setup, over repeated cycles, with a quantitative measurement of the information capacity of the XNA system reported.
why: It directly tests whether genetic polymers with non-natural backbones can support heredity on their own, informing both xenobiology and origins-of-life scenarios built on alternative informational polymers.
key_works: Pinheiro et al. (2012), [Synthetic genetic polymers capable of heredity and evolution](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1217622); Zhang et al. (2026), [Klenow-fragment engineering](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkag697).

title: Quantitative catalytic limits of XNA
open: Do synthetic genetic polymers (XNA) have catalytic abilities that differ in kind or degree from those of DNA and RNA, and can we map which XNA reaction classes are efficiently accessible? Formally, this asks for a quantitative characterization of the catalytic repertoires accessible to alternative genetic chemistries.
status: Multiple XNA chemistries yielded cleavage and ligation catalysts in 2015; their broader catalytic landscape remains unmapped. Key work: Taylor et al. (2015), [Catalysts from synthetic genetic polymers](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13982).
solved_when: A map of efficiently accessible XNA catalytic reaction classes exists, together with a determination — quantitative where possible — of whether these repertoires differ systematically from those of DNA and RNA.
why: It establishes the functional possibilities and limitations of alternative polymers, delimiting what xenobiological systems can in principle catalyze.
key_works: Taylor et al. (2015), [Catalysts from synthetic genetic polymers](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13982).

title: Predicting higher-order structures in expanded alphabets
open: Can we predict how long nucleic acids built from more than four nucleotide letters fold, mispair, and form functional structures? In formal terms, the goal is a theory capable of predicting folding, mispairing, and functional structures of long-sequence expanded-alphabet nucleic acids.
status: Eight-letter hachimoji duplex thermodynamics and functional transcription were demonstrated in 2019 (Hoshika et al. (2019), [Hachimoji DNA and RNA: A genetic system with eight building blocks](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0971)); general long-sequence folding remains open.
solved_when: A predictive theory exists for folding, mispairing, and functional structures of long nucleic acids containing more than four nucleotide letters, beyond simple duplexes.
why: It would make expanded alphabets designable, so that sequences with more than four letters can be engineered for intended structures and functions rather than only simple duplex pairing.
key_works: Hoshika et al. (2019), [Hachimoji DNA and RNA: A genetic system with eight building blocks](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0971).

title: Context-independent retention of unnatural base pairs
open: Can we predict, for an unnatural base pair, how well it will be retained as the surrounding DNA sequence varies and as the pair is copied again and again — and can we do so while cleanly separating the contributions of the polymerase, the chemistry of the base pair itself, and the cellular environment? In formal terms, this asks for a predictive, context-independent account of retention rates with decomposed error sources.
status: Cellular maintenance of an unnatural base pair was demonstrated in 2014 and information retrieval from it in 2017; sequence-general reliability remains a broader target. Key work: Malyshev et al. (2014), [A semi-synthetic organism with an expanded genetic alphabet](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13314).
solved_when: A demonstrated ability to predict unnatural-base-pair retention across arbitrary sequence contexts and over repeated rounds of copying, with polymerase, chemical, and cellular error sources separately quantified.
why: It would make expanded genetic information dependable rather than merely possible, allowing synthetic organisms to stably store and retrieve added bases without context-specific failures.
key_works: Malyshev et al. (2014), [A semi-synthetic organism with an expanded genetic alphabet](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature13314).

title: Economical manufacture of mirror-image binding proteins
open: Can mirror-image (D-protein) binding proteins be manufactured reproducibly at a useful scale, at costs low enough for routine use? Concretely, this means driving down the combined synthesis, purification, and folding costs of finite D-protein binders across diverse target sequences.
status: A functional mirror-image monobody was chemically synthesized in 2024 (Hayashi et al. (2024), [Generating a mirror-image monobody targeting MCP-1 via TRAP display and chemical protein synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54902-x)), but economical production across diverse sequences remains open.
solved_when: Finite D-protein binders can be produced reproducibly at useful scale, with synthesis, purification, and folding costs reduced relative to current chemical synthesis practice, and the approach shown to work across diverse sequences rather than a single example.
why: Cheap D-protein production would make unusually stable binding reagents and therapeutic candidates widely accessible, since mirror-image proteins resist natural proteolytic degradation.
key_works: Hayashi et al. (2024), [Generating a mirror-image monobody targeting MCP-1 via TRAP display and chemical protein synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54902-x).

title: Predictive disposition of finite mirror-image proteins
open: Can we build predictive, validated models of the tissue distribution, clearance, accumulation, and immune interactions of finite mirror-image proteins in living systems? That is, quantitative pharmacokinetic and disposition models for D-protein reagents, sufficient to forecast their behavior from molecular properties rather than empirical observation alone.
status: Selected binding, stability, and biological responses of mirror-image proteins were demonstrated in 2024, including the TRAP-display and chemical-protein-synthesis generation of a mirror-image monobody targeting MCP-1 (Hayashi et al. (2024), [Generating a mirror-image monobody targeting MCP-1 via TRAP display and chemical protein synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54902-x)); however, general pharmacokinetic and long-term disposition models remain absent.
solved_when: Validated models exist that predict tissue distribution, clearance, accumulation, and immune interactions of finite mirror-image proteins, including long-term disposition, grounded in demonstrated experimental data.
why: Such models would allow informed development of persistent molecular reagents, replacing trial-and-error dosing and safety assessment with predictive design.
key_works: Hayashi et al. (2024), [Generating a mirror-image monobody targeting MCP-1 via TRAP display and chemical protein synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54902-x).

title: Predictive composition across hosts and environments
open: Can we predict how an assembled genetic circuit will behave across different host strains, media conditions, temperatures, and growth phases, with uncertainty estimates that hold up prospectively rather than after the fact? Formally, the goal is a predictive model of circuit performance under context change with calibrated prospective uncertainty.
status: Cello achieved automated circuit construction in 2016; Cello 2.0 broadened support in 2022, while retaining characterized-library and deployment constraints. Jones et al. (2022), [Genetic circuit design automation with Cello 2.0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41596-021-00675-2).
solved_when: Predictions of assembled-circuit behavior across strains, media, temperatures, and growth phases are delivered with calibrated prospective uncertainty.
why: It would make circuit reuse dependable — designs could be transferred between hosts and conditions without re-characterization.
key_works: Jones et al. (2022), [Genetic circuit design automation with Cello 2.0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41596-021-00675-2).

title: Independent allocation of multiple cellular resources
open: Can a cell be engineered so that transcription, translation, folding, and degradation capacity are each allocated independently across modules? A sharper version asks whether such multi-resource budgets can be maintained while quantitatively predicting the residual coupling that arises as different resources become the bottleneck.
status: Dynamic orthogonal-ribosome allocation reduced coupling between two co-expressed genes in 2018 (Darlington et al. (2018), [Dynamic allocation of orthogonal ribosomes facilitates uncoupling of co-expressed genes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-02898-6)); simultaneous isolation across multiple resource pools remains open.
solved_when: A system demonstrates simultaneous independent allocation across transcription, translation, folding, and degradation resource pools, with a predictive account of residual coupling between modules as bottlenecks shift.
why: Without independent allocation, one module's resource demand destabilizes the behavior of others, breaking compositionality in engineered gene circuits.
key_works: Darlington et al. (2018), [Dynamic allocation of orthogonal ribosomes facilitates uncoupling of co-expressed genes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-018-02898-6).

title: Burden feedback with specified productivity guarantees
open: Can a gene circuit maintain a specified production output and host-growth envelope even as nutrient conditions and expression demands change? Formally, this asks for burden-responsive feedback that guarantees constrained regulation across stresses rather than for a single construct.
status: Burden-responsive feedback was demonstrated in 2018 (Ceroni et al. (2018), [Burden-driven feedback control of gene expression](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4635)); cross-stress guarantees remain construct-dependent.
solved_when: A burden-driven feedback design is shown to keep both output and host growth within specified envelopes across changing nutrient and expression demands, with the guarantees stated independently of any particular construct.
why: It preserves useful production without exhausting the host, so engineered circuits stay productive rather than collapsing under their own expression load.
key_works: Ceroni et al. (2018), [Burden-driven feedback control of gene expression](https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.4635).

title: Predicting resource-induced changes of circuit state
open: When a synthetic gene circuit shares the cell's limited resources, when does the resulting feedback create or destroy stable states, oscillations, or switching thresholds — and can we predict the rare-transition probabilities between states? A formal criterion delineating which resource-coupled circuit architectures undergo such qualitative changes is the goal.
status: Resource competition was shown experimentally to redirect cascading cell-fate transitions in 2021 (Zhang et al. (2021), [Winner-takes-all resource competition redirects cascading cell fate transitions](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21125-3)), but transferable quantitative boundaries remain unresolved; related statistical-physics work on noise-driven bifurcations is a neighboring thread.
solved_when: A transferable quantitative theory gives boundaries in parameter space that predict the emergence or loss of stable states, oscillations, and switching thresholds under resource competition, including rare-transition probabilities, and these boundaries are validated beyond a single experimental setting.
why: It explains unexpected circuit behavior that appears after integration into a host cell, turning resource competition from a source of unexplained failures into a designable, predictable factor.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2021), [Winner-takes-all resource competition redirects cascading cell fate transitions](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21125-3).

title: Supercoiling-aware circuit layout
open: Can we predict transcriptional interference from gene order, orientation, spacing, and topological constraints well enough to lay out a synthetic circuit prospectively, before building it? In other words, is there a layout calculus that takes syntax and supercoiling-mediated feedback into account and outputs an arrangement predicted to behave as intended?
status: Syntax-dependent supercoiling feedback and improved compact circuits were demonstrated in 2026 by Johnstone et al. (2026), [Gene syntax defines supercoiling-mediated transcriptional feedback](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adw1925); however, a general layout calculus remains open.
solved_when: A general layout calculus exists: a method that, given a desired circuit, predicts transcriptional interference effects from gene order, orientation, spacing, and topological constraints accurately enough to guide prospective circuit layout rather than post-hoc explanation.
why: It would make sequence arrangement an explicit, engineerable design variable in synthetic gene circuits, rather than a confounding side effect.
key_works: Johnstone et al. (2026), [Gene syntax defines supercoiling-mediated transcriptional feedback](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adw1925).

title: Large orthogonal regulatory alphabets with measured limits
open: How many independently addressable regulatory channels can a host cell support before crosstalk and burden collapse the system's fidelity? Formally, determine the maximum number of orthogonal regulatory channels that can coexist at a specified error rate and burden budget, accounting for higher-order interference beyond pairwise effects.
status: Orthogonal repressor libraries have supported circuits since 2014; however, pairwise specificity does not establish collective capacity. Key work: Stanton et al. (2014), [Genomic mining of prokaryotic repressors for orthogonal logic gates](https://doi.org/10.1038/nchembio.1411).
solved_when: A measured limit is established: the maximum number of coexisting orthogonal regulatory channels at a stated error tolerance and burden budget, with higher-order interference quantified rather than extrapolated from pairwise specificity alone.
why: It defines realistic scaling limits for gene circuits, telling designers when adding another channel stops buying capacity and starts corrupting the whole system.
key_works: Stanton et al. (2014), [Genomic mining of prokaryotic repressors for orthogonal logic gates](https://doi.org/10.1038/nchembio.1411).

title: Reliable asynchronous genetic logic
open: Can we design a compilation procedure for synthetic genetic circuits that tolerates uncertain biological delays, taking explicit assumptions about input transitions and delivering bounds on transient errors? In other words, is there an analogue of asynchronous circuit synthesis that yields provable timing-robustness guarantees for logic implemented in living cells?
status: Hazard-aware genetic-circuit analysis and redesign were demonstrated in 2020; large-circuit stochastic guarantees remain open. Key work: Fontanarrosa et al. (2020), [Genetic Circuit Dynamics: Hazard and Glitch Analysis](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.0c00055).
solved_when: A method exists that, given a circuit with stated input-transition assumptions and uncertain biological delays, produces verified bounds on transient errors (glitches/hazards), demonstrated to scale beyond small circuits with stochastic guarantees.
why: Without delay-aware guarantees, genetic logic can fail nondeterministically depending on timing, so identical circuits behave differently from cell to cell or run to run; bounding transient errors makes digital genetic computation reliable enough to build on.
key_works: Fontanarrosa et al. (2020), [Genetic Circuit Dynamics: Hazard and Glitch Analysis](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.0c00055).

title: Sequence diversification without functional drift
open: Can we rewrite a genetic circuit so that no repeated DNA sequences remain, while leaving its quantitative dynamical behavior — the very dynamics it was built to produce — intact and measurably reducing recombination- and mutation-driven failures?
status: Thousands of nonrepetitive parts were designed automatically in 2020, per Hossain et al. (2020), [Automated design of thousands of nonrepetitive parts for engineering stable genetic systems](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0584-2); however, whole-circuit equivalence and lifetime gains remain broader, untested challenges.
solved_when: A method demonstrably removes repeated sequences from a circuit, preserves quantitative dynamics equivalent to the original, and reduces measured recombination and mutation failures relative to the unrewritten circuit.
why: Sequence repetition inside a circuit is a source of instability, so eliminating it improves long-term stability without sacrificing the intended behavior of the system.
key_works: Hossain et al. (2020), [Automated design of thousands of nonrepetitive parts for engineering stable genetic systems](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0584-2).

title: Prospective prediction of circuit evolutionary lifetime
open: Can we predict, before a circuit is ever built or run, how long it will persist and function in a given host — that is, its time-to-failure distribution — from its sequence, host background, expression levels, and cultivation history alone? A complete answer would furnish such predictions prospectively, across designs, and confirm them experimentally.
status: A 2025 computational study (Byrom and Darlington (2025), [Genetic controllers for enhancing the evolutionary longevity of synthetic gene circuits in bacteria](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63627-4)) predicted over threefold half-life gains for some controllers; cross-design experimental lifetime prediction remains open.
solved_when: Predicted time-to-failure distributions for gene circuits, derived from sequence, host, expression, and cultivation history, are validated prospectively in experiments across different circuit designs.
why: It turns evolutionary stability from an afterthought into a measurable design specification that can be engineered for upfront.
key_works: Byrom and Darlington (2025), [Genetic controllers for enhancing the evolutionary longevity of synthetic gene circuits in bacteria](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63627-4).

title: Quantitative cotranscriptional RNA design
open: Can we predict the complete response curve of an RNA regulator — its quantitative input–output behavior — directly from its sequence, folding kinetics, ligand association, and intracellular conditions? In formal terms, this asks for a transferable, quantitative model mapping sequence and cellular context to regulator response.
status: General riboswitch-sensitivity tuning mechanisms were identified in 2025 by Bushhouse, Fu, and Lucks (2025), [RNA folding kinetics control riboswitch sensitivity in vivo](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-55601-3); intracellular states and transferable quantitative prediction remain uncertain.
solved_when: A method exists that quantitatively predicts complete RNA-regulator response curves from sequence, folding kinetics, ligand association, and intracellular conditions, and the predictions transfer across contexts.
why: It would make RNA regulation predictable from design, turning riboswitch and regulator engineering from trial-and-error into rational design.
key_works: Bushhouse, Fu, and Lucks (2025), [RNA folding kinetics control riboswitch sensitivity in vivo](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-55601-3).

title: Deep composable RNA logic
open: Can RNA-based computational cascades be chained through many processing stages while preserving signal strength, keeping leakage low, and maintaining predictable timing — and can we characterize how deep and how fan-out-capable such cascades can be? Formally, the goal is to establish quantitative depth and fan-out limits for composable RNA logic stages.
status: A 12-input ribocomputing device was demonstrated in Green et al. (2017), [Complex cellular logic computation using ribocomputing devices](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature23271); however, wide input integration does not establish deep composability.
solved_when: A multi-stage RNA-processing cascade is demonstrated whose signal, leakage, and timing remain within specified bounds across many stages, together with an analysis establishing the depth and fan-out limits of such composability.
why: It would let complex RNA programs be assembled reliably from reusable stages, moving RNA computation from single wide-input devices toward true layered circuit design.
key_works: Green et al. (2017), [Complex cellular logic computation using ribocomputing devices](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature23271).

title: Scalable orthogonal RNA trans-splicing
open: Can RNA trans-splicing regulators be scaled to many simultaneous, orthogonal pairs in a living cell, with reliable prediction of mis-splicing, leakage, and stoichiometry across diverse transcript contexts? Formally, the goal is an engineering framework that expands the number of concurrently operating orthogonal trans-splicing regulators while quantitatively forecasting crosstalk and expression ratios in any given transcript setting.
status: SENTRs supported up to six-input logic in 2025 (Gao et al. (2025), [Programmable trans-splicing riboregulators for complex cellular logic computation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-024-01781-4)); higher-dimensional interference and portability remain open.
solved_when: A scalable set of orthogonal trans-splicing regulators is demonstrated that exceeds the six-input logic level and whose mis-splicing, leakage, and stoichiometry can be predicted across transcript contexts.
why: It expands programmable processing of cellular RNAs, enabling more complex RNA-level computation and regulation in cells.
key_works: Gao et al. (2025), [Programmable trans-splicing riboregulators for complex cellular logic computation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-024-01781-4).

title: Interchangeable RNA-trigger-to-effector transduction
open: Can we build a transduction architecture in which any intended RNA input can be converted into an activated noncoding-RNA output, with specificity, amplification, and leakage that are predictable across arbitrary input–output combinations?
status: UNBAR demonstrated several effector classes in January 2026; universal interchangeability and large multi-device operation remain open. Key work: Lim et al. (2026), [A programmable ribozyme for RNA signal transduction](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-68175-5).
solved_when: A platform demonstrates universal interchangeability of RNA-trigger-to-effector pairings and reliable operation of large multi-device circuits, with quantitatively predictable specificity, amplification, and leakage across input–output combinations.
why: It would connect RNA sensing directly to diverse cellular actions, letting detection of arbitrary RNA signals drive programmable downstream responses rather than a fixed, hard-wired effector.
key_works: Lim et al. (2026), [A programmable ribozyme for RNA signal transduction](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-68175-5).

title: General discovery of useful small-molecule RNA sensors
open: Can we build a general method that discovers selective intracellular RNA sensors for arbitrary specified small molecules? Formally, the goal is to produce sensors for specified diverse ligands with a known success rate and a useful response range.
status: DRIVER automated multiplexed biosensor evolution was demonstrated in 2021 (Townshend et al. (2021), [A multiplexed, automated evolution pipeline enables scalable discovery and characterization of biosensors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21716-0)), but broad ligand coverage with prospective guarantees remains unresolved.
solved_when: A method exists that yields selective intracellular RNA sensors for a specified diverse set of ligands, with a measured success rate and sensors operating in a useful response range.
why: It expands the range of chemical inputs that living circuits can sense and act on.
key_works: Townshend et al. (2021), [A multiplexed, automated evolution pipeline enables scalable discovery and characterization of biosensors](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-21716-0).

title: RNA generative design outside the training distribution
open: Can we design functional RNA regulators for structural families, sensing regimes, and cellular contexts that lie outside what current generative models were trained on, with calibrated uncertainty over their predicted behavior and prospective experimental validation? Formally, the goal is generative design that reliably mechanistically extrapolates beyond the training distribution rather than interpolating among familiar sequences.
status: SANDSTORM/GARDN generated functional candidates from relatively small datasets in 2025, per Riley et al. (2025), [Generative and predictive neural networks for the design of functional RNA molecules](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59389-8), but reliable mechanistic extrapolation remains open.
solved_when: A generative design method produces functional RNA regulators for new structural families, sensing regimes, and cellular contexts, with calibrated uncertainty estimates on its predictions, and those designs are validated prospectively in experiments.
why: It extends RNA design beyond interpolation among familiar sequences, enabling regulation in settings where no similar training data exists.
key_works: Riley et al. (2025), [Generative and predictive neural networks for the design of functional RNA molecules](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59389-8).

title: Reusable deep proteolytic circuits
open: Can a multistage proteolytic circuit be made to operate repeatedly, processing changing inputs over many cycles? Formally, this requires sustained resettable operation in which circuit components are replenished and cleavage products from earlier cycles do not interfere with subsequent ones.
status: Composable regulated-protease circuits were demonstrated in 2018 (Gao et al. (2018), [Programmable protein circuits in living cells](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat5062)); sustained resettable operation introduces additional constraints beyond that demonstration.
solved_when: A multistage protease circuit demonstrates repeated, resettable processing of changing inputs with component replenishment and no cross-cycle interference from cleavage products.
why: It converts one-time cleavage logic into reusable computation, moving protein circuits from single-use devices toward genuinely reusable signal processors.
key_works: Gao et al. (2018), [Programmable protein circuits in living cells](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat5062).

title: Predictably wired phosphorylation networks
open: Can phosphorylation-based signaling modules be connected into larger synthetic networks that still behave as designed, with their transfer functions and timing preserved even when enzymes are shared between modules, reactions saturate, and endogenous interactions interfere?
status: Modular synthetic phosphorylation networks were established in human cells in 2025 by Yang et al. (2025), [Engineering synthetic phosphorylation signaling networks in human cells](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adm8485); extensive scaling and portability remain open.
solved_when: Coupled phosphorylation modules operate in cells with their designed transfer functions and dynamics retained despite shared enzymes, saturation, and endogenous crosstalk; scaling beyond initial demonstrations and portability across settings would mark fuller success.
why: It would enable rapid analog and dynamic computation in living cells, moving synthetic biology toward predictable, circuit-like signal processing.
key_works: Yang et al. (2025), [Engineering synthetic phosphorylation signaling networks in human cells](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adm8485).

title: Specified allosteric response functions
open: Can we design protein assemblies whose signaling response — cooperativity, thresholds, hysteresis, and switching kinetics — is programmed to arbitrary, pre-specified quantitative targets? More precisely, can such prescribed response functions be engineered while preserving the output activity of the assembly?
status: Allosterically switchable assemblies were designed in 2024 — Pillai et al. (2024), [De novo design of allosterically switchable protein assemblies](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07813-2) — but arbitrary quantitative response programming remains unestablished.
solved_when: A protein assembly is designed whose cooperativity, thresholds, hysteresis, and switching kinetics match pre-specified quantitative values, with output activity preserved.
why: It would make protein behavior programmable beyond binding affinity, turning assemblies into engineered signal-processing components.
key_works: Pillai et al. (2024), [De novo design of allosterically switchable protein assemblies](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07813-2).

title: Integral control with variable dilution and resource constraints
open: Can a synthetic integral controller for a living cell maintain a specified tracking error and stability while growth dilution, resource availability, and actuator saturation all vary at once? Formally, the goal is a controller design with provable guarantees on tracking error and closed-loop stability under simultaneous dilution, resource, and saturation constraints.
status: Sensor-based antithetic control improved speed and noise attenuation experimentally in 2026 (Filo et al. (2026), [Engineering sensor-based antithetic integral controllers for enhanced dynamic performance and noise attenuation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2025.101512)), but combined physiological guarantees — tracking and stability under dilution, resource, and saturation effects together — remain open.
solved_when: A controller design is achieved that meets the specified tracking error and stability targets under simultaneous growth dilution, resource changes, and actuator saturation, with the guarantees stated and verified.
why: It would make cellular regulation robust outside narrowly tuned conditions, where current controllers fail once growth or resources shift.
key_works: Filo et al. (2026), [Engineering sensor-based antithetic integral controllers for enhanced dynamic performance and noise attenuation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2025.101512).

title: Robust control of entire single-cell distributions
open: Can a controller keep the entire output distribution of a stochastic biomolecular network — including rare tail probabilities and temporal correlations — at specified targets while reaction rates and environmental conditions drift? Formally, this asks for robust full-distribution control, not merely of the mean and noise.
status: Theory and simulations of simultaneous mean and noise adaptation appeared in 2025/2026, notably Lim et al. (2026), "Toward single-cell control: noise-robust perfect adaptation in biomolecular systems" (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67736-y); full-distribution experimental control remains broader than current results.
solved_when: A scheme exists (analytically and/or experimentally demonstrated) that maintains prescribed output distributions, rare tails, and temporal correlations under perturbed reaction rates and changing environments.
why: It would enable control of clinically and industrially important rare-cell behavior, which mean-level regulation cannot reach.
key_works: Lim et al. (2026), [Toward single-cell control: noise-robust perfect adaptation in biomolecular systems](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67736-y).

title: Attainable joint limits on control precision, speed, and cost
open: What are the ultimate physical limits on how precisely, how quickly, and how cheaply a biological control system can operate — and can we build systems that approach those limits? Formally, the goal is to derive tight joint bounds linking noise, response speed, adaptation accuracy, and resource expenditure, and to construct systems approaching them.
status: Molecular noise-suppression bounds date to Lestas, Vinnicombe, and Paulsson (2010), [Fundamental limits on the suppression of molecular fluctuations](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09333); subsequent trade-off results remain assumption-dependent.
solved_when: Tight joint bounds on noise suppression, response speed, adaptation accuracy, and resource expenditure are derived, together with constructions of systems approaching those bounds.
why: A solution separates engineering deficiencies from genuine physical limitations, telling us when a control system fails because it was built poorly and when no better system is physically possible.
key_works: Lestas, Vinnicombe, and Paulsson (2010), [Fundamental limits on the suppression of molecular fluctuations](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature09333).

title: Experimentally useful observability and controllability tests
open: Do the noisy sensors and constrained inputs actually available in a synthetic biology experiment allow practical state inference and control of a circuit? More formally, develop observability and controllability tests that remain meaningful under realistic noise, input constraints, and model uncertainty.
status: Structural analyses of selected nonlinear synthetic circuits appeared in 2024–2025, notably Pardo et al. (2024), [Analysing control-theoretic properties of nonlinear synthetic biology circuits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05450), arXiv:2411.05450; finite-data and model-uncertainty guarantees remain open.
solved_when: Checkable tests exist that certify — or refute — practical observability and controllability from finite, noisy data under input constraints and model uncertainty, replacing purely structural analyses with finite-data guarantees.
why: Such tests tell the experimenter when inference and control are possible with what is on the bench, and identify when additional sensors or actuators must be added.
key_works: Pardo et al. (2024), [Analysing control-theoretic properties of nonlinear synthetic biology circuits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.05450), arXiv:2411.05450.

title: Single-cell control without measurement distortion
open: Can we control fast intracellular dynamics when the act of measuring the cell — reporter maturation, delay, phototoxicity, and sensing burden — distorts the very signal being controlled? In formal terms, this asks for a control scheme that achieves regulation of the biological quantity of interest despite measurement back-action rather than regulation of a proxy readout.
status: Deep predictive control reached thousands of individual cells in 2024; high-bandwidth control of nonproxy outputs remains open. Key work: Lugagne, Blassick, and Dunlop (2024), [Deep model predictive control of gene expression in thousands of single cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46361-1). Related ideas from control theory include delayed observers and measurement back-action.
solved_when: A control method is demonstrated that actuates fast intracellular dynamics at high bandwidth on a nonproxy output, explicitly compensating for reporter maturation, delay, phototoxicity, and sensing burden, so that the controlled variable is the biological quantity of interest rather than the measured reporter signal.
why: Without this, closed-loop control tuned on a distorted readout can diverge from the biologist's actual target; solving it makes measured control correspond to the biological quantity of interest.
key_works: Lugagne, Blassick, and Dunlop (2024), [Deep model predictive control of gene expression in thousands of single cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46361-1).

title: Verified circuit guarantees despite model discrepancy
open: Can a designed genetic circuit be certified for safe, reliable behavior even when its mathematical model is only an approximation of the living cell it runs in? Formally, produce probabilistic guarantees that remain valid under parameter uncertainty, unmodeled host interactions, and measured model discrepancy between model and implementation.
status: Stochastic hazard verification was demonstrated with iBioSim and STAMINA in 2021 (Buecherl et al. (2021), [Stochastic Hazard Analysis of Genetic Circuits in iBioSim and STAMINA](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.1c00159)); transferring those guarantees to uncertain living implementations remains open.
solved_when: A method exists that yields probabilistic safety/reliability guarantees for a genetic circuit that provably account for parameter uncertainty, unmodeled host interactions, and measured model discrepancy, with the guarantees holding for the actual living implementation rather than only the nominal model.
why: It closes the gap between formal verification and actual biological reliability: today's verified guarantees apply to models, so they do not yet certify real living circuits.
key_works: Buecherl et al. (2021), [Stochastic Hazard Analysis of Genetic Circuits in iBioSim and STAMINA](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.1c00159).

title: Synthetic signaling near measured information limits
open: Can we engineer synthetic cellular signaling systems that operate close to the information-transmission limits already measured for natural biochemical motifs, while respecting realistic constraints on energy, timing, and molecular copy numbers? In other words, can experimental attainment of these intrinsic limits be demonstrated with realistic dynamic inputs?
status: Intrinsic limits of information transmission in biochemical signaling motifs were analyzed in 2018 by Suderman and Deeds (2018), [Intrinsic limits of information transmission in biochemical signalling motifs](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6227803/); experimental attainment of these limits with realistic dynamic inputs remains open.
solved_when: A synthetic signaling system is experimentally shown to approach the previously established intrinsic information-transmission capacity of a biochemical motif under the specified energy, timing, and molecular-number constraints, using realistic dynamic inputs.
why: It establishes how efficiently cells can actually sense and communicate, showing which physical limits are achievable in engineered biological circuits rather than merely theoretical.
key_works: Suderman and Deeds (2018), [Intrinsic limits of information transmission in biochemical signalling motifs](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6227803/).

title: Robustly tunable synthetic Turing patterns
subfield: Spatial computation and programmed multicellular organization
open: Can we build a synthetic reaction–diffusion system whose spatial patterning can be tuned independently along several axes at once — setting wavelength, contrast, and onset time separately — while the underlying Turing mechanism remains verified across all those conditions?
status: A three-node circuit produced stationary periodic patterns in bacterial colonies in 2024 (Tica et al. (2024), [A three-node Turing gene circuit forms periodic spatial patterns in bacteria](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2024.11.002)); robust multiparameter control remains open.
solved_when: A synthetic circuit is experimentally shown to tune wavelength, contrast, and onset time independently, with the reaction–diffusion mechanism verified to persist across the varied conditions.
why: It would turn self-organized biological patterning from a qualitative demonstration into a quantitatively useful engineering tool for programming multicellular organization.
key_works: Tica et al. (2024), [A three-node Turing gene circuit forms periodic spatial patterns in bacteria](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2024.11.002).

title: Size-invariant synthetic patterning
subfield: Spatial computation and programmed multicellular organization
open: Can a synthetic patterning program be made size-invariant, so that the relative sizes of the domains it specifies are preserved when the total tissue size or initial cell number changes substantially? In formal terms, the goal is a construction — a programmed cell–cell signaling scheme — whose output pattern scales proportionally rather than collapsing or drifting as system size varies.
status: Layered self-organizing structures were demonstrated in Toda et al. (2018), [Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0271), and synthetic organizer cells guiding development via spatial and biochemical instructions were reported in Yamada et al. (2025), [Synthetic organizer cells guide development via spatial and biochemical instructions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2024.11.017); however, general proportional scaling of synthetic patterns remains unresolved. Related work in developmental biology concerns morphogen-gradient scaling.
solved_when: A synthetic patterning program is demonstrated that preserves relative domain sizes under substantial changes in total tissue size or starting cell number, with the proportions of the resulting domains maintained across those size variations.
why: It would let one genetic program produce correctly proportioned patterns across a range of tissue sizes, instead of requiring retuning for each size; without it, engineered multicellular structures only work near the conditions in which they were calibrated.
key_works: Yamada et al. (2025), [Synthetic organizer cells guide development via spatial and biochemical instructions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2024.11.017); Toda et al. (2018), [Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0271).

title: Reliable restoration of specified synthetic patterns after damage
subfield: Spatial computation and programmed multicellular organization
open: Can a synthetic multicellular system reliably rebuild a chosen spatial pattern after cells are killed or displaced? The goal is an engineered construct that restores a specified organization from damage, with measured convergence behavior and quantified failure probabilities.
status: Cleaved three-layer structures were shown to self-repair in Toda et al. (2018), [Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0271); general recovery across patterns, injuries, and repeated perturbations remains open.
solved_when: A constructed system recovers a target spatial pattern after cell removal or displacement, with quantified convergence (time or rounds to restoration) and failure probabilities, ideally across patterns, injury types, and repeated perturbations.
why: It would make programmed multicellular organization fault-tolerant, so engineered tissues and spatial computations survive damage instead of needing perfect initial conditions.
key_works: Toda et al. (2018), [Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0271).

title: Predictive mechanical coupling in patterning circuits
subfield: Spatial computation and programmed multicellular organization
open: Can we predict the spatial outcome of a synthetic patterning circuit from a joint model of signaling, growth, crowding, adhesion, and mechanical boundary conditions? More formally, is there a predictive framework that couples these mechanochemical factors so that pattern geometry can be computed in advance rather than observed after the fact?
status: Density-dependent synNotch behavior and growth-mediated pattern control were demonstrated in 2024, but transferable mechanochemical rules remain open. Key work: Santorelli et al. (2024), [Control of spatio-temporal patterning via cell growth in a multicellular synthetic gene circuit](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-53078-8).
solved_when: A transferable set of mechanochemical rules or model exists that quantitatively predicts spatial patterning outcomes from signaling, growth, crowding, adhesion, and mechanical boundary conditions across contexts, not merely fits a single experiment.
why: Without such a framework, geometry and growth can silently alter the computation a circuit performs, causing patterning outcomes to deviate from design; a solution would let tissue geometry and growth be treated as predictable parts of the computation itself.
key_works: Santorelli et al. (2024), [Control of spatio-temporal patterning via cell growth in a multicellular synthetic gene circuit](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-53078-8).

title: Autonomous execution of large distributed genetic computations
subfield: Spatial computation and programmed multicellular organization
open: Can an engineered multicellular system carry out an entire distributed genetic computation from start to finish, with subpopulations communicating and coordinating, entirely without manual intervention between stages? More precisely, can a complete partitioned computation be executed autonomously across communicating populations of cells, with the cumulative error of the whole computation actually measured?
status: The state of the art is the partitioning of a 2-bit hash function across 66 communicating strains, achieved in 2024/2025 by Padmakumar et al. (2025), [Partitioning of a 2-bit hash function across 66 communicating cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-024-01730-1); this work demonstrated subcircuits and two- and three-layer communication, but not full autonomous execution.
solved_when: A full partitioned computation runs across communicating populations with no manual stage transfers, and the cumulative error of the execution is quantitatively reported.
why: Autonomy is what allows synthetic genetic computations to exceed the capacity of a single cell; without it, each additional subcircuit adds hands-on overhead that limits scaling.
key_works: Padmakumar et al. (2025), [Partitioning of a 2-bit hash function across 66 communicating cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-024-01730-1).

title: Compilation from temporal specifications to working circuits
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Can we build a compiler that turns high-level temporal specifications — pulses, delays, adaptation, and memory — into genetic circuits that actually work, with prospective guarantees on timing and expression burden before anything is built? Formally, this asks for a complete design-automation pipeline from temporal behavior specifications to feasible molecular implementations carrying a priori timing and burden guarantees.
status: Cello 2.0 formalized Boolean design and deployment in 2022 (Jones et al. (2022), [Genetic circuit design automation with Cello 2.0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41596-021-00675-2)); general experimentally validated temporal compilation remains open.
solved_when: A compilation pipeline exists that takes pulse, delay, adaptation, and memory specifications as input and produces feasible circuits with prospective timing and burden guarantees, validated experimentally in general settings.
why: It would let users specify the behavior they want rather than the molecular implementation, making temporal circuit design accessible without low-level engineering expertise.
key_works: Jones et al. (2022), [Genetic circuit design automation with Cello 2.0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41596-021-00675-2).

title: Auditable identity of complex constructs in pooled screens
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Can each observed phenotype in a pooled screen be linked to the actual complete construct that produced it, accounting for rearrangements, multiple integrations, and barcode errors?
status: CLASSIC measured over 100,000 circuit designs in 2026, but uncertain physical mixtures and complex construct states remain harder to resolve. Related work: Rai et al. (2026), [Ultra-high-throughput mapping of genetic design space](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09933-9). The problem connects to data-science questions of uncertain entity resolution and measurement error.
solved_when: A method assigns every phenotype in a pooled screen to its true complete construct, correctly handling rearrangements, multiple integrations, and barcode errors, at the scale of at least the 100,000 circuit designs measured in 2026.
why: It prevents incorrect genotype–phenotype assignments, which would otherwise corrupt the design–function maps that pooled screens exist to produce.
key_works: Rai et al. (2026), [Ultra-high-throughput mapping of genetic design space](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09933-9).

title: A cross-context benchmark for complete genetic circuits
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Do genetic-circuit design rules hold up when the same circuit is moved to a different host, genomic integration site, growth condition, or laboratory? The goal is a benchmark that measures identical circuits across these context shifts using predefined statistical transfer tests.
status: CLASSIC produced large human-cell design-space datasets in 2026 (Rai et al. (2026), [Ultra-high-throughput mapping of genetic design space](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09933-9)); systematic cross-context generalization is a separate benchmark that remains to be built, with domain-generalization benchmarks in machine learning as a related line of work.
solved_when: A cross-context benchmark exists in which identical circuits are measured across hosts, integration sites, conditions, and laboratories, with transfer tests specified in advance, and the degree of generalization is quantitatively reported.
why: It measures whether design rules travel beyond one platform; without it, circuit design knowledge may be platform-bound and unportable.
key_works: Rai et al. (2026), [Ultra-high-throughput mapping of genetic design space](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09933-9).

title: A long-duration single-cell circuit dynamics benchmark
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Can we build a benchmark dataset that simultaneously tracks individual engineered cells over long durations, capturing trajectories, lineage, perturbations, growth, and eventual failures across diverse circuit families? Formally, this asks for a harmonized record in which all of these modalities are co-measured per single cell over extended horizons, rather than in separate short experiments.
status: Large individual-cell control datasets were demonstrated in 2024 — see Lugayne, Blassick, and Dunlop (2024), [Deep model predictive control of gene expression in thousands of single cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46361-1) — but harmonized long-duration coverage of the kind described remains absent.
solved_when: A publicly documented benchmark exists that jointly records, for individual cells across diverse circuit families, their dynamics trajectories, lineage history, applied perturbations, growth, and eventual failures over long durations in a harmonized format.
why: Such data is what makes it possible to forecast drift, switching, and failure in engineered circuits, which in turn enables principled long-horizon and survival analysis of synthetic biology designs.
key_works: Lugagne, Blassick, and Dunlop (2024), [Deep model predictive control of gene expression in thousands of single cells](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-46361-1).

title: Complete reporting of failed biological designs
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Can the synthetic biology community establish complete, interoperable reporting of failed biological designs — including failed builds, null phenotypes, protocol deviations, and censoring reasons — together with incentives that make such reporting sustainable?
status: NIST (accessed 2026), [Engineering Biology](https://www.nist.gov/mml/bbd/primary-focus-areas/engineering-biology) identifies comparable reference data and DBTL integration as continuing infrastructure needs; comprehensive failure-aware datasets remain open.
solved_when: Interoperable datasets exist that record failed builds, null phenotypes, protocol deviations, and censoring reasons, sustained by reporting incentives that keep the practice viable.
why: It reduces selection bias and prevents researchers from repeating unsuccessful designs that never get published.
key_works: NIST (accessed 2026), [Engineering Biology](https://www.nist.gov/mml/bbd/primary-focus-areas/engineering-biology).

title: Honest generalization tests for biological design models
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: How can we benchmark biological design models so that their scores honestly reflect performance on genuinely new situations rather than memorized or correlated data? Concretely, this means separating related sequences, batches, architectures, and deployment contexts in benchmark splits, and requiring prospective uncertainty calibration as part of the evaluation.
status: Strong RNA-design models appeared by 2025 (Riley et al. (2025), [Generative and predictive neural networks for the design of functional RNA molecules](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59389-8)), but their performance under structured biological novelty remains insufficiently characterized.
solved_when: A benchmark protocol exists that enforces separation of related sequences, batches, architectures, and deployment contexts, and requires prospective uncertainty calibration; models evaluated under it have their performance characterized under structured biological novelty.
why: Without such tests, estimates of practical design capability are inflated, leading to overconfident deployment of models whose real-world biological design performance is unknown.
key_works: Riley et al. (2025), [Generative and predictive neural networks for the design of functional RNA molecules](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59389-8).

title: Joint design of circuit function and evolutionary behavior
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Can we design synthetic circuits that not only perform a specified initial function but also respond to future mutations in a specified, intended way, with those evolutionary outcomes confirmed experimentally?
status: Joint generative design of both functional and evolutionary properties was demonstrated using simulated RNA circuits in Gallup and Steel (2026), [Generative design of synthetic gene circuits for functional and evolutionary properties](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41540-026-00683-6); prospective experimental validation remains open.
solved_when: A circuit is designed with both its initial function and its specified responses to future mutations as explicit design objectives, and the predicted evolutionary behavior is validated prospectively in experiments.
why: It makes future evolution part of the design objective itself, rather than an afterthought, so engineered circuits remain useful as they evolve.
key_works: Gallup and Steel (2026), [Generative design of synthetic gene circuits for functional and evolutionary properties](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41540-026-00683-6).

title: Traceable design-to-material provenance
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Can a biofoundry maintain a complete, auditable chain of provenance linking design versions, physical samples, execution histories, measurements, and training data — and automatically detect when a sample or datum does not match the identity it is claimed to have? In other words, can digital–physical provenance be kept consistent end-to-end across the design-to-material workflow rather than reconstructed after the fact?
status: SBOL 3.1.0 standardized design exchange in 2023 (Buecherl et al. (2023), [Synthetic biology open language (SBOL) version 3.1.0](https://doi.org/10.1515/jib-2022-0058)), but complete maintained digital–physical provenance remains an integration problem. Related work exists in scientific computing on data lineage and uncertain digital twins.
solved_when: An integrated system maintains auditable links among design versions, physical samples, execution histories, measurements, and training data, and successfully detects identity mismatches between them; no further quantitative budget is specified.
why: Without it, biological results cannot be reliably reproduced or audited, since there is no trustworthy way to verify which design or sample a given measurement actually came from.
key_works: Buecherl et al. (2023), [Synthetic biology open language (SBOL) version 3.1.0](https://doi.org/10.1515/jib-2022-0058).

title: Physiologically comparable fluorescence measurements
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
