open: When fluorescence is measured on different instruments or in cells under different physiological states, can we infer the underlying biological quantities in a form that is genuinely comparable — with a complete accounting of the uncertainties involved?
status: Interlaboratory optical calibration is established, but changing cell size, maturation, and growth complicate the interpretation of fluorescence in terms of protein abundance (Beal et al. (2021), [Comparative analysis of three studies measuring fluorescence from engineered bacterial genetic constructs](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8183995/)).
solved_when: A method exists that infers comparable biological quantities from fluorescence measurements across instruments and physiological states, with complete uncertainty budgets attached to the inferred values.
why: It prevents calibrated optical signals from being mistaken for equivalent biology, so cross-experiment and cross-lab comparisons reflect real differences rather than measurement artifacts.
key_works: Beal et al. (2021), [Comparative analysis of three studies measuring fluorescence from engineered bacterial genetic constructs](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8183995/).

title: Reference standards for nonfluorescent circuit outputs
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Can the synthetic biology community agree on shared reference standards that make nonfluorescent circuit outputs — secretion, electrical response, mechanical actuation, and dynamic state changes — meaningfully comparable across laboratories? Formally, this asks for a set of consensus metrics and measurement protocols covering each of these functional output classes.
status: International engineering-biology standards work identified continuing measurement needs in 2024, notably Freemont et al. (2024), [Engineering Biology Metrics and Technical Standards for the Global Bioeconomy](https://doi.org/10.25561/110822); related efforts concern metrology, including dynamic reference materials and calibration.
solved_when: Accepted shared standards exist for secretion, electrical response, mechanical actuation, and dynamic state changes, enabling comparable quantification of these outputs across laboratories.
why: Without such standards, circuits with nonfluorescent outputs cannot be benchmarked or exchanged reliably between labs; with them, functional outputs become comparable across laboratories.
key_works: Freemont et al. (2024), [Engineering Biology Metrics and Technical Standards for the Global Bioeconomy](https://doi.org/10.25561/110822).

title: Executable experimental semantics across laboratory platforms
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Can a protocol's biological meaning—its timing, mixing, tolerances, and feedback—be preserved when the same protocol executes on different laboratory automation systems? Formally, this asks for executable experimental semantics such that execution on distinct platforms yields physically equivalent outcomes.
status: LabOP currently provides protocol representations and execution infrastructure, but general physical execution equivalence remains open.
solved_when: A protocol representation and execution infrastructure exists that preserves timing, mixing, tolerances, and feedback across different automation systems, with physical execution equivalence holding in general rather than for special cases.
why: It would make automated experiments portable, so a validated protocol can move between laboratories and platforms without re-engineering or loss of biological intent.
key_works: Biological Protocols Working Group (ongoing), [Laboratory Open Protocol Language](https://github.com/Bioprotocols/labop).

title: Autonomous recovery from failed laboratory operations
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: Can an autonomous laboratory platform detect that an experiment has failed, diagnose the cause, and recover — without human intervention — while preserving sample identity and statistically valid uncertainty estimates throughout?
status: Autonomous enzyme-engineering platforms were demonstrated in 2025; general verified exception recovery remains open. Key work: Singh et al. (2025), [A generalized platform for artificial intelligence-powered autonomous enzyme engineering](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61209-y).
solved_when: A demonstrated system detects, diagnoses, and recovers from unexpected experimental failures during unattended operation, with sample identity preserved and uncertainty estimates remaining valid across the recovery process.
why: It enables unattended design–build–test–learn cycles beyond idealized workflows, so biofoundries can run reliably even when operations deviate from plan.
key_works: Singh et al. (2025), [A generalized platform for artificial intelligence-powered autonomous enzyme engineering](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61209-y).

title: Sustained support for shared biological reference infrastructure
subfield: Design automation, data, measurement, and biofoundries
open: How can the synthetic biology community fund and govern shared reference infrastructure — maintained circuits, calibration materials, software, and recurring independent benchmarks — so that it persists beyond the lifetime of any individual grant?
status: The Global Biofoundry Alliance formed in 2019; long-term reference infrastructure remains a continuing coordination problem. Key works: Hillson et al. (2019), [Building a global alliance of biofoundries](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10079-2); Freemont et al. (2024), [Engineering Biology Metrics and Technical Standards for the Global Bioeconomy](https://doi.org/10.25561/110822).
solved_when: A durable funding and governance mechanism exists that supports maintained reference circuits, calibration materials, software, and recurring independent benchmarks on a continuing basis rather than per-grant.
why: Without sustained support, shared foundations decay between projects, forcing each new effort to rebuild common resources.
key_works: Hillson et al. (2019), [Building a global alliance of biofoundries](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-10079-2); Freemont et al. (2024), [Engineering Biology Metrics and Technical Standards for the Global Bioeconomy](https://doi.org/10.25561/110822).

title: Mechanism-general de novo enzyme design
open: Can we design efficient enzymes for a reaction mechanism we choose in advance, with a calibrated probability that the design will actually work — including for mechanisms that no natural enzyme has ever exemplified?
status: In 2025–2026, metallohydrolase designs achieved substantial activity without experimental optimization, but these selected mechanisms do not establish general design reliability. Key work: Kim et al. (2026), [Computational design of metallohydrolases](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09746-w).
solved_when: A design method prospectively selects target mechanisms, including template-free ones, and produces efficient catalysts with success probabilities that are calibrated against experimental outcomes.
why: It would expand the space of accessible biochemical transformations beyond what natural enzymology provides, enabling chemistry that biology has never evolved.
key_works: Kim et al. (2026), [Computational design of metallohydrolases](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09746-w).

title: Joint activity–stability–selectivity optimization
open: Can an enzyme be engineered to meet simultaneous specifications for activity, selectivity, solvent tolerance, and operating lifetime, with the trade-offs among these properties predicted and validated in advance?
status: AI redesign improved stability and subsequent evolution in 2026, per Krasnow et al. (2026), [AI-redesigned starting points and outcomes enhance protein evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10820-0); arbitrary combinations of industrial constraints remain open.
solved_when: A designed enzyme satisfies the stated rate, selectivity, solvent-tolerance, and lifetime specifications at once, and the predicted trade-offs between these constraints are experimentally validated.
why: It produces enzymes suitable for real industrial processes rather than laboratory conditions.
key_works: Krasnow et al. (2026), [AI-redesigned starting points and outcomes enhance protein evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10820-0).

title: Predictable polyketide module interfaces
open: Can we predict, from sequence or structure alone, which interfaces between unfamiliar polyketide synthase modules will preserve intermediate transfer and maintain throughput? The goal is a design rule that yields working junctions on the first try, without empirical junction screening.
status: The problem dates to combinatorial biosynthesis efforts in the 1990s. Broadly useful junction motifs were identified in Huang et al. (2025), [Plug-and-play engineering of modular polyketide synthases](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-025-01878-4), but universal compatibility of module interfaces remains unestablished.
solved_when: A predictive method exists that specifies module interfaces reliably enough to eliminate empirical junction searches while preserving intermediate transfer and throughput in unfamiliar module combinations.
why: It would make complex natural-product synthesis programmable, turning modular polyketide assembly into a predictable engineering discipline rather than a trial-and-error search.
key_works: Huang et al. (2025), [Plug-and-play engineering of modular polyketide synthases](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-025-01878-4).

title: Many-edit assembly lines without cumulative yield loss
open: Can a biosynthetic assembly line be reprogrammed at many positions at once while keeping practical titers and purity? More formally, is there a set of predictive interaction rules for multi-site editing of modular biosynthesis that avoids cumulative yield collapse?
status: The state of the art is five-step skeletal editing of a modular polyketide synthase, reported in 2026 by Kudo et al. (2026), [Skeletal editing via multi-step engineering of a modular polyketide synthase](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-71501-0); that effort retained 26% of starting productivity, and cumulative losses remain consequential.
solved_when: Numerous biosynthetic positions can be edited simultaneously with retained practical throughput and purity, and predictive rules for interactions among edits are demonstrated — substantially overcoming the cumulative losses seen today, where five-step editing retains only 26% of starting productivity.
why: It would enable substantial molecular redesign without sacrificing manufacturability, turning biosynthetic assembly lines into reliably editable platforms rather than ones whose yield erodes with each edit.
key_works: Kudo et al. (2026), [Skeletal editing via multi-step engineering of a modular polyketide synthase](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-71501-0).

title: Portable noncanonical-cofactor enzyme conversion
open: Can diverse redox enzymes be re-engineered to use inexpensive, orthogonal cofactors while preserving their native activity and selectivity?
status: Large specificity switches and adjustable redox driving forces were demonstrated in 2024 (Aspacio et al. (2024), [Shifting redox reaction equilibria on demand using an orthogonal redox cofactor](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-024-01702-5)); methods remain architecture- and reaction-dependent.
solved_when: A general method exists for converting diverse redox enzymes to inexpensive orthogonal cofactors such that activity and selectivity are preserved, without the outcome depending heavily on enzyme architecture or reaction type.
why: It decouples desired reactions from native redox constraints, enabling redox chemistry that native cofactor systems cannot drive.
key_works: Aspacio et al. (2024), [Shifting redox reaction equilibria on demand using an orthogonal redox cofactor](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-024-01702-5).

title: Thermodynamic yield–rate–protein frontier
open: What are the fundamental limits on how much product a metabolic pathway can yield at a given flux, when ATP generation, enzyme mass, reaction reversibility, and metabolite concentrations are all accounted for together? Formally, derive achievable bounds linking product yield, flux, ATP generation, and enzyme mass while accounting for reversibility and metabolite concentrations.
status: Measurements across glycolytic strategies in 2025 connected thermodynamics to protein burden (Khana et al. (2025), [Thermodynamics shapes the in vivo enzyme burden of glycolytic pathways](https://doi.org/10.1128/mbio.01837-25)), but general pathway bounds remain unavailable. A related line of work exists in nonequilibrium physics on finite-power efficiency bounds.
solved_when: A general theory of achievable pathway bounds is derived that quantitatively connects product yield, flux, ATP generation, and enzyme mass under reversibility and finite metabolite concentrations.
why: Such bounds would identify the realistic design limits of metabolic engineering, telling engineers which yield–rate–protein trade-offs are physically attainable rather than merely unoptimized.
key_works: Khana et al. (2025), [Thermodynamics shapes the in vivo enzyme burden of glycolytic pathways](https://doi.org/10.1128/mbio.01837-25).

title: In vivo enzyme-saturation prediction
open: Can we predict, from intracellular metabolite concentrations alone, how occupied each enzyme will be and what flux it will carry in a living cell — before any engineered pathway is built? Formally, this asks for a quantitative theory that maps intracellular concentrations to enzyme saturation states and pathway fluxes under crowded, regulated in vivo conditions.
status: Optimal-utilization theory advanced in 2023 through Sahin, Weilandt, and Hatzimanikatis (2023), [Optimal enzyme utilization suggests that concentrations and thermodynamics determine binding mechanisms and enzyme saturations](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-38159-4), but crowded, regulated cellular conditions remain difficult to predict quantitatively.
solved_when: A quantitative method exists that predicts enzyme occupancy and flux from intracellular concentrations with useful accuracy under crowded, regulated cellular conditions, enabling such predictions prior to constructing an engineered pathway.
why: It would let engineers distinguish failures caused by catalytic shortages from failures caused by unfavorable metabolite levels, pointing directly at which fix a pathway needs.
key_works: Sahin, Weilandt, and Hatzimanikatis (2023), [Optimal enzyme utilization suggests that concentrations and thermodynamics determine binding mechanisms and enzyme saturations](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-38159-4).

title: Prospectively correct production-host selection
open: Can we predict, before any wet-lab work, which production host will deliver the best achievable yield, rate, and recovery cost for an untested product–feedstock combination? In formal terms, this asks for a prospectively validated model that ranks candidate chassis correctly on real processes rather than retrospectively on computational comparisons alone.
status: Five hosts and 235 chemicals were compared computationally in 2025 by Kim, Kim, and Lee (2025), [Comprehensive evaluation of the capacities of microbial cell factories](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58227-1); real-process ranking remains a prospective validation gap.
solved_when: A method exists that selects the optimal host for an untested product–feedstock combination and whose ranking is confirmed by prospective, real-process validation — covering comparisons at least at the scale of the computational benchmark of 5 hosts and 235 chemicals.
why: It prevents expensive investment in unsuitable hosts, saving development resources that would otherwise be spent scaling a chassis that cannot deliver.
key_works: Kim, Kim, and Lee (2025), [Comprehensive evaluation of the capacities of microbial cell factories](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58227-1).

title: Product-export capacity and energy bounds
open: What is the maximum export flux a cell can sustain once membrane area, transporter kinetics, and the cellular energy budget are all accounted for? In formal terms, establish a bound on sustainable product-export capacity as a function of these coupled constraints.
status: Import–export coordination models advanced in 2025; general experimentally validated export bounds remain open. Key work: Mannan et al. (2025), [Design principles for engineering bacteria to maximise chemical production from batch cultures](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-55347-y).
solved_when: A general, experimentally validated bound on maximum sustainable export flux — incorporating membrane area, transporter kinetics, and energy budgets — is derived and confirmed.
why: It identifies when transport, rather than metabolism, is the bottleneck on production, telling engineers where further optimization is futile.
key_works: Mannan et al. (2025), [Design principles for engineering bacteria to maximise chemical production from batch cultures](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-55347-y).

title: Productive ambient-air CORE-cycle integration
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can aerobic CO₂-to-formate reduction, downstream carbon assimilation, and renewable cofactor regeneration be run as one productive system under ambient air, with complete sustained carbon and energy balances across the whole cycle?
status: CORE supported E. coli C1 metabolism and serine biosynthesis in 2025 (Satanowski et al. (2025), [Design and implementation of aerobic and ambient CO₂-reduction as an entry-point for enhanced carbon fixation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-57549-4)); productive renewable-energy integration remains open.
solved_when: The coupled CORE-cycle system demonstrates sustained, fully balanced operation: continuous CO₂ reduction to formate, assimilation of that carbon into biomass or product, and renewable-energy-driven cofactor regeneration, with complete carbon and energy accounting over the operating period.
why: It would connect ambient carbon capture directly to useful biosynthesis, turning dilute atmospheric CO₂ into products rather than an energy sink.
key_works: Satanowski et al. (2025), [Design and implementation of aerobic and ambient CO₂-reduction as an entry-point for enhanced carbon fixation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-57549-4).

title: High-flux methanol growth with high product yield
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can a synthetic methylotroph be engineered to grow rapidly on methanol alone while also converting most of that carbon into a desired product at high cell density and with stable fermentation performance?
status: Methanol-only growth and a bioproduction chassis were established by 2024 (Reiter et al. (2024), [A synthetic methylotrophic Escherichia coli as a chassis for bioproduction from methanol](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-024-01137-0)); simultaneous optimization of rapid growth, yield, and high-density fermentation remains product-specific.
solved_when: A strain achieves rapid methanol-only growth, high product carbon yield, and stable high-density fermentation simultaneously; success is judged per product, since the joint optimization targets are product-specific.
why: It would make methanol a practical manufacturing feedstock for industrial bioproduction.
key_works: Reiter et al. (2024), [A synthetic methylotrophic Escherichia coli as a chassis for bioproduction from methanol](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-024-01137-0).

title: Formaldehyde damage under fluctuating methanol supply
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can a methanol-based bioprocess be designed so that genetic integrity and product output are preserved even when methanol feed, oxygenation, and formaldehyde assimilation rates fluctuate independently of one another? Formally, the goal is a cultivation strategy or engineered chassis in which formaldehyde-associated DNA–protein damage does not accumulate under such fluctuating operation.
status: Methanol-grown E. coli reached a 3.5-hour doubling time in 2024 (Nieh et al. (2024), [Evolutionary engineering of methylotrophic E. coli enables fast growth on methanol](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-53206-4)), but formaldehyde-associated DNA–protein damage remains a challenge under fluctuating operation. A related avenue is DNA–protein crosslink repair.
solved_when: A methanol-grown production strain maintains genetic integrity and production under independently fluctuating methanol supply, oxygenation, and formaldehyde assimilation, without cumulative formaldehyde-associated DNA–protein damage during industrial cultivation.
why: Without this, cumulative formaldehyde-associated DNA–protein damage builds up over industrial cultivation runs, degrading both the host and its productivity; solving it makes long, fluctuating methanol-fed processes robust.
key_works: Nieh et al. (2024), [Evolutionary engineering of methylotrophic E. coli enables fast growth on methanol](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-53206-4).

title: Efficient electrogenerated-formate fermentation
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can electrochemical formate production and microbial fermentation be combined into a single integrated process that performs under realistic impurities and variable power supply? The goal is an integrated system with complete product-level efficiency accounting across the electrochemical and biological stages.
status: Synthetic formatotrophic E. coli achieved doubling below 4.5 hours in 2025 (Cowan et al. (2025), [Fast growth and high-titer bioproduction from renewable formate via metal-dependent formate dehydrogenase in Escherichia coli](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61001-y)), but integrated electrochemical-to-product performance remains separate. A related obstacle is durable CO₂-to-formate electrolysis.
solved_when: An integrated electrochemical formate production–fermentation process is demonstrated that operates under realistic impurities and variable power, with full accounting of efficiency from electricity to final product; the reference biological benchmark is synthetic formatotrophic E. coli achieving doubling below 4.5 hours (2025).
why: It connects renewable electricity directly to biomanufacturing, turning intermittent clean power into chemical products without separate optimization of each stage.
key_works: Cowan et al. (2025), [Fast growth and high-titer bioproduction from renewable formate via metal-dependent formate dehydrogenase in Escherichia coli](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61001-y).

title: Portable reductive-glycine yield advantage
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can we predict, and then reproduce, the yield gains of the synthetic reductive glycine pathway when it is moved from one host organism to another? In formal terms, can a quantitative framework account for the energy, maintenance, and regulatory costs of the pathway so that its yield advantage transfers predictably across hosts?
status: Replacing the Calvin cycle with the reductive glycine pathway improved yield in Cupriavidus necator, reported in 2025 (Dronsella et al. (2025), [One-carbon fixation via the synthetic reductive glycine pathway exceeds yield of the Calvin cycle](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41564-025-01941-9)), but the advantage has not transferred uniformly to heterotrophic hosts.
solved_when: A model incorporating energy, maintenance, and regulatory costs correctly predicts reductive-glycine pathway yields in hosts beyond the original demonstration, and those predicted gains are experimentally reproduced — including in heterotrophic hosts where the advantage has so far failed to transfer uniformly.
why: It would establish general conditions under which replacing a native carbon-fixation pathway actually improves real production, turning pathway replacement from a case-by-case empirical gamble into an engineering discipline.
key_works: Dronsella et al. (2025), [One-carbon fixation via the synthetic reductive glycine pathway exceeds yield of the Calvin cycle](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41564-025-01941-9).

title: Broad-product industrial gas fermentation
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can continuous gas fermentation retain high selectivity when extended to products with widely differing ATP, redox, and precursor requirements? The goal is to generalize this industrial platform beyond the handful of metabolically favorable products to broad chemical coverage.
status: Pilot acetone and isopropanol production approached 3 g/L/h and 90% selectivity in 2022; much broader chemical coverage remains open. Key work: Liew et al. (2022), [Carbon-negative production of acetone and isopropanol by gas fermentation at industrial pilot scale](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-021-01195-w). Gas–liquid mass-transfer limits remain a relevant chemical-engineering constraint.
solved_when: Continuous gas fermentation at industrially relevant rates achieves high selectivity across a broad range of products with different ATP, redox, and precursor demands, matching or exceeding the pilot benchmark of 3 g/L/h and 90% selectivity.
why: A solution expands gas fermentation beyond a few favorable products, enabling carbon-negative manufacture of a much wider chemical portfolio.
key_works: Liew et al. (2022), [Carbon-negative production of acetone and isopropanol by gas fermentation at industrial pilot scale](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-021-01195-w).

title: Power-following microbial electrosynthesis
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can microbial electrosynthesis maintain predictable product output and cell viability through the fluctuations and outages of renewable power supply, without resorting to excessive storage or backup power? Formally, the goal is a reactor system whose production rate and culture health remain within acceptable bounds across repeated power-cycling and restart events.
status: Improved reactors brought acetate productivity toward conventional biotechnology rates in 2025 (Deutzmann, Callander, and Spormann (2025), [Improved reactor design enables productivity of microbial electrosynthesis on par with classical biotechnology](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biortech.2024.131733)); repeated cycling and restart reliability remain open.
solved_when: A reactor design or operating strategy is demonstrated that preserves output and viability through realistic renewable-power fluctuations and outages, with repeated cycling and restart reliability established, and without requiring excessive storage or backup power capacity.
why: It would let electricity-driven biological production track variable renewable supply, turning biomanufacturing into a flexible electricity consumer rather than one demanding firm power.
key_works: Deutzmann, Callander, and Spormann (2025), [Improved reactor design enables productivity of microbial electrosynthesis on par with classical biotechnology](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biortech.2024.131733).

title: High-rate electrosynthesis beyond acetate and methane
subfield: Synthetic carbon fixation and one-carbon biomanufacturing
open: Can a microbial electrosynthesis system be engineered to make a product more complex than acetate or methane while keeping electron uptake, selectivity, and reactor productivity at the levels those simple-product systems achieve?
status: High-rate acetate and methane systems exist, but their performance is not a general property of engineered product pathways; Deutzmann, Callander, and Spormann (2025), [Improved reactor design enables productivity of microbial electrosynthesis on par with classical biotechnology](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biortech.2024.131733), represent the state of the art in reactor productivity.
solved_when: An engineered pathway beyond acetate and methane is demonstrated at high rate, with electrode productivity and system efficiency comparable to existing acetate and methane systems.
why: It would extend electrobiology from a handful of simple products to a general manufacturing platform, expanding the product range of microbial electrosynthesis.
key_works: Deutzmann, Callander, and Spormann (2025), [Improved reactor design enables productivity of microbial electrosynthesis on par with classical biotechnology](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biortech.2024.131733).

title: Long-lived self-maintaining enzyme factories
open: Can a cell-free enzyme factory keep producing indefinitely by continuously replacing its own deactivated enzymes and cofactors, at a total cost below that of periodically discarding and rebuilding the batch?
status: A self-replenishing CO₂-fixing system operated for six hours in 2022 (Luo et al. (2022), [A cell-free self-replenishing CO₂-fixing system](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-022-00746-x)); industrially meaningful long-duration operation remains open.
solved_when: A cell-free system sustains production over a long-duration, industrially meaningful operating period while self-replenishing inactive enzymes and cofactors, with overall cost lower than periodic batch replacement.
why: It extends catalyst lifetime and reactor utilization, turning cell-free systems from short-lived batch reactions into continuously operating factories.
key_works: Luo et al. (2022), [A cell-free self-replenishing CO₂-fixing system](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-022-00746-x).

title: Near-stoichiometric inexpensive ATP regeneration
open: Can ATP be regenerated from inexpensive feedstocks at near-theoretical energetic yield, in a cell-free system that supports diverse enzyme cascades without accumulating by-products that inhibit them?
status: A 2025 system achieved 2.53 ATP equivalents per fructose against a theoretical three; general process compatibility remains open. Key work: Kraußer et al. (2025), [Cell-Free Reaction System for ATP Regeneration from d-Fructose](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40143462/).
solved_when: A regeneration scheme converts cheap inputs (e.g., d-fructose) to ATP at close to the theoretical stoichiometry — the benchmark being improvement on the 2.53 ATP equivalents per fructose against a theoretical three — while remaining compatible with a broad range of cascade reactions and avoiding inhibitory by-product buildup.
why: ATP supply is a major cost driver in cell-free biomanufacturing; a near-stoichiometric, inexpensive regeneration route would substantially cut that cost.
key_works: Kraußer et al. (2025), [Cell-Free Reaction System for ATP Regeneration from d-Fructose](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40143462/).

title: Economical complex-cofactor cell-free synthesis
open: Can a long, multi-enzyme cofactor-synthesis pathway be run economically in a cell-free system, with productivity and catalyst utilization high enough to compete with microbial fermentation? Formally, the goal is to engineer cell-free routes to complex cofactors whose cost per unit product matches fermentation-based production.
status: A 36-enzyme cell-free system for vitamin B₁₂ synthesis yielded 0.42 or 5.78 mg/L depending on the precursor in 2023 (Kang et al. (2023), [A synthetic cell-free 36-enzyme reaction system for vitamin B₁₂ production](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-40932-4)), but the manufacturing economics remain unresolved.
solved_when: A cell-free synthesis of a complex cofactor achieves productivity and catalyst utilization sufficient to be economically competitive with fermentation, as judged by a manufacturing-economics analysis that resolves the currently unresolved cost question.
why: It would enable controlled, fermentation-free manufacture of complex biochemical cofactors.
key_works: Kang et al. (2023), [A synthetic cell-free 36-enzyme reaction system for vitamin B₁₂ production](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-40932-4).

title: Carbon-conserving crude-lysate metabolism
open: Can a crude cell-free lysate match the carbon selectivity of a purified, defined-enzyme system while retaining the economic advantages of the lysate format, despite endogenous reactions competing for carbon?
status: Carbon-conserving malate production was demonstrated in 2025; inhibition and dilution were needed to manage endogenous metabolism. Key work: Cardiff et al. (2025), [Carbon-conserving bioproduction of malate in an E. coli-based cell-free system](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40210085/).
solved_when: A crude-lysate platform achieves carbon selectivity for the target product equivalent to a defined-enzyme system, without the need for complete purification of components.
why: A solution improves product yield while preserving the low cost of crude lysates, avoiding the expense of enzyme purification.
key_works: Cardiff et al. (2025), [Carbon-conserving bioproduction of malate in an E. coli-based cell-free system](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40210085/).

title: Formulation transfer across lysates and proteins
open: Can we predict formulation conditions that will perform robustly for a new lysate lot or a new target protein, without extensive re-optimization for each case? Formally, this asks whether formulation knowledge learned on tested lysate–protein systems transfers reliably across preparations, laboratories, and folding requirements.
status: Design-driven studies improved tested systems in 2026; transfer across preparations, laboratories, and folding requirements remains open. Key work: Olsen et al. (2026), [Design-driven optimization of low-cost reagent formulations for reproducible and high-yielding cell-free gene expression](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69605-8).
solved_when: A method exists that, given a new lysate lot and/or protein (including those with distinct folding requirements), predicts formulations whose performance is robust without extensive re-optimization, and this transfer is demonstrated across preparations and laboratories.
why: It would cut the optimization cost of setting up each new cell-free expression system and reduce batch-to-batch variability in yield and reproducibility.
key_works: Olsen et al. (2026), [Design-driven optimization of low-cost reagent formulations for reproducible and high-yielding cell-free gene expression](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69605-8).

title: Microscale enzyme-screen to reactor transfer
open: Can we predict whether an enzyme variant's ranking from a microscale cell-free screen will survive purification, immobilization, and scale-up to a manufacturing reactor? A satisfactory answer would let us disentangle changes that merely improve expression in the screen from genuine catalytic improvements that persist in production.
status: Machine-learning-guided cell-free enzyme engineering advanced in 2025 with Landwehr et al. (2025), [Accelerated enzyme engineering by machine-learning guided cell-free expression](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-55399-0), but transfer to the manufacturing environment remains additional work.
solved_when: A validated method exists that predicts, from microscale screening data, which enzyme variants retain their performance ranking after purification, immobilization, and reactor scale-up, with a demonstrated ability to separate expression-level effects from true catalytic gains.
why: It prevents engineering campaigns from selecting variants whose apparent improvements vanish during production, wasting downstream development on artifacts of the screening environment.
key_works: Landwehr et al. (2025), [Accelerated enzyme engineering by machine-learning guided cell-free expression](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-55399-0).

title: Coupled-gradient scale-down fidelity
open: Can we design scale-down simulators that reproduce the coupled oxygen, substrate, pH, and shear histories a cell actually experiences at industrial scale, so that performance losses at a previously unseen reactor scale can be predicted before scale-up?
status: Scale-down research spans decades, and a 2024 three-compartment simulator reproduced substrate-related cellular lifelines, but general multivariable fidelity across coupled gradients remains open. Key work: Zhao et al. (2024), [Developing rational scale-down simulators for mimicking substrate heterogeneities based on cell lifelines in industrial-scale bioreactors](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38272147/).
solved_when: A laboratory-scale simulator reproduces the joint multivariable (oxygen, substrate, pH, shear) environmental histories of industrial-scale cultivation and accurately predicts process performance losses at reactor scales it was not calibrated on.
why: It would make laboratory experiments genuinely predictive of industrial bioreactor behavior, replacing empirical scale-up rules with tested fidelity.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2024), [Developing rational scale-down simulators for mimicking substrate heterogeneities based on cell lifelines in industrial-scale bioreactors](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38272147/).

title: Long-duration productive-population stability
open: Can a microbial production strain be engineered or operated so that high-producing cells remain the dominant fraction of the population over a long continuous-cultivation campaign, even though faster-growing low-producing variants constantly arise and process conditions fluctuate?
status: This is a longstanding industrial problem. Worland et al. (2026; online 2025), [Staying productive under pressure: systems evaluations of β-carotene production in Yarrowia lipolytica under continuous fermentation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.08.019), observed substantial production loss after approximately 18 generations under continuous cultivation.
solved_when: A continuous fermentation sustains a high-producing population fraction over long durations, demonstrably resisting takeover by fitter low-producing variants; the reference point to beat is the substantial production loss observed after approximately 18 generations in the 2025/2026 Yarrowia work.
why: Stable producing populations would make long production campaigns dependable, avoiding the yield collapse that currently cuts continuous fermentations short.
key_works: Worland et al. (2026; online 2025), [Staying productive under pressure: systems evaluations of β-carotene production in Yarrowia lipolytica under continuous fermentation](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.08.019).

title: Forecasting producer collapse from population measurements
open: Can we predict when a production strain will collapse, using only early measurements of growth, population heterogeneity, and stress? More formally, is there a prospective method that outputs a calibrated failure-time forecast for a fermentation batch from such early-phase data?
status: Recent fermentation models connect subpopulation changes to production loss (Worland et al. (2026; online 2025), [Staying productive under pressure](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.08.019)), but general prospective failure-time prediction remains absent.
solved_when: A predictive method demonstrably forecasts production-collapse timing from early growth, heterogeneity, and stress measurements with calibrated false-alarm rates in a prospective setting.
why: It enables intervention before expensive batches fail.
key_works: Worland et al. (2026; online 2025), [Staying productive under pressure](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2025.08.019).

title: Public paired laboratory–industrial performance datasets
open: Can the community assemble and publish paired datasets that match strain information, laboratory measurements, large-reactor exposure data, and actual production outcomes — including failed transfers and data from held-out facilities — so that scale-up predictions can be tested against reality?
status: Individual mechanistic case studies exist, such as Zhao et al. (2024), [Developing rational scale-down simulators for mimicking substrate heterogeneities based on cell lifelines in industrial-scale bioreactors](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38272147/), but a broad prospective scale-up benchmark remains an infrastructure gap.
solved_when: A public benchmark dataset exists that pairs strain, laboratory, large-reactor exposure, and production data, and explicitly includes failed scale-up transfers along with held-out facilities reserved for independent evaluation.
why: Such data allows independent validation of scale-up predictions, turning scale-up from anecdote into a testable science.
key_works: Zhao et al. (2024), [Developing rational scale-down simulators for mimicking substrate heterogeneities based on cell lifelines in industrial-scale bioreactors](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38272147/).

title: Affordable integrated pilot-fermentation access
open: Can shared infrastructure combining fermentation, feed preparation, and downstream processing be sustained at prices accessible to teams without dedicated plants?
status: EBRC's 2021 roadmap identified this gap; translation and scale-up remain active 2025–2026 priorities. Key work: EBRC (2021), [Engineering Biology & Materials Science: Processing](https://roadmap.ebrc.org/2021-roadmap-materials/technical-themes-materials/processing/).
solved_when: Integrated pilot-fermentation facilities exist that are affordable to teams lacking their own plants and operate on a sustained basis.
why: Such facilities bridge laboratory demonstrations and commercial decisions, enabling scale-up work that small teams could not otherwise perform.
key_works: EBRC (2021), [Engineering Biology & Materials Science: Processing](https://roadmap.ebrc.org/2021-roadmap-materials/technical-themes-materials/processing/).

title: Experimentally grounded scale-up economics and carbon accounting
open: Can we predict the full-scale cost and environmental performance of an industrial biomanufacturing process with calibrated uncertainty, and validate those predictions against the actual performance of operating commercial plants?
status: Techno-economic analysis (TEA) and life-cycle assessment (LCA) are widespread in the field; 2026 assessments emphasize integration, while prospective validation across commercial outcomes remains limited. Key works: Kim et al. (2026), [Beyond petrochemicals: challenges and opportunities in industrial-scale biomanufacturing](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73835-1).
solved_when: A predictive framework exists for full-scale cost and environmental performance whose uncertainty estimates are calibrated and validated against outcomes at operating commercial plants.
why: It prevents misleading early claims of economic or environmental advantage before processes reach commercial scale.
key_works: Kim et al. (2026), [Beyond petrochemicals: challenges and opportunities in industrial-scale biomanufacturing](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73835-1).

title: Low-pH organic-acid production without hidden energy penalties
open: Can engineered hosts sustain high product yields at a recovery-friendly low pH once proton export, acid re-entry, and cellular energy costs are fully accounted for? Formally, the goal is an integrated process design in which no energy penalty hidden in acid tolerance erodes the yield gained from operating at low pH.
status: Acid-tolerant yeast engineering advanced in 2025, notably Tran et al. (2025), [Decompartmentalization of the yeast mitochondrial metabolism to improve chemical production in Issatchenkia orientalis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62304-w); however, the integrated advantages of low-pH operation remain pathway- and host-dependent.
solved_when: A production host achieves high organic-acid yields at recovery-friendly low pH, with the energy costs of proton export and acid re-entry explicitly quantified and shown not to undermine those yields.
why: It removes hidden energy penalties that would otherwise negate the savings, directly reducing neutralization and separation costs in large-scale organic-acid manufacturing.
key_works: Tran et al. (2025), [Decompartmentalization of the yeast mitochondrial metabolism to improve chemical production in Issatchenkia orientalis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62304-w).

title: High-crystallinity PET recycling with little pretreatment
open: Can crystalline post-consumer PET be depolymerized enzymatically at high solids loading, using little enzyme and little energy for amorphization pretreatment?
status: Engineered hydrolases already support efficient recycling; 2026 PHL7 variants improve performance (Blázquez-Sánchez et al. (2026), [Computational engineering of the polyester hydrolase PHL7 for efficient poly(ethylene terephthalate) degradation in biocatalytic recycling processes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-70868-4)), while accessibility and full pretreatment costs remain constraints.
solved_when: A process achieves depolymerization of crystalline post-consumer PET at high solids loading with low enzyme use and minimal amorphization energy, without substantial pretreatment.
why: It would extend economical enzymatic recycling to the harder, highly crystalline fraction of PET waste that current processes struggle to handle cost-effectively.
key_works: Blázquez-Sánchez et al. (2026), [Computational engineering of the polyester hydrolase PHL7 for efficient poly(ethylene terephthalate) degradation in biocatalytic recycling processes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-70868-4).

title: Variable multilayer-packaging enzymatic recycling
open: Can variable, contaminated multilayer packaging waste be enzymatically recycled so that useful fractions are recovered while every recovered material retains acceptable properties?
status: Enzymatic recycling of PET–PE multilayer packaging reached 4.5 kg scale in 2025 (Van Vliet et al. (2025), [Efficient Recycling of PET-PE Multilayer Packaging Materials Based on Enzymatic Depolymerization of PET](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.4c09388)); diverse adhesives, pigments, residues, and polymer combinations remain unresolved.
solved_when: A process handles diverse adhesives, pigments, residues, and polymer combinations in variable multilayer packaging and recovers each material fraction at acceptable quality, extending beyond the PET–PE system demonstrated at 4.5 kg scale.
why: It addresses packaging streams that existing recycling poorly serves, converting heterogeneous mixed-material waste into usable feedstocks.
key_works: Van Vliet et al. (2025), [Efficient Recycling of PET-PE Multilayer Packaging Materials Based on Enzymatic Depolymerization of PET](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.4c09388).

title: Complete-carbon polyamide-hydrolysate upgrading
open: Can realistic nylon hydrolysates — the complex, contaminated mixtures that actual chemical depolymerization produces — be converted into specified products with high carbon recovery and minimal feed purification?
status: Chemical hydrolysis combined with engineered Pseudomonas upcycling was demonstrated in 2025 (De Witt et al. (2025), [Upcycling of polyamides through chemical hydrolysis and engineered Pseudomonas putida](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41564-025-01929-5)); mixed formulations and contamination remain open.
solved_when: Realistic mixed nylon hydrolysate components are upgraded to specified products with high carbon recovery and little feed purification, with mixed formulations and contamination addressed rather than avoided.
why: It recovers value from multiple waste components, turning heterogeneous polyamide waste streams into products rather than requiring sorted, clean inputs.
key_works: De Witt et al. (2025), [Upcycling of polyamides through chemical hydrolysis and engineered Pseudomonas putida](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41564-025-01929-5).

title: Stable mixed-plastic conversion across feed shifts
open: Can a microbial consortium hold its composition, carbon recovery, and product quality when the proportions of plastic-derived feeds shift over time? More precisely, is it possible to engineer a stable consortium that tolerates real, undiluted deconstruction mixtures through varying feed compositions?
status: Specialist consortia have processed diluted real deconstruction mixtures in 2026; robustness on undiluted feeds and scale-up remain open.
solved_when: A consortium maintains composition, carbon recovery, and product quality across changes in plastic-derived feed proportions, and demonstrates robustness on undiluted real deconstruction mixtures at scale.
why: It unlocks production from inconsistent mixed waste, which is the realistic input for any circular-plastics process, rather than from carefully controlled synthetic feeds.
key_works: Diao et al. (2026), [Engineering microbial consortia for mixed plastic upcycling](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67409-w).

title: High-yield conversion of real lignin streams
open: Can diverse industrial lignin streams be converted into a single recoverable product at high yield, while properly accounting for insoluble material and unconsumed oligomers?
status: Biological funneling has progressed for over a decade; 2025 scale-up work still faces whole-lignin accessibility and rate constraints, as in Seeger et al. (2025), [Scaling-up the Bioconversion of Lignin to 2,4-Pyridinedicarboxylic Acid With Engineered Pseudomonas putida for Bio-Based Plastics Production](https://doi.org/10.1002/bit.70020).
solved_when: A process converts diverse industrial lignins into one recoverable product with the mass balance explicitly closing over insoluble material and unconsumed oligomers, at yields suitable for scale-up.
why: It would make a large fraction of biomass available as a manufacturing feedstock rather than waste.
key_works: Seeger et al. (2025), [Scaling-up the Bioconversion of Lignin to 2,4-Pyridinedicarboxylic Acid With Engineered Pseudomonas putida for Bio-Based Plastics Production](https://doi.org/10.1002/bit.70020).

title: Predictable regulation for unknown aromatic mixtures
open: Can a metabolic funneling pathway be adapted to aromatic mixtures it has never seen before, without accumulating toxic intermediates or requiring extensive external tuning? Formally, this asks for regulation that remains predictable and safe across heterogeneous, a priori unknown feedstock compositions.
status: Autonomous layered regulation was demonstrated in 2026; transfer to broader industrial mixtures remains open. Key work: Xu et al. (2026), [Engineering a robust and autonomous biological funneling for efficient valorization of lignin-related aromatics](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74424-y).
solved_when: A biological funneling system handles previously unseen aromatic mixtures while avoiding toxic intermediate accumulation and without extensive external tuning, and the approach is shown to transfer to broader industrial mixtures.
why: It would make lignin valorization robust to the variable composition of real lignin-derived feed streams, which is a key obstacle to industrial deployment.
key_works: Xu et al. (2026), [Engineering a robust and autonomous biological funneling for efficient valorization of lignin-related aromatics](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74424-y).

title: Durable low-salt nonsterile fermentation
subfield: Nonconventional microbial, fungal, and algal chassis
open: Can an open, nonsterile fermentation process be kept economically productive over an extended production campaign despite invading competitors and variations in the feed stream? More precisely, can contamination events and feed shifts be managed so that recovery costs do not erase the savings from operating without sterilization?
status: Halomonas has been engineered to reach 76 g/L biomass containing 86% PHB at 0.5% NaCl (Sun et al. (2026), [Engineering Halomonas for low-salt, open, and unsterile production of polyhydroxybutyrate](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2026.01.002)), but campaign-long robustness of such processes remains unaddressed as a separate challenge.
solved_when: A design is demonstrated that maintains economical open, low-salt, nonsterile fermentation over a long production campaign, with contamination-recovery costs included in the overall economics.
why: It removes the costs of sterilization and high-salinity operation, which are major expenses in current fermentation processes.
key_works: Sun et al. (2026), [Engineering Halomonas for low-salt, open, and unsterile production of polyhydroxybutyrate](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tibtech.2026.01.002).

title: Predictive fungal morphology across scales
subfield: Nonconventional microbial, fungal, and algal chassis
open: Can we genetically specify fungal morphology and predict the resulting viscosity, oxygen transfer, and product formation across different reactor geometries?
status: Engineered dispersion improved Aspergillus production in 2025; advantageous morphology remains process-dependent. Key work: Zhou et al. (2025), [Engineering dispersed mycelium morphology in Aspergillus niger for enhanced mycoprotein production via CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biortech.2025.132652).
solved_when: A filamentous fungal host's morphology can be genetically programmed such that viscosity, oxygen transfer, and product formation are quantitatively predicted across reactor geometries.
why: Makes filamentous hosts easier to scale, connecting genetic design to bioreactor performance.
key_works: Zhou et al. (2025), [Engineering dispersed mycelium morphology in Aspergillus niger for enhanced mycoprotein production via CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biortech.2025.132652).

title: Product-general fungal secretion improvement
subfield: Nonconventional microbial, fungal, and algal chassis
open: Can we predict, for a protein never produced in a fungal host before, which secretion intervention will improve its export without harming folding, activity, growth, or production lifetime? In other words, is there a product-general design rule for fungal secretion rather than case-by-case empirical tuning?
status: Overexpression of msnA was reported in 2026 to reprogram metabolism and enhance recombinant protein secretion by up to 2.8-fold across Aspergillus species, though target-specific and total-protein effects differed (Antoniel et al. (2026), [Overexpression of msnA reprograms metabolism to enhance recombinant protein secretion across Aspergillus species](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12934-026-02975-2)).
solved_when: A method exists that, applied to new target proteins in fungal chassis, reliably improves secretion while preserving folding, activity, growth, and production lifetime — matching or exceeding the roughly 2.8-fold secretion improvements reported across Aspergillus species, and doing so predictably rather than by screening.
why: It would make fungal protein production transferable between products, so each new enzyme or therapeutic protein does not require a fresh empirical secretion campaign.
key_works: Antoniel et al. (2026), [Overexpression of msnA reprograms metabolism to enhance recombinant protein secretion across Aspergillus species](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12934-026-02975-2).

title: Productive cyanobacteria under fluctuating light
subfield: Nonconventional microbial, fungal, and algal chassis
open: Can engineered cyanobacteria maintain product yield under realistic fluctuating light — bright light, shading, darkness, and mixing — without diverting excessive carbon into protective mechanisms?
status: Improved tolerance to fluctuating light was genetically characterized in 2026; stable industrial product output remains a further target. Key work: Figueroa-Gonzalez et al. (2026), [Improving tolerance to fluctuating light through adaptive laboratory evolution in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-72689-x).
solved_when: A cyanobacterial production strain sustains stable product output through cycles of bright light, shading, darkness, and mixing, with no excessive protective carbon diversion.
why: It would make phototrophic production resilient to the illumination conditions actually encountered outdoors or in industrial photobioreactors, rather than the controlled light of laboratory settings.
key_works: Figueroa-Gonzalez et al. (2026), [Improving tolerance to fluctuating light through adaptive laboratory evolution in the cyanobacterium Synechocystis](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-72689-x).

title: Stable algal nuclear expression across environments
subfield: Nonconventional microbial, fungal, and algal chassis
open: Can we sustain predictable multigene expression across industrial algal backgrounds, extended cultivation, and environmental variation? Formally, the goal is a construction approach in which introduced pathways maintain stable, foreseeable expression levels regardless of strain background, cultivation time, and changing environmental conditions.
status: A transgene-selective silencing pathway was identified in 2020 by Neupert et al. (2020), [An epigenetic gene silencing pathway selectively acting on transgenic DNA in the green alga Chlamydomonas](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-19983-4); broad reliable expression remains incomplete.
solved_when: Multigene constructs deployed in algal nuclear genomes retain predictable expression across industrial algal backgrounds, over extended cultivation, and under environmental variation, without reliable expression breaking down.
why: Solving this unlocks robust deployment of engineered metabolic pathways in algal chassis, which is currently blocked by unstable transgene expression.
key_works: Neupert et al. (2020), [An epigenetic gene silencing pathway selectively acting on transgenic DNA in the green alga Chlamydomonas](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-19983-4).

title: Complex chloroplast pathways with predictable flux
subfield: Nonconventional microbial, fungal, and algal chassis
open: Can we engineer a chloroplast to host a complex metabolic pathway whose flux is predictable, by designing enzyme ratios, cofactor usage, and metabolite exchange so that a specified flux is delivered across different host backgrounds and scales?
status: A modular platform and a synthetic photorespiration pathway were demonstrated in 2025 (Inckemann et al. (2025), [A modular high-throughput approach for advancing synthetic biology in the chloroplast of Chlamydomonas](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41477-025-02126-2)); arbitrary-pathway flux prediction remains open.
solved_when: A chloroplast pathway is designed in advance and its flux measured to match a specified target across multiple backgrounds and scales, with arbitrary-pathway flux prediction working rather than requiring empirical re-tuning per construct.
why: It converts demonstrated chloroplast assembly capability into predictable production, making chloroplasts a reliable engineering chassis rather than a trial-and-error host.
key_works: Inckemann et al. (2025), [A modular high-throughput approach for advancing synthetic biology in the chloroplast of Chlamydomonas](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41477-025-02126-2).

title: Programmable archaeal-lipid manufacturing
subfield: Nonconventional microbial, fungal, and algal chassis
open: Can we manufacture archaeal lipids of defined composition and architecture at useful yield, while accurately predicting how the host tolerates production and what properties the recovered material will have? Formally, the goal is a programmable platform linking engineered ether-lipid pathways to host fitness and final membrane-material characteristics.
status: Production of saturated archaeal lipids in engineered E. coli advanced online in 2025 (Jiang et al. (2025, online), [Engineering Escherichia coli for the production of saturated archaeal lipids](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymben.2025.12.004)); control over complex lipid compositions remains open.
solved_when: Defined ether-lipid compositions and architectures are produced at useful yield, with quantitative prediction of both host fitness and recovered-material properties.
why: It provides tunable, stable membrane materials whose properties can be dialed in for a given application.
key_works: Jiang et al. (2025, online), [Engineering Escherichia coli for the production of saturated archaeal lipids](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymben.2025.12.004).

title: Sequence-to-macroscopic-assembly prediction
open: Can we predict the size, shape, mechanical properties, and reversibility of a self-assembled structure directly from its genetically encoded surface interactions, while accounting for cell growth during assembly? More sharply: is there a predictive theory mapping sequence-level design of surface interactions to macroscopic material outcomes in growing engineered living systems?
status: Elastin-like-polypeptide assemblies spanning micrometers to centimeters were demonstrated by Browning et al. (2026) in [De Novo Engineered Living Materials via Elastin-Like Polypeptide-Mediated Self-Assembly](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.6c00073), but a general predictive theory remains open. Related work in active matter addresses self-assembly of growing particles.
solved_when: A theory exists that predicts aggregate size, shape, mechanics, and reversibility from the genetically encoded surface interactions, with growth explicitly accounted for.
why: It would connect genetic design directly to material specifications, allowing engineered living materials to be designed top-down rather than discovered empirically.
key_works: Browning et al. (2026), [De Novo Engineered Living Materials via Elastin-Like Polypeptide-Mediated Self-Assembly](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssynbio.6c00073).

title: Thick living composites with controlled internal alignment
open: Can we grow living composite materials to substantial thickness while imposing a specified three-dimensional alignment of fibers and particles inside them, without starving the embedded cells of nutrients? Formally, the goal is a construction route that achieves prescribed internal architecture and sustained biological activity simultaneously in thick (diffusion-limited) specimens.
status: Flow-aligned cellulose nanocomposites were demonstrated in 2025 (Saadi et al. (2025), [Flow-induced 2D nanomaterials intercalated aligned bacterial cellulose](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60242-1)); general three-dimensional architecture control remains diffusion-limited.
solved_when: A thick living composite is grown with a specified internal fiber/particle alignment while nutrient supply and cellular activity are maintained throughout; general three-dimensional architecture control is demonstrated, not just flow-aligned or other restricted geometries.
why: It enables structurally useful bulk living materials — composites whose mechanical performance relies on controlled anisotropy at full scale rather than only in thin, diffusion-fed sheets.
key_works: Saadi et al. (2025), [Flow-induced 2D nanomaterials intercalated aligned bacterial cellulose](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60242-1).

title: Living-sensor calibration despite biological aging
open: Can a living material's mechanical sensing response remain calibrated while its constituent cells grow, die, and remodel over time — and can the resulting drift be predicted and corrected? Formally, the goal is an engineered living sensor whose input–output calibration is stable or predictably correctable over the organism's life cycle.
status: Programmable microbial force sensors showed rapid recovery in 2026, but long-term biological calibration remains open; see Shi et al. (2026), [A programmable living force sensor fabricated with surface engineered microbial network](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-75944-3). Related work exists on adaptive time-varying sensor calibration in metrology.
solved_when: A living force sensor maintains a calibrated mechanical response over repeated long-term use despite biological aging, with a drift-correction scheme that predicts the calibration change as cells grow and remodel.
why: It makes living sensors reliable over repeated use, turning laboratory demonstrations into dependable measurement devices.
key_works: Shi et al. (2026), [A programmable living force sensor fabricated with surface engineered microbial network](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-75944-3).

title: Tumor recognition that survives antigen heterogeneity
open: Can we design cell therapies whose recognition logic depends on multiple tumor antigens in a way that stays sensitive as tumors evolve and lose individual targets? Formally, the goal is a multi-antigen recognition circuit that retains tumor sensitivity during antigen heterogeneity while staying within a prespecified healthy-tissue false-activation limit.
status: Synthetic antigen AND gates were demonstrated in 2016; longitudinal, patient-general recognition remains a stricter target. Key work: Roybal et al. (2016), [Precision Tumor Recognition by T Cells With Combinatorial Antigen-Sensing Circuits](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2016.01.011).
solved_when: A multi-antigen recognition design is achieved that maintains tumor sensitivity during tumor evolution and meets the prespecified healthy-tissue false-activation limit.
why: It improves therapeutic specificity and makes recognition robust against antigen escape, a major failure mode of current cell therapies.
key_works: Roybal et al. (2016), [Precision Tumor Recognition by T Cells With Combinatorial Antigen-Sensing Circuits](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2016.01.011).

title: Exhaustion control without uncontrolled cell persistence
open: Can engineered immune cells be made to withstand repeated stimulation without becoming exhausted, while still keeping the ability to contract, being terminable on demand, and resisting abnormal proliferation?
status: c-Jun engineering improved exhaustion resistance in 2019 (Lynn et al. (2019), [c-Jun overexpression in CAR T cells induces exhaustion resistance](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1805-z)), but indefinitely safe persistence was not established.
solved_when: A design is demonstrated that preserves cell function under repeated stimulation and simultaneously shows exhaustion resistance, controllable termination, protection against abnormal proliferation, and safe, non-persistent behavior — with indefinite safety of persistence established rather than assumed.
why: It would sustain therapeutic effectiveness over time while keeping the duration of the therapy controllable, which is what currently missing safety evidence blocks.
key_works: Lynn et al. (2019), [c-Jun overexpression in CAR T cells induces exhaustion resistance](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1805-z).

title: Anatomically restricted therapeutic secretion
open: Can engineered therapeutic cells be made to deliver effective payload levels within a chosen organ while quantitatively restricting secretion once those cells exit it?
status: Brain-sensing T cells delivered therapeutic payloads in 2024 mouse studies; human localization–efficacy windows remain open. Key works: Simic et al. (2024), [Programming tissue-sensing T cells that deliver therapies to the brain](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adl4237).
solved_when: A design is demonstrated that achieves therapeutically effective payload secretion in the target organ together with a quantified, bounded secretion level after the engineered cells leave that organ.
why: It concentrates therapeutic action where it is needed and limits exposure elsewhere, turning living cells into organ-targeted delivery agents rather than systemic ones.
key_works: Simic et al. (2024), [Programming tissue-sensing T cells that deliver therapies to the brain](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adl4237).

title: Local immune suppression with preserved protective immunity
open: Can a therapeutic be designed to shut down a specified pathological immune response at a chosen site in the body while leaving protective immunity intact elsewhere, and restore normal local immune function once treatment ends?
status: Synthetic suppressor T cells demonstrated localized immunoprotection in 2024; durable selective human control remains open. Key work: Reddy et al. (2024), [Engineering synthetic suppressor T cells that execute locally targeted immunoprotective programs](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adl4793).
solved_when: A therapy demonstrates localized suppression of a defined pathological response with protective immunity preserved systemically and local immune competence restored after the treatment period.
why: It would make immune regulation spatially restricted, allowing treatment of local inflammation or autoimmune activity without the systemic immunosuppression and infection risk that current approaches carry.
key_works: Reddy et al. (2024), [Engineering synthetic suppressor T cells that execute locally targeted immunoprotective programs](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adl4793).

title: Complete multicomponent circuits delivered in vivo
open: Can we deliver and assemble a complete sensing–computation–response circuit directly inside the intended endogenous cells of a living animal, rather than engineering cells outside the body? Formally, this means achieving in vivo delivery and assembly of all circuit components at controlled ratios, with the off-target distribution of each component measured.
status: In vivo CAR expression was demonstrated in 2022 (Rurik et al. (2022), [CAR T cells produced in vivo to treat cardiac injury](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abm0594)), and targeted integration advanced in humanized mice in 2026 (Nyberg et al. (2026), [Targeted in vivo integration study](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10235-x)), but general multicomponent delivery remains open.
solved_when: A complete multicomponent sensing–computation–response circuit is delivered and assembled in vivo in the intended endogenous cell population, with component ratios controlled and off-target distribution measured.
why: Success would remove the dependence on ex vivo cell manufacturing, making living therapeutics far cheaper and more broadly accessible.
key_works: Rurik et al. (2022), [CAR T cells produced in vivo to treat cardiac injury](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abm0594); Nyberg et al. (2026), [Targeted in vivo integration study](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10235-x).

title: Immune compatibility of programmable receptor parts
open: Can we predict, and then minimize, the immune responses that patients mount against complete synthetic receptors and regulators, including over repeated exposure?
status: SNIPR broadened modular receptor design in 2022 (Zhu et al. (2022), [Modular design of synthetic receptors for programmed gene regulation in cell therapies](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2022.03.023)), but experimental function does not establish population-wide compatibility. Related work exists on immunogenicity prediction for therapeutic proteins.
solved_when: A demonstrated approach predicts and minimizes immune responses to complete synthetic receptor/regulator systems across patients and over repeated exposure.
why: It would support durable, long-term use of synthetic receptor systems in living therapeutics; without it, even experimentally functional receptors may fail in patients.
key_works: Zhu et al. (2022), [Modular design of synthetic receptors for programmed gene regulation in cell therapies](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2022.03.023).

title: Rapid and durable synthetic endocrine feedback
open: Can we build implanted cellular endocrine controllers — such as glucose-responsive designer cells — that act fast enough for physiological feedback yet remain retrievable and hold their calibration for years of meals, exercise, illness, and shifting hormone sensitivity? Formally, the goal is a synthetic closed-loop endocrine device whose response kinetics and long-term set-point stability jointly survive the full扰动 of daily living.
status: Glucose-responsive designer cells were demonstrated in 2016 (Xie et al. (2016), [β-cell-mimetic designer cells provide closed-loop glycemic control](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaf4006)); chronic robustness remains distinct from short-term control and has not been achieved.
solved_when: A retrievable cellular controller is demonstrated that both responds rapidly (on physiological closed-loop timescales, as in short-term glycemic control) and retains its calibration over years, maintaining function across meals, exercise, illness, and changing sensitivity — i.e., chronic robustness is shown, not just short-term control.
why: It unlocks long-lived physiological replacement systems: synthetic endocrine feedback that could substitute for failing native regulation over a patient's lifetime rather than a few days.
key_works: Xie et al. (2016), [β-cell-mimetic designer cells provide closed-loop glycemic control](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaf4006).

title: Chronic electronic interfaces to living gene circuits
open: Can an implanted electronic interface keep issuing calibrated commands to a living gene circuit over months to years, as electrodes age, fibrotic encapsulation develops, and the cells' sensitivity drifts? Formally, the goal is an engineering architecture that maintains stable, quantitatively calibrated control of gene expression despite these chronic degradation processes.
status: DART demonstrated direct-current gene control in 2023; multiyear implant reliability remains open. Key work: Huang et al. (2023), [An electrogenetic interface to program mammalian gene expression by direct current](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-023-00850-7).
solved_when: A demonstrated implantable interface that sustains direct-current control of mammalian gene expression with maintained calibration over multiyear implant lifetimes, compensating for electrode aging, encapsulation, and changing cellular sensitivity.
why: It would make living therapeutics externally adjustable in real time, so dosing can be tuned by clinicians rather than hardwired into the circuit at manufacture.
key_works: Huang et al. (2023), [An electrogenetic interface to program mammalian gene expression by direct current](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42255-023-00850-7).

title: Calibrated RNA-state sensing across patients
open: Can we infer clinically relevant cell states from endogenous RNAs with error rates that are validated and hold across patients? Formally, the goal is sensing that remains calibrated across transcript, isoform, and RNA-editing variation between individuals.
status: CellREADR and related ADAR sensors demonstrated programmable RNA sensing in 2022 (Qian et al. (2022), [Programmable RNA sensing for cell monitoring and manipulation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-05280-1)); cross-patient calibration remains open.
solved_when: A sensor framework infers clinically relevant cell states from endogenous RNAs with validated error rates that remain calibrated across patients, accounting for transcript, isoform, and editing variation.
why: It connects cell atlases to reliable therapeutic targeting, so that RNA-based sensors can be trusted to act on the right cells in different patients.
key_works: Qian et al. (2022), [Programmable RNA sensing for cell monitoring and manipulation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-05280-1).

title: Reliable elimination of every dangerous therapeutic-cell subclone
open: Can we guarantee that every dangerous subclone in a therapeutic cell population is eliminated, including rare ones whose safety switches are weak or silenced, and including cells dispersed across tissue compartments?
status: Inducible caspase eliminated over 90% of modified cells rapidly in a 2011 clinical study (Di Stasi et al. (2011), [Inducible Apoptosis as a Safety Switch for Adoptive Cell Therapy](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1106152)); complete removal and later failure resistance remain stronger targets.
solved_when: A removal method exists with measurable, quantitative guarantees of eliminating all dangerous subclones — surpassing the inducible-caspase benchmark of over 90% rapid elimination from the 2011 clinical study — achieving complete removal and resistance to later failure across tissue compartments.
why: It improves controllability of persistent living therapies, so a therapy cannot escape control through rare switch-resistant cells left behind in any tissue.
key_works: Di Stasi et al. (2011), [Inducible Apoptosis as a Safety Switch for Adoptive Cell Therapy](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1106152).

title: Compiling desired tissue geometry into cell programs
open: Can a specified three-dimensional tissue shape, together with its arrangement of cell types, be translated into a developmental program that dispersed cells execute reliably? Formally, the goal is a construction: given a target geometry and cell-type layout, produce a cell program whose self-organization reliably realizes it.
status: Programmed self-organization was demonstrated in Toda et al. (2018), [Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0271); arbitrary geometry with controlled tolerances remains open.
solved_when: A specified three-dimensional shape and cell-type arrangement is compiled into a reliable developmental program starting from dispersed cells; in particular, arbitrary geometry with controlled tolerances is achieved.
why: It would make tissue form a programmable specification, turning desired geometry into an executable cellular program rather than an empirical outcome.
key_works: Toda et al. (2018), [Programming self-organizing multicellular structures with synthetic cell-cell signaling](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat0271).

title: Predicting mechanics from synthetic adhesion rules
open: Can we predict the mechanical behavior of a tissue — its sorting, tension, viscoelasticity, and failure — from engineered adhesion molecules alone, when active junction remodeling is at play? More formally, is there a sequence-to-mechanics rule that maps synthetic adhesion design to emergent tissue material properties in remodeled epithelia?
status: Synthetic adhesion molecules were used to program multicellular assembly in Stevens et al. (2023), "Programming multicellular assembly with synthetic cell adhesion molecules" (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-05622-z); general sequence-to-mechanics rules remain open.
solved_when: A quantitative framework is given that predicts cell sorting outcomes, tissue tension, viscoelastic response, and failure from the engineered adhesion input, explicitly accounting for active junction remodeling, with validated agreement in synthetic-adhesion experiments.
why: It would close the gap between molecular recognition and tissue-level material properties, letting tissue engineers program mechanics by sequence design rather than trial and error.
key_works: Stevens et al. (2023), [Programming multicellular assembly with synthetic cell adhesion molecules](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-05622-z).

title: Self-assembled hierarchical perfusion networks
open: Can we program a self-assembled vascular network that grows from large vessels down to capillaries, perfusing an entire engineered tissue and adapting its structure to local metabolic demand?
status: Modular arterial organoids achieved rapid perfusion in 2026 (Kong et al. (2026), [Modular assembly of arterial organoids enables rapid blood perfusion to ameliorate ischemic diseases](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-77553-6)); complete hierarchical vascularization of arbitrary engineered organs remains open.
