solved_when: A stable, hierarchical large-vessel-to-capillary network perfuses a complete engineered tissue and demonstrates adaptation to local demand.
why: It enables thicker, functional engineered tissues beyond current diffusion-limited constructs.
key_works: Kong et al. (2026), [Modular assembly of arterial organoids enables rapid blood perfusion to ameliorate ischemic diseases](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-77553-6).

title: Specified innervation of engineered tissues
open: Can we engineer tissues that come with a pre-specified neural wiring diagram, so that designated neurons innervate designated targets and exert selective, stable functional control over them?
status: Functional cortico-motor assembloids were reported in 2020; prescribed wiring and mature long-term control remain open. Key work: Andersen et al. (2020), [Generation of Functional Human 3D Cortico-Motor Assembloids](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2020.11.017).
solved_when: An engineered tissue is produced with neural connections matching a predetermined specification, and selective functional control of the tissue is demonstrated and remains stable over the long term.
why: It enables integrated neuromuscular and organ function in engineered tissues, closing the gap between building tissue and getting the nervous system to operate it.
key_works: Andersen et al. (2020), [Generation of Functional Human 3D Cortico-Motor Assembloids](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2020.11.017).

title: Predictable fertilizer replacement by engineered root symbionts
open: Can engineered root symbionts displace synthetic nitrogen fertilizer at a level agronomists can predict in advance — across soils, climates, crop genotypes, and management regimes? Formally, the goal is to predict fertilizer displacement and yield with independently verified nitrogen budgets.
status: Engineered diazotrophs already show field activity; partial replacement of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer was reported in 2024 (Martinez-Feria et al. (2024), [Genetic remodeling of soil diazotrophs enables partial replacement of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer with biological nitrogen fixation in maize](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41596-024-78243-3)), while site-specific reliability remains open.
solved_when: Fertilizer displacement and yield are predictable across soils, climates, genotypes, and management, with nitrogen budgets independently verified at each site.
why: It would make biological nitrogen provision agronomically dependable, turning a site-specific curiosity into a farm-level input decision.
key_works: Martinez-Feria et al. (2024), [Genetic remodeling of soil diazotrophs enables partial replacement of synthetic nitrogen fertilizer with biological nitrogen fixation in maize](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-024-78243-3).

title: Integrated C4 photosynthesis in rice
open: Can rice be engineered to perform full C4 photosynthesis — combining altered leaf anatomy, cell-type-specific expression, metabolite transport, and the C4 enzymatic cycle — into a single working plant? Success would mean an integrated C4 rice showing a measured yield advantage over conventional C3 rice.
status: This moonshot has been pursued since the 2000s. Regulatory logic for bundle-sheath-specific expression advanced in 2025 with Hua et al. (2025), [A transcription factor ensemble orchestrates bundle sheath expression in rice](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62087-0), but full integration of all required components remains unfinished.
solved_when: A rice line exists in which C4 anatomy, bundle-sheath and mesophyll cell-specific expression, transporters, and C4 enzymes function together, and the plant demonstrates a measured yield advantage attributable to improved carbon assimilation.
why: Functional C4 rice would improve carbon assimilation and resource efficiency in the world's most important staple crop, translating to higher yields from the same inputs.
key_works: Hua et al. (2025), [A transcription factor ensemble orchestrates bundle sheath expression in rice](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62087-0).

title: Photorespiratory bypasses with reproducible food-crop yield gains
open: Can engineered photorespiratory bypasses deliver harvestable-yield gains that reproduce across diverse food crops and environments, and can those gains be cleanly attributed to improved carbon fixation rather than to a repartitioning of biomass?
status: Tobacco field gains were demonstrated in South et al. (2019), [Synthetic glycolate metabolism pathways stimulate crop growth and productivity in the field](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat9077); rice paddy-field gains were reported online in 2025 by Chen et al. (2025/2026), [Rice photorespiratory-bypass field study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cj.2025.03.001), leaving broad reproducibility across crops and environments open.
solved_when: Harvestable-yield increases from a photorespiratory bypass are reproducibly demonstrated across diverse food crops and multiple environments, with the productivity effect separated from biomass repartitioning.
why: It converts a demonstrated pathway-level metabolic improvement into dependable, reproducible gains in actual food production.
key_works: South et al. (2019), [Synthetic glycolate metabolism pathways stimulate crop growth and productivity in the field](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aat9077); Chen et al. (2025/2026), [Rice photorespiratory-bypass field study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cj.2025.03.001).

title: Fast photoprotection without stress vulnerability
open: Can the kinetics of photoprotection recovery be engineered to be faster while a crop still withstands heat, drought, and sustained excess light under realistic field conditions? Formally, the goal is a genotype whose accelerated recovery is reproducibly maintained across combined stresses in field trials.
status: Recovery engineering improved productivity in 2016 and soybean yields in 2022 (De Souza et al. (2022), [Soybean photosynthesis and yield study](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adc9831)); the foundational acceleration work is Kromdijk et al. (2016), [Improving photosynthesis and crop productivity by accelerating recovery from photoprotection](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aai8878). Whether the gain holds consistently under combined stresses remains open.
solved_when: A modified plant shows accelerated photoprotection recovery in reproducible field trials while retaining heat, drought, and sustained-excess-light resilience.
why: Faster recovery captures more fluctuating sunlight for photosynthesis, but only matters if it does not trade away the resilience that protects yield under stress; solving it would couple the productivity gain with stress robustness.
key_works: Kromdijk et al. (2016), [Improving photosynthesis and crop productivity by accelerating recovery from photoprotection](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aai8878); De Souza et al. (2022), [Soybean photosynthesis and yield study](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adc9831).

title: Root programs that adapt to heterogeneous soil
open: Can we engineer root architecture that responds predictably to spatial variation in water and nutrient availability, while preserving useful above-ground growth?
status: Synthetic circuits reprogrammed Arabidopsis roots in 2022 (Brophy et al. (2022), [Synthetic genetic circuits as a means of reprogramming plant roots](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abo4326)); autonomous adaptation in elite crops and soil remains open.
solved_when: A root program is demonstrated that adapts to heterogeneous soil — responding predictably to spatial water and nutrient variation — in elite crops under soil conditions, while maintaining above-ground growth.
why: It would improve resource acquisition under variable field conditions, the core limit on crop performance in heterogeneous environments.
key_works: Brophy et al. (2022), [Synthetic genetic circuits as a means of reprogramming plant roots](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abo4326).

title: Plant memory that remains accurate through development
open: Can a plant be engineered to record environmental events in its intended lineages while maintaining accuracy across an entire crop life cycle? Formally, the goal is a stable memory circuit that stays faithful through development, with quantified false records and losses over the full cycle.
status: Stable plant memory circuits were demonstrated by Lloyd et al. (2022), [Synthetic memory circuits for stable cell reprogramming in plants](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-022-01383-2); developmental fidelity and field-length validation remain open.
solved_when: A plant memory circuit records environmental events in the intended lineages with false records and losses quantified over a complete crop life cycle, not just in a laboratory growth stage.
why: It enables reliable environmental recording and conditional plant development, turning the crop itself into an accurate log of what it experienced.
key_works: Lloyd et al. (2022), [Synthetic memory circuits for stable cell reprogramming in plants](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-022-01383-2).

title: Genotype-independent transformation and regeneration
open: Can we install complex genetic programs into elite crop varieties and regenerate them into fertile, normal plants without having to redevelop the process for each genotype?
status: Morphogenic-regulator approaches continue to broaden genotype access, but are not universal. Ramasamy et al. (2026), [Boosting genome editing in perennial plants by CRISPR-Combo mediated morphogenic gene activation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-76367-w), achieved results across several perennial crops in 2026, though general regeneration remains unsolved.
solved_when: A transformation and regeneration pipeline exists that works across diverse elite crop genotypes, producing fertile plants free of major abnormalities, without genotype-specific redevelopment.
why: Genotype dependence is a central bottleneck in crop engineering; removing it would let engineered traits reach elite varieties directly instead of requiring costly per-cultivar optimization.
key_works: Ramasamy et al. (2026), [Boosting genome editing in perennial plants by CRISPR-Combo mediated morphogenic gene activation](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-76367-w).

title: Portable chloroplast engineering across crop species
open: Can multigene plastid designs be transferred across crop species so that expression levels, inheritance, and pathway function are predictable rather than rediscovered empirically in each host?
status: A 2025 Chlamydomonas platform supplied over 140 regulatory parts (Inckemann et al. (2025), [A modular high-throughput approach for advancing synthetic biology in the chloroplast of Chlamydomonas](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41477-025-02126-2)), but cross-crop transferability remains empirical.
solved_when: A multigene plastid design moved between crop species achieves expression, inheritance, and pathway function that are predictable in advance — quantitatively, performance matching the design specification in the recipient species without host-by-host empirical retuning.
why: It would make organelle design libraries broadly reusable across crops, turning species-specific engineering into a portable design discipline.
key_works: Inckemann et al. (2025), [A modular high-throughput approach for advancing synthetic biology in the chloroplast of Chlamydomonas](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41477-025-02126-2).

title: Orthogonal plant-hormone control in the field
open: Can we engineer plant hormone–receptor pairs that let a grower steer development in chosen tissues, so that an applied chemical in the field produces the intended effect at a predictable dose?
status: An orthogonal auxin–TIR1 pair was demonstrated in 2018 by Uchida et al. (2018), [Chemical hijacking of auxin signaling with an engineered auxin–TIR1 pair](https://doi.org/10.1038/nchembio.2555); delivery, persistence, and agronomic selectivity remain open.
solved_when: An orthogonal hormone–receptor pair achieves spatially selective development with predictable field dose–responses, including solved delivery, persistence, and agronomic selectivity.
why: It would make plant genetic programs externally adjustable after planting — a chemical dial for traits already in the ground — rather than fixed at the seed stage.
key_works: Uchida et al. (2018), [Chemical hijacking of auxin signaling with an engineered auxin–TIR1 pair](https://doi.org/10.1038/nchembio.2555).

title: Therapeutic output that survives gut evolution
open: Can an engineered microbe maintain a specified per-cell therapeutic output throughout prolonged colonization of the human gut, and can we predict how long that engineered function will last before evolution erodes it?
status: The 2025 controlled-colonization study documented genetic-stability challenges, showing that strain persistence does not establish payload persistence (Whitaker et al. (2025), [Controlled colonization of the human gut with a genetically engineered microbial therapeutic](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adu8000)).
solved_when: A colonizing engineered strain is shown to sustain its specified per-cell output over the full colonization period, with a validated prediction of the engineered function's lifetime in vivo.
why: It preserves therapeutic action after engraftment; without stability of the payload, strain persistence alone does not guarantee the therapy still works.
key_works: Whitaker et al. (2025), [Controlled colonization of the human gut with a genetically engineered microbial therapeutic](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adu8000).

title: Quantitative clinical interpretation of living gut diagnostics
open: Can microbial sensor recordings from the gut be converted into calibrated clinical estimates of when inflammation occurred, where it occurred in the gut, and how severe it is? Formally, this asks for a quantitative inversion that accounts for microbial abundance and intestinal transit when mapping recorded signals to disease parameters.
status: Long-term inflammatory sensing in the mammalian gut was demonstrated in mice in 2017 by Riglar et al. (2017), [Engineered bacteria can function in the mammalian gut long-term as live diagnostics of inflammation](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3879); clinical sensitivity and specificity remain unmet requirements.
solved_when: Engineered-gut diagnostic recordings can be inverted to yield calibrated estimates of disease timing, location, and severity, with clinically validated sensitivity and specificity in humans.
why: It converts raw biological recordings from living diagnostics into interpretable, quantitative diagnostic readouts a clinician can act on.
key_works: Riglar et al. (2017), [Engineered bacteria can function in the mammalian gut long-term as live diagnostics of inflammation](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3879).

title: Causal spatial models of engineered microbiomes
open: Can we predict how the metabolic outputs and host-exposure profile of a microbiome change when specific members are relocated or locally modified in space? The goal is a causal, spatially resolved model whose predictions are validated by spatial interventions in the community.
status: MaPS-seq mapped microbial spatial associations in 2019 (Sheth et al. (2019), [Spatial metagenomic characterization of microbial biogeography in the gut](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-019-0183-2)), but causal spatial design remains harder than measuring co-location; related foundations exist in spatial causal inference in statistics and reaction–diffusion ecology.
solved_when: A model correctly predicts metabolic and host-exposure changes resulting from spatial interventions (relocation or local modification of community members), with those predictions validated experimentally.
why: It would enable engineering of microbiomes beyond bulk community composition, giving control over function through spatial arrangement rather than only overall makeup.
key_works: Sheth et al. (2019), [Spatial metagenomic characterization of microbial biogeography in the gut](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-019-0183-2).

title: Community evolution that optimizes a durable collective function
open: When does selection applied at the community level produce a persistent improvement in a collective function, rather than merely transient shifts in composition or the enrichment of members that do not contribute? A predictive account should specify the conditions under which community-level heritability suffices for directed evolution of a durable ecosystem-level trait.
status: Directed-community-evolution frameworks advanced in 2021, notably Chang et al. (2021), [Engineering complex communities by directed evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-021-01457-5), but general experimentally validated heritability rules remain open.
solved_when: A general, experimentally validated rule for community-level heritability exists that predicts, for a given selection scheme, whether functional improvement will persist across generations instead of decaying or being eroded by noncontributor enrichment.
why: Such a rule would make it possible to evolve useful ecosystem-level traits on demand, turning community selection from an empirical gamble into an engineering method.
key_works: Chang et al. (2021), [Engineering complex communities by directed evolution](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-021-01457-5).

title: Surrogate endpoints that predict microbial-therapy benefit
open: When do strain-level biomarkers or metabolite conversion measurements genuinely predict that a microbial therapy will deliver patient-important benefit, rather than merely tracking exposure? A formal answer would specify the conditions under which such markers are valid causal surrogates for clinical outcomes across doses and populations.
status: The leading test case is the phenylketonuria live bacterial therapeutic platform, which progressed from 2018 development work (Isabella et al. (2018), [Development of a synthetic live bacterial therapeutic for the human metabolic disease phenylketonuria](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4222)) to a 2023 phase 2 report; however, the general question of surrogate validity remains unaddressed as a separate matter.
solved_when: A validated causal surrogate-validation framework shows that strain biomarkers or metabolite conversion causally predict patient-important outcomes across doses and populations, with the validation demonstrated on real microbial-therapy trial data.
why: It would let trials for engineered microbiome therapies be interpreted through measurable biomarkers rather than hard clinical endpoints, speeding therapeutic development and dose selection.
key_works: Isabella et al. (2018), [Development of a synthetic live bacterial therapeutic for the human metabolic disease phenylketonuria](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.4222).

title: Plant-protective communities that generalize across soils
open: Can we design a defined microbial community that reproducibly improves crop stress phenotypes even when deployed across diverse resident microbiomes and soil types? In other words, when does an engineered community's protective effect generalize beyond the soil in which it was built?
status: Desert-rhizosphere communities improved tomato salt resilience in 2022; environmental transfer remains open. Key work: Schmitz et al. (2022), [Synthetic bacterial community derived from a desert rhizosphere confers salt stress resilience to tomato in the presence of a soil microbiome](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41396-022-01238-3).
solved_when: A defined community is shown to improve crop stress phenotypes reproducibly across distinct resident microbiomes and soil types, with environmental transfer demonstrated.
why: It would make microbial crop protection dependable in the field, rather than effective only under the conditions where the community was originally assembled.
key_works: Schmitz et al. (2022), [Synthetic bacterial community derived from a desert rhizosphere confers salt stress resilience to tomato in the presence of a soil microbiome](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41396-022-01238-3).

title: Complete remediation of changing pollutant mixtures
open: Can a contained engineered microbiome keep treating pollutant mixtures whose composition changes over time, while also identifying the major transformation products and closing contaminant mass balances? Formally, the goal is a construction that sustains mixture-general degradation performance with by-product assurance.
status: Engineered degradation of multiple pollutants was demonstrated in 2025 by Su et al. (2025), [Bioremediation of complex organic pollutants by engineered Vibrio natriegens](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08947-7); mixture-general performance and by-product assurance remain open. A related concern from environmental chemistry is the characterization of unknown transformation products.
solved_when: A contained treatment system demonstrates degradation of variable pollutant mixtures, identifies the major transformation products, and closes contaminant mass balances — with contaminant disappearance shown to correspond to reduced hazard.
why: Without by-product assurance, apparent contaminant disappearance could leave unknown transformation products of uncertain hazard; a solution establishes that remediation genuinely reduces risk.
key_works: Su et al. (2025), [Bioremediation of complex organic pollutants by engineered Vibrio natriegens](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08947-7).

title: Field-calibrated living environmental sensors
open: Can living microbial sensors be engineered to report analyte concentrations accurately in the field over long periods, when temperature, hydration, ambient chemistry, and the age of the sensor cells themselves all drift? Formally, the goal is a construction achieving field-calibrated, long-duration analyte inference that remains reliable despite these environmental and cellular-aging variations.
status: Remote bacterial sensing was demonstrated in 2017, but operational calibration and maintenance remain open. Key work: Belkin et al. (2017), [Remote detection of buried landmines using a bacterial sensor](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3791).
solved_when: A living sensor system is built whose analyte-level readouts stay calibrated in the field across seasonal temperature, hydration, and chemistry changes and cellular aging, with operational maintenance requirements specified and met over long deployment durations.
why: It would make long-duration environmental monitoring dependable enough to trust in real deployments, rather than only in controlled demonstrations.
key_works: Belkin et al. (2017), [Remote detection of buried landmines using a bacterial sensor](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3791).

title: Climate-resilient symbioses without hidden fitness costs
open: When does an engineered or evolved symbiont that tolerates climate stress actually benefit its host across the full life cycle, without imposing hidden reproductive or ecological costs? Formally, can we predict the conditions under which increased symbiont stress tolerance translates into net host fitness gains rather than trade-offs?
status: Heat-evolved algae experimentally improved coral bleaching tolerance in 2020 (Buerger et al. (2020), [Heat-evolved microalgal symbionts increase coral bleaching tolerance](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aba2498)); whether the benefit persists lifelong and transfers ecologically remains open.
solved_when: A predictive account (validated experimentally) identifies when improved symbiont stress tolerance yields lifelong host benefit without unacceptable reproductive or ecological costs, including whether such tolerance can transfer ecologically.
why: It would ground conservation interventions like assisted evolution in evidence, replacing trial-and-error deployment of engineered symbioses with predictable outcomes.
key_works: Buerger et al. (2020), [Heat-evolved microalgal symbionts increase coral bleaching tolerance](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aba2498).

title: Integrated biological life support with closed material budgets
open: Can biology be engineered to sustain human life in remote environments as a single integrated system — producing food, oxygen, and materials while recycling waste with closed material budgets? Formally, can production, waste recycling, and resource recovery be integrated with quantified external inputs, demonstrated failure recovery, and measurable mission-level advantages over conventional resupply?
status: A 2020 Mars-biotechnology roadmap — Nangle et al. (2020), [The case for biotech on Mars](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0485-4) — articulated the opportunity, but existing work consists of isolated demonstrations that do not establish integrated mission-scale performance.
solved_when: An integrated biological life-support system is demonstrated whose material budgets are closed at a quantified level, whose external inputs are quantified, whose recovery from defined failures is demonstrated, and whose mission-level advantages over alternatives are quantified — at mission scale rather than in isolated demonstrations.
why: It would sharply reduce dependence on resupply for remote environments such as long-duration space missions, where every launched kilogram carries large cost and risk.
key_works: Nangle et al. (2020), [The case for biotech on Mars](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41587-020-0485-4).

title: Predictive lifetime bounds for biological containment
open: Can we predict the probability that an engineered organism escapes its designed containment over a specified population size, number of generations, and environmental range, with validated confidence intervals? In formal terms, this asks for predictive lifetime bounds on containment failure that hold quantitatively across populations, generations, and environments.
status: Strong laboratory synthetic dependencies were demonstrated in 2015; general lifetime prediction remains unresolved. Key works: Mandell et al. (2015), [Biocontainment of genetically modified organisms by synthetic protein design](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14121).
solved_when: A predictive model exists that yields containment-failure probabilities with validated confidence intervals over specified populations, generations, and environments.
why: It would convert isolated laboratory escape assays into interpretable reliability evidence that can be acted on for biosafety and governance decisions.
key_works: Mandell et al. (2015), [Biocontainment of genetically modified organisms by synthetic protein design](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature14121).

title: Containment of engineered DNA after cell death
open: How long does engineered DNA persist in the environment after its host cells die, and how much of it can still transfer functionally to other organisms — and can we build mechanisms that limit both?
status: Targeted DNA destruction was demonstrated in 2015 by Caliando and Voigt (2015), [Targeted DNA degradation using a CRISPR device stably carried in the host genome](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms7989); environmental fate and transfer assurance, however, still require broader evidence.
solved_when: A quantitative characterization of genetic-material persistence and functional transfer after engineered cell death exists, together with a demonstrated method that limits both, supported by broader environmental evidence than current demonstrations provide.
why: It addresses the fate of genetic material independently of cell viability, so containment assurances cannot be undone by dead cells leaking functional DNA into the environment.
key_works: Caliando and Voigt (2015), [Targeted DNA degradation using a CRISPR device stably carried in the host genome](https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms7989).

title: Containment assays that capture dormancy and resuscitation
open: Can we develop standardized containment assays that reliably distinguish microbial death from temporary nonculturability, and quantify the extent of later resuscitation across different physiological states?
status: Modern kill-switch systems provide test cases, but shared assurance covering latent survival remains an infrastructure gap. Key work: Rottinghaus et al. (2022), [Genetically stable CRISPR-based kill switches for engineered microbes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-28163-5).
solved_when: A validated, standardized assay exists that distinguishes death from dormant viable-but-nonculturable states and quantitatively measures subsequent resuscitation across physiological states.
why: It prevents false confidence from culture-negative measurements, which currently can miss latent surviving engineered cells that later resuscitate.
key_works: Rottinghaus et al. (2022), [Genetically stable CRISPR-based kill switches for engineered microbes](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-022-28163-5).

title: Independent, privacy-preserving synthesis-screening assurance
open: Can the sensitivity, specificity, privacy protections, and update reliability of DNA synthesis screening be evaluated by an independent party without exposing sensitive sequences or customer designs? In formal terms: is there a protocol or dataset that yields verifiable, system-wide performance metrics while preserving confidentiality of both hazardous-sequence data and proprietary customer information?
status: SecureDNA reported operational screening at substantial scale in 2026 (Baum et al. (2026), [A system capable of verifiably and privately screening global DNA synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1093/nsr/nwag103)); independent system-wide assurance and adoption remain separate challenges.
solved_when: An independent evaluation exists that measures screening sensitivity, specificity, privacy, and update reliability across the system without disclosing sensitive sequences or customer designs.
why: It would support trustworthy screening across providers, giving regulators, customers, and the public grounds to trust that screening systems perform as claimed without leaking the very information they must protect.
key_works: Baum et al. (2026), [A system capable of verifiably and privately screening global DNA synthesis](https://doi.org/10.1093/nsr/nwag103).

title: Bounding mirror-life risks without creating mirror organisms
open: Can we quantify how ecologically disruptive or immunologically dangerous mirror organisms would be — using only nonliving components, existing observations, and independently scrutinized models — without ever constructing a mirror organism? Formally, the goal is to derive evidence-based bounds on ecological and immune risks of mirror life that require no experiments on living mirror systems.
status: A 2024 assessment identified potentially severe risks and advocated against creating mirror bacteria; evidence-based risk bounds remain open. Key work: Adamala et al. (2024), [Confronting risks of mirror life](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.ads9158).
solved_when: Quantitative, evidence-based risk bounds for mirror-life ecological and immune harms are established using nonliving components, existing observations, and independently scrutinized models, with no construction of a mirror organism.
why: Such bounds would directly inform what research restrictions and oversight are warranted, replacing conjecture with evidence while never constructing the hazardous system itself.
key_works: Adamala et al. (2024), [Confronting risks of mirror life](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.ads9158).

title: Durable global access to verified biological materials
open: How can the global research community sustain affordable, durable access to authenticated biological materials — strains, plasmids, and standards — including their preservation, documentation, replacement, and delivery? Formally, the goal is a functioning long-term system (financial and logistical) that keeps verified materials available to researchers worldwide at reasonable cost.
status: Addgene reported expanded international distribution in 2026 (Addgene, [Strengthening Foundations: Reflections on 2025 and What’s Ahead for 2026](https://blog.addgene.org/strengthening-foundations-reflections-on-2025-and-whats-ahead-for-2026)); access inequalities and long-term repository financing remain open.
solved_when: A durable mechanism exists that provides affordable access to authenticated strains, plasmids, and standards worldwide, covering preservation, documentation, replacement, and delivery, with long-term repository financing secured and access inequalities substantially reduced.
why: It makes reproducible research possible beyond well-resourced centers; without it, scientific results remain unverifiable by much of the world.
key_works: Addgene (2026), [Strengthening Foundations: Reflections on 2025 and What’s Ahead for 2026](https://blog.addgene.org/strengthening-foundations-reflections-on-2025-and-whats-ahead-for-2026).

title: Funded capacity for locally chosen synthetic-biology priorities
open: Can durable funding and technical support be established that lets under-resourced communities choose, evaluate, and maintain their own synthetic-biology applications? In formal terms, the goal is a sustained capacity-building arrangement that transfers operational capability and local decision-making power rather than externally dictated projects.
status: CBD Decision 16/21 initiated capacity-building work in 2024; its 2025–2026 program ties activities to resource availability. Reference: Convention on Biological Diversity (2024), [Decision 16/21: Synthetic biology](https://www.cbd.int/doc/decisions/cop-16/cop-16-dec-21-en.pdf).
solved_when: Under-resourced communities have stable funding and technical support sufficient to select, evaluate, and maintain their own synthetic-biology applications on an ongoing basis.
why: A solution transfers operational capability and local decision-making power to the communities themselves.
key_works: Convention on Biological Diversity (2024), [Decision 16/21: Synthetic biology](https://www.cbd.int/doc/decisions/cop-16/cop-16-dec-21-en.pdf).

title: Comparable evidence for environmental decisions
open: Can we build evidence packages for environmental decisions about synthetic biology that are interoperable across jurisdictions — covering function, persistence, reversibility, ecological effects, and uncertainty — without losing local relevance? In formal terms, the goal is a standardized but adaptable evidence framework that supports comparison and scrutiny across decision contexts.
status: The CBD's 2024 decision provides an institutional starting point, but universally validated experimental criteria remain absent. Convention on Biological Diversity (2024), [Decision 16/21: Synthetic biology](https://www.cbd.int/doc/decisions/cop-16/cop-16-dec-21-en.pdf).
solved_when: A widely usable framework of interoperable evidence packages exists that addresses function, persistence, reversibility, ecological effects, and uncertainty while retaining local relevance.
why: It improves comparability and scrutiny of environmental decisions, making evidence from different settings assessable against common criteria.
key_works: Convention on Biological Diversity (2024), [Decision 16/21: Synthetic biology](https://www.cbd.int/doc/decisions/cop-16/cop-16-dec-21-en.pdf).
